en: I praise Agni, the domestic priest, the god who is the officiant of the sacrifice, the invoker,
the bestower of the most excellent treasures.
Agni is worthy of praise by the ancient seers and by those of the present;
may he bring the gods here to us.
Through Agni, may one obtain wealth and nourishment day by day— wealth that is glorious and most rich in heroic sons.
O Agni, whatever sacrifice or ritual you encompass on every side,
that alone reaches the gods.
Agni, the invoker, possessed of the insight of a seer, true and of most wondrous fame—
may the god come hither with the gods.
Whatever good you shall do for the donor, O Agni,
that is indeed true of you, O Aṅgiras.
O Agni, illuminator of the darkness, day by day we approach you with our prayer,
bringing homage.
Him who rules over the sacrifices, the radiant guardian of the cosmic order,
increasing within his own abode.
O Agni, be easy of access to us, as a father is to his son;
attend to us for our well-being.
O Vāyu, come hither, O beautiful one; these Soma juices have been prepared.
Drink of them and hear our call.
O Vāyu, the singers praise you with hymns; the pressers of Soma, who know the days, sing toward you.
O Vāyu, your mingling speech goes forth to the donor,
far-reaching for the drinking of Soma.
O Indra and Vāyu, these pressed juices are here; come hither with refreshments, for the drops long for you both.
O Vāyu and Indra, you two who possess wealth in horses, take notice of the pressed juices;
come hither quickly!
O Vāyu and Indra, come to the prepared place of the one who presses the soma;
quickly, O heroes, through this very prayer.
I invoke Mitra of purified will and Varuṇa, the destroyer of enemies, as they perfect the prayer that drips with clarity.
By means of *ṛta*, O Mitra and Varuṇa, you who increase *ṛta* and touch *ṛta*, you have attained great mental power.
O Mitra and Varuṇa, our seers, of many births and wide dwellings, you two bestow skillful and active wisdom.
O Aśvins, lords of splendor with swift hands, you who enjoy much, take pleasure in these sacrificial offerings.
O Aśvins, performers of many wonders, O heroes, with powerful insight, you who are worthy of praise,
accept our songs.
O wonder-workers, O Nāsatyas, these pressed juices are for you;
the sacred grass is strewn—come hither, O you whose path is red with flame!
O Indra, come, O you of wondrous luster; these pressed juices long for you, purified through the fine fingers and the body of the filter.
O Indra, come, impelled by our prayer and urged on by the sages, to the invocations of the worshipper who has pressed the soma.
O Indra, Lord of the Bay Horses, come swiftly toward our sacred prayers;
take pleasure in our pressed soma.
O protectors, supporters of the people, all you gods, come hither;
you who give, come to the pressed juice of the giver.
O All-Gods, you who cross the waters, come quickly to the pressed juice,
as cows go to their stalls.
May all the gods— free from failure, possessing the power of illusion, and devoid of malice— the bearers of the sacrifice, take pleasure in this oblation.
May Sarasvatī, the purifier, rich in spoils through her strengths, who possesses wealth through her wisdom, desire our sacrifice.
Impelling true words of joy and awakening gracious thoughts,
Sarasvatī has established the sacrifice.
The great ocean, Sarasvatī, makes herself known by her signal;
she illumines all inspired thoughts.
Day after day, we invoke for our protection the maker of beautiful forms, like a well-milking cow for the milker.
Come to our libations; O drinker of Soma, drink of the Soma!
O giver of cattle, the exhilaration of the wealthy one is indeed yours.
Then may we find from you your most intimate favors;
do not overlook us, but come to us.
Go forth and ask the wise Indra, the invincible,
who is more excellent for you than [all] your friends.
And let our revilers say, "Let them turn away from elsewhere," while they offer worship only to Indra.
And may the people, O Wondrous One, call us fortunate;
may we abide in the protection of Indra.
Bring this swift one for the swift one, who is the glory of the sacrifice and the delight of men;
flying, he gladdens his friend.
Having drunk of this, O Śatakratu, you became the slayer of the Vṛtras; you have protected the victor in the contests for booty.
O Śatakratu, we strengthen you, the prize-winner, for the sake of prizes;
O Indra, for the winning of riches.
To him who is a great source of wealth, easy to cross over, and a friend to the one who presses the soma—
sing to that Indra.
Come hither and sit down; sing forth to Indra, O friends who bring hymns of praise!
To Indra, the most frequent among the many, the lord of desirable things, when the Soma is pressed.
May he indeed be with us in our endeavor; may he be with us for wealth and for inspired wisdom.
May he come to us with spoils of victory.
Sing for that Indra, at whose conclusion of battle his two bay steeds the enemies cannot withstand in combats.
To the drinker of the pressed juice, these pure pressed drops go for his enjoyment— Soma juices mixed with curds.
O Indra, you of noble will, having grown great at once for the drinking of the pressed juice, you were born for preeminence.
O Indra, lover of songs, let the swift Soma juices enter you; may they be a source of well-being for you, the wise one.
The hymns have magnified you; the recitations have magnified you, O Lord of a hundred powers;
may our songs magnify you.
May Indra, whose protection is imperishable, win this thousandfold booty,
in which all manly powers reside.
O Indra, lover of songs, let not mortals do harm to our bodies;
as the sovereign lord, ward off the weapon of death.
Those who stand around harness the ruddy, bright one as he moves; the luminous realms shine in heaven.
They yoke his two beloved bay horses to the chariot on its two sides—
red, bold, and carrying the hero.
Making a signal for the signalless, O men, and a form for the formless,
you were born together with the dawns.
Then indeed, according to their own nature, they have again assumed the state of embryos,
assuming names worthy of sacrifice.
O Indra, with those who shatter even what is firm and with those who carry you as priests,
you found the ruddy cows even within the cave.
Seeking the gods, they have raised their voices toward the one who finds wealth, according to their thought; they have praised the great, the renowned one.
For you shall be seen united with Indra, having come together with him who is fearless— both of you joyful and equal in splendor.
With blameless, radiant throngs that are dear to Indra, the sacrifice shines with power.
From there, O wanderer, come hither, or from the luminous realm of heaven;
our songs of praise strive together toward him.
We seek bounty from here, or from heaven, or from the earth; we seek Indra from the great mid-region.
To Indra alone have the singers sung aloud; to Indra with hymns have the chanters chanted;
to Indra have the voices cried out.
Indra indeed is joined with the two bay steeds, mingled with them, yoked by a word; Indra is the wielder of the thunderbolt, golden-hued.
Indra raised the sun high in heaven for far-reaching vision;
he split the mountain asunder with his rays.
O Indra, protect us in the contests for booty and in battles where thousands are won, you,
the fierce one, with your fierce aids.
We invoke Indra in the great contest, Indra in the small; we call upon the wielder of the thunderbolt as our ally against the Vṛtras.
O Bull, O ever-conquering one, open up for us that vessel of oblation;
be irresistible for us.
In every pressing, at every higher [rite], the hymns of Indra, the wielder of the thunderbolt, increase;
I find no adequate praise for him.
Like a bull among the herds, he drives the people forward with his might—
the sovereign, the unopposed.
He who alone rules over the people, over riches,
and over the five tribes— Indra.
We invoke Indra for you from all sides, away from other people;
may he be ours alone.
O Indra, bring us for our protection wealth that is most excellent, victorious, ever-conquering, and capable of winning.
By which we may, with your aid, strike down the Vṛtras with our fists and overcome them with our horses.
O Indra, protected by you, may we take up the thunderbolt as a weapon;
may we completely conquer our rivals in battle.
O Indra, with you as our ally, may we, together with heroic archers, overcome those who attack us.
Great is Indra, and let his greatness extend even further to the wielder of the thunderbolt; in breadth, his power is like the sky.
Or those men who have sought refuge in you during the confusion for the winning of offspring—
whether they be inspired poets yearning with their prayers.
His belly, which drinks most Soma, swells like the ocean;
it is like the waters from the vast throat of the cloud.
For thus indeed is his gracious bounty— abundant, rich in cattle, and great—
like a branch laden with ripe fruit for the donor.
For thus indeed are thy powers and thy aids, O Indra, for one such as I;
they are ready at once for the donor.
For thus indeed are his desirable [hymns]: the *stoma* and the *uktha* are to be recited for Indra, for the drinking of the soma.
Come, O Indra, and exhilarate yourself with the soma-juice through all the Soma-offerings;
you are great, a helper by your might.
Release him upon the pressed juice— for Indra who delights in delight— the exhilarating one,
for the doer of all deeds.
O you with the beautiful jaws, lord of all people, rejoice in these exhilarating hymns of praise at these libations.
O Indra, songs have been released for you; they have risen up toward you—the unsatisfied one, toward the bull, the lord.
O Indra, impel toward us a wondrous and choice gift; let it be abundant and sufficient for you.
O Indra, impel us well in that regard toward wealth— us who are zealous,
O you of many glories, and full of renown.
O Indra, bestow upon us wide and lofty fame, rich in cattle and in booty;
grant us all-encompassing, imperishable life.
Bestow upon us great renown and splendor that wins a thousandfold;
O Indra, grant us those nourishments borne on chariots.
Praising with songs Indra, the lord of wealth, the one worthy of praise,
who comes for our protection— him we invoke.
At every pressing, for him who is his own home, the noble one sings forth a great song of strength for the mighty Indra.
The singers of the *gāyatrī* chant thee; the reciters of hymns praise thy song.
O Lord of a hundred powers, the priests have raised thee up like a pole.
When he climbed from ridge to ridge and beheld much that was yet to be done, Indra perceived his purpose; the bull moves forth with his herd.
Yoke, O Indra, your two long-maned, bay horses, the vigorous ones that fill out the girths;
then, O Soma-drinker, come to listen to our songs.
Come hither, respond to our hymns, sing aloud, and roar!
O Vasu, O Indra, favor our prayer and increase our sacrifice.
A hymn worthy of praise has been recited for Indra, a source of strength for him who bestows many gifts,
so that Śakra may take delight in our pressed juices and in our friendship.
Him indeed we seek for friendship, him for wealth, him for heroic power;
may that Śakra Indra be able to help us, bestowing riches.
O Indra, well-opened and free from dust is the glory bestowed by you;
open the stall of the cows and bestow bounty, O wielder of the stone.
For neither of the two worlds, heaven and earth, can restrain you when you are acting with fierce wrath;
conquer the waters rich in light, and pour down the cattle upon us.
O you whose ears are quick to hear, listen to my call; now indeed take up my songs.
O Indra, place this hymn of mine even closer than your own companions.
For we know you as the most virile one, who hears our invocation in the contests for booty;
we invoke the aid of the most virile one, that which bestows a thousandfold gain.
O Indra, son of Kuśika, rejoicing, drink our pressed soma! Prolong our new span of life; make us a seer who wins a thousandfold.
O lover of songs, may these hymns encompass you from every side; may these increasing praises follow after you, the long-lived one, and may they be dear to you as you are dear to them.
All songs have magnified Indra, who is as expansive as the ocean—
the best of charioteers among charioteers, the lord and true master of spoils.
In your friendship, O Indra, we who possess strength—O Lord of Might—let us not fear.
We cry out toward you, the conqueror who is never defeated.
The many gifts of Indra do not fail;
his aids do not cease, when he bestows wealth consisting of cattle as bounty upon his praisers.
The breaker of forts, the youth, the sage of immeasurable power was born—
Indra, the sustainer of every deed, the wielder of the thunderbolt, praised by many.
O Lord of the Stones, you opened the cave of Vala who possessed the cattle;
the gods, being pressed forward, sought you out while remaining fearless.
O Hero, through your gifts I have come back, calling out to the river; O lover of songs, the poets who know you have stood near you.
O Indra, with your wondrous powers you overthrew the guileful Śuṣṇa;
the wise know this deed of yours—exalt their renown.
The hymns have sung aloud to Indra, the ruler by his might,
he whose gifts are a thousand or even more numerous.
We choose Agni as our messenger, the invoker, the possessor of all wealth, the one of skillful intellect for this sacrifice.
With invocations, they ever call upon Agni, Agni, the lord of the people,
the bearer of oblations, the one beloved by many.
O Agni, being born, bring the gods here for the one who has strewn the sacrificial grass;
you are our invoker, worthy of praise.
Awaken those who desire it, O Agni, when you go on your mission as a messenger;
sit together with the gods upon the sacred grass.
O Agni, invoked with clarified butter, shining one, burn against those who cause harm, you who possess the power to destroy the sorcerers.
By Agni is Agni kindled— the sage, the master of the house, the youth, the bearer of oblations, whose mouth is the sacrificial ladle.
Praise Agni the seer, whose laws are true at the sacrifice,
the god who drives away disease.
O Agni, for that lord of oblations who worships you as his divine messenger,
be his protector.
O Purifier, be gracious to him who, possessing oblations, seeks to win over Agni for the feast of the gods.
O purifying, radiant Agni, bring the gods here to us—
to our sacrifice and our oblation.
Being thus praised with this newest song, bring us wealth and food accompanied by heroic sons.
O Agni, with your bright flame and with all invocations of the gods,
graciously accept this hymn of praise from us.
Well-kindled, O Agni, bring the gods hither for the one who offers the oblation; O Purifier, as the Hotṛ priest, perform the sacrifice.
O Sage Tanūnapāt, today make our honey-sweet sacrifice among the gods for their enjoyment.
I invoke here at this sacrifice the beloved Narāśaṃsa,
the honey-tongued one, who has prepared the oblation.
O Agni, being invoked, bring the gods hither on your most comfortable chariot;
you are the Hotṛ-priest appointed by Manu.
O wise ones, spread the sacrificial grass in due order, its back anointed with ghee,
where the manifestation of immortality is seen.
May the divine doors, increasers of cosmic order, unceasing, open wide today and now for the sacrifice.
I invoke Night and Dawn, the beautifully adorned, at this sacrifice;
may they sit upon this sacred grass of ours.
I invoke those two divine Hotṛ-priests, the sages with beautiful tongues;
may they perform this sacrifice of ours.
May Iḷā, Sarasvatī, and Mahī— the three goddesses who bring delight—
sit upon the sacrificial grass, they who are unfailing.
I invoke here Tvaṣṭṛ, the foremost, who possesses all forms;
may he be ours alone.
O divine Lord of the Forest, release the oblation for the gods;
may the consciousness of the giver be directed forward.
With *svāhā*, perform the sacrifice for Indra in the house of the sacrificer;
there I invoke the gods.
O Agni, with all these gods, come to our service and our songs for the drinking of Soma, and perform the sacrifice.
The Kaṇvas have called upon you; they, O inspired one, sing your praises with their hymns. O Agni, come hither with the gods!
Indra and Vāyu, Bṛhaspati, Mitra and Agni, Pūṣan, Bhaga, the Ādityas, and the host of Maruts.
Your exhilarating, intoxicating drops are being brought forward—
the drops of honey resting in the vessels.
Seeking your aid, the Kaṇvas, having spread the sacrificial grass, rich in oblations and having prepared everything, invoke you.
O Agni, may those steeds who carry you— whose backs are sprinkled with ghee, who are yoked by thought—
bring the gods here for the drinking of Soma.
O Agni, make those worshipful ones, who increase the cosmic order, accompanied by their wives;
O fair-tongued one, cause them to drink of the honeyed draught.
O Agni, let those who are worthy of sacrifice and those who are to be praised drink of this honeyed [oblation] with your tongue at the utterance of *vaṣaṭ*.
From the very realm of light of the sun, may the inspired priest, as the invoker here, bring hither all the gods who awaken at dawn.
O Agni, drink the Soma mead with all [the gods], with Indra, and with Vāyu; drink it according to the abodes of Mitra.
O Agni, you sit as the Hotṛ priest, established by Manu, at the sacrifices;
therefore, perform this sacrifice of ours.
Yoke, O God, the ruddy mares to your chariot—the bay and the red ones;
with them, bring the gods here.
O Indra, drink the Soma according to the season; let the drops enter you—intoxicating ones that dwell in that very place.
O Maruts, drink according to the season from the Potar’s cup; purify the sacrifice, for you are indeed the bounteous givers.
O Gṇās, favor our sacrifice; O Neṣṭar, drink according to the season, for you are the bestower of treasures.
O Agni, bring the gods here; seat them in the three wombs;
attend to them and drink according to the season.
O Indra, drink the Soma from the Brahmin’s gift according to the seasons;
for your friendship is invincible.
O Mitra and Varuṇa, you who uphold the sacred law, you have attained through the cosmic order a skill that is difficult to overcome at the sacrifice.
The givers of wealth, with pressing-stones in hand at the sacrifice,
invoke the god for wealth during the rites.
May Draviṇodas grant us those riches which are renowned;
may we win them among the gods.
The giver of wealth desires to drink; offer the oblation and step forward;
proceed from the office of the Neṣṭṛ according to the seasons.
When we worship you, the giver of wealth, with the four seasonal offerings,
then indeed become our bestower.
O Aśvins, drink the honeyed draught, you whose fire is radiant and whose vows are pure,
who, according to the season, carry the sacrifice.
O truthful one, through the domestic fire and according to the season, you are the leader of the sacrifice;
worship the gods for the sake of the seeker of the gods.
Let the bay steeds bring you hither, the bull, for the drinking of the Soma;
O Indra, let those with sun-like eyes bring you.
May these roasted grains dripping with ghee bring the two bay steeds here; may they carry Indra upon his most comfortable chariot.
We invoke Indra in the morning; we invoke Indra as the sacrifice proceeds;
we invoke Indra for the drinking of the Soma.
Come to our pressed juice, O Indra, with your long-maned bay horses;
for we invoke you when the juice is pressed.
Come to this our hymn of praise; come to this pressed libation.
Drink like a thirsty buffalo.
These Soma drops, the pressed juices, are upon the sacred grass;
O Indra, drink them for the sake of strength.
May this foremost hymn of praise reach your heart, most soothing;
then drink the pressed Soma.
Indra, the slayer of Vṛtra, goes to every pressed libation for exhilaration, to drink the Soma.
Fulfill this desire of ours with cattle and horses, O Śatakratu;
we, with attentive minds, shall praise you.
I choose for myself the protection of Indra and Varuṇa, the two sovereign kings;
may they both be gracious to us in such a state.
For you two are indeed the ones who come for the protection of the invocation of a sage such as I; you are the sustainers of the peoples.
O Indra and Varuṇa, satisfy us with wealth according to our desire;
as such, we seek you most closely.
For may we be among those who receive your powers, may we be among those who receive your favors— yea,
among those who receive your gifts of booty.
Indra is the most eminent among those who give by the thousands, and Varuṇa is the most praiseworthy; he becomes the one worthy of hymns as the inspired power.
Through the protection of these two, may we win and store up [wealth];
and may there be a surplus for distribution.
O Indra and Varuṇa, I invoke you both for wondrous bounty;
make us truly victorious.
O Indra and Varuṇa, now indeed, while our prayers desire to win you,
grant protection to us.
O Indra and Varuṇa, may this excellent praise reach you both, which I invoke— the joint hymn of praise that you two cause to prosper.
O Brahmaṇaspati, make Soma our praiser,
Kakṣīvat, the son of Uśij.
May he who is wealthy, the dispeller of disease, the finder of riches, the increaser of prosperity— may he, the swift one, attend to us.
May the curse of the stingy mortal, his treacherous assault, not reach us;
protect us, O Brahmaṇaspati!
That mortal whom Indra, Brahmaṇaspati, and Soma impel— verily, that hero does not come to harm.
O Brahmaṇaspati, may you, Soma, and Indra, and may Dakṣiṇā, protect that mortal from distress.
I have approached the wondrous Lord of the Assembly, the beloved and desirable friend of Indra, the winner of wealth and the source of inspired wisdom.
Without whom even the sacrifice of the wise man does not succeed, he promotes the application of our prayers.
Then he makes the performance of the oblation successful; he makes the sacrifice proceed forward, and the invocation goes to the gods.
I have beheld Narāśaṃsa, the most courageous and most far-reaching,
like the dwelling-place of heaven that gathers the sacrifice.
To this beautiful sacrifice you are summoned for protection;
O Agni, come with the Maruts.
Neither god nor mortal is beyond the power of your great will; O Agni, come hither with the Maruts.
O Agni, come with the Maruts— those all-pervading gods who are free from malice and who know the great realm of space.
Those who, fierce and unassailable by their might, have sent forth the hymn of praise—
O Agni, come hither with those Maruts.
Those who are radiant, of terrible form, possessing excellent dominion, and destroyers of enemies—
with those Maruts, O Agni, come hither!
Those gods who dwell upon the luminous vault of the firmament in heaven— O Agni, come hither with the Maruts.
O Agni, come with the Maruts— those who shake the mountains across the billowing ocean.
Those who extend across the ocean with their rays by means of their might— O Agni, come hither with those Maruts.
I pour forth for you the Soma-mead for the first draught;
O Agni, come hither with the Maruts.
This hymn, O gods, for the sake of the people, has been fashioned by the inspired poets with devotion as the bestower of most abundant wealth.
Those who for Indra fashioned with their mind the two bay horses yoked by speech, they have attained the sacrifice through their labors.
For the Nāsatyas they fashioned a comfortable, all-encompassing chariot;
for them they fashioned a cow that yields milk at all times.
The *Ṛbhus*, whose mantras are true and who strive for rectitude, have made their parents young again through their skillful work.
Your exhilarating draughts have come together with Indra accompanied by the Maruts,
and with the Ādityas, the kings.
And that new cup of the divine Tvaṣṭṛ, which had been fashioned,
you made into four again.
Bestow upon us treasures— threefold sets for the one who presses the soma—
with each one granted through our excellent praises.
The bearers [of the sacrifice] have maintained [the ritual]; through their skillful action, they have obtained among the gods a share worthy of sacrifice.
Here I invoke Indra and Agni; we desire their hymn of praise. They two are the supreme drinkers of Soma; they [drink] the Soma.
Praise them at the sacrifices, O men; beautify Indra and Agni;
sing of them in *gāyatra* hymns.
Those two who are the praises of Mitra, Indra and Agni, we invoke them as Soma-drinkers for the drinking of the Soma.
Being mighty ones, we invoke you both to this pressed libation;
may Indra and Agni come hither.
O Indra and Agni, great guardians of the assembly, crush the demons;
let the devourers be childless.
By that truth, be watchful upon the mindful station;
O Indra and Agni, grant us protection.
Awaken the two Aśvins, yoked at dawn; let them come here to drink of this Soma.
Those two who possess excellent chariots, the best of charioteers, the two gods who touch the heavens— those Aśvins we invoke.
O Aśvins, with that whip of yours which is honeyed and full of truth,
sprinkle the sacrifice.
For there is no place far away for you two, where you do not go with your chariot,
O Aśvins, to the house of the Soma-presser.
I invoke Savitṛ, the golden-handed, for aid;
he, the god, knows the place.
Praise Savitṛ, the Son of the Waters, for protection;
we desire to follow his sacred laws.
We invoke Savitṛ, the beholder of men, the distributor of wonderful wealth and bounty.
O friends, sit down; Savitṛ is now to be praised by us—he, the giver of boons, makes them beautiful.
O Agni, bring hither the willing wives of the gods,
and Tvaṣṭṛ, for the drinking of the Soma.
O Agni, youngest one, bring hither for our protection the divine ladies, Hotrā, Bhāratī,
Varūtrī, and Dhiṣaṇā.
May the goddesses, the wives of the lords of men, with their great protection and shelter, come to us with their unbroken wings.
I invoke Indrāṇī here for well-being, Varuṇānī for prosperity,
and Agnāyī for the drinking of Soma.
May the great Heaven and Earth sprinkle this sacrifice for us; may they fill us with nourishments.
The inspired poets lick with their prayers the ghee-rich milk of those two,
in the fixed place of the Gandharva.
O Earth, be pleasant, thornless, and a place of rest for us;
grant us wide-spreading shelter.
May the gods protect us from that place whence Viṣṇu strode forth across the seven domains of the earth.
Viṣṇu strode through this [universe]; in three places he planted his step; his footmark is gathered in the dust.
Viṣṇu, the undeceivable guardian, strode forth his three steps,
thereby upholding the sacred laws.
Behold the deeds of Viṣṇu, through which he has made his vows manifest—
he who is the close ally and friend of Indra.
The wise ever behold that highest step of Viṣṇu,
like an eye fixed in the sky.
The inspired poets, full of praise and ever-watchful, kindle that which is the highest step of Viṣṇu.
Strong are these Soma juices; come hither! These pressed juices are mixed with milk; O Vāyu, drink them as they are set forth.
We invoke both gods, Indra and Vāyu, who touch the heavens,
for the drinking of this Soma.
The inspired poets invoke Indra and Vāyu, who are swift as thought, for their protection— the thousand-eyed lords of our prayers.
We invoke Mitra and Varuṇa for the drinking of Soma—
those who are born with purified strength.
Those two who, through *ṛta*, increase *ṛta* and are the lords of the light of *ṛta*—
those Mitra and Varuṇa I invoke.
May Varuṇa be our protector and Mitra with all his aids;
may they both make us richly blessed.
We invoke Indra, accompanied by the Maruts, for the drinking of the Soma; may he, in harmony with his troop, satisfy himself.
With Indra as their chief, the hosts of Maruts, the gods who grant prosperity through Pūṣan—
may all of them hear my call.
O bounteous ones, with the powerful Indra as your ally, slay Vṛtra;
let not the malevolent one have power over us.
We invoke all the gods, the Maruts, for the drinking of the Soma;
for the fierce ones are the sons of Pṛśni.
Like the roar of victors, the thundering of the Maruts goes forth boldly when you go to glory,
O heroes.
Born from the laughter of lightning, may they protect us;
may the Maruts be gracious to us.
O Pūṣan, O glowing one, bring [the horse] that is upon the variegated sacrificial grass, the support of heaven,
like a lost animal.
Pūṣan, the glowing king, found the one hidden in a secret cave, concealed upon the variegated sacrificial grass.
And so, by means of the drops, he has sent six yoked [oxen] after me; like one who plows barley with cattle, he has tilled [the field].
The waters go along their paths like sisters for those performing the sacrifice,
blending their milk with honeyed sweetness.
Those [goddesses] who are near the sun, or those with whom the sun is joined—
may they speed our sacrifice forward.
I invoke the divine waters where our cattle drink;
an oblation must be prepared for the rivers.
Within the waters is immortality; within the waters is healing. And for the praise of the waters, O gods, be victorious!
Soma has told me that within the waters are all healing remedies,
as well as Agni who brings welfare to all, and the waters which possess every medicine.
O Waters, bestow healing medicine as a protection for my body,
so that I may long behold the sun.
O Waters, carry away this whatever evil is in me—
whether it be that which I have committed as treachery, or that which I have sworn falsely, or even any untruth.
Today I have entered the waters; we have united with their essence.
O Agni, come hither full of milk; endow me with splendor.
O Agni, endow me with splendor, with progeny, and with long life.
May the gods take note of this of mine; may Indra, together with the seers, take note.
Of which of the immortals, of whom indeed, shall we now invoke the beloved name of the god?
Who will give us back to mighty Aditi, so that I may behold my father and my mother?
We meditate upon the name of Agni, the first of the immortals, the beloved name of the god. May he restore us to great Aditi, so that I may behold my father and my mother once more.
O God Savitṛ, sovereign lord of all desirable things, we ever seek a portion from you, O bountiful one.
For whatever Bhaga, exerting himself thus from of old before reproach,
has placed in your hands that which is free from hatred.
May we, as partakers of thy bounty, rise up through thy protection to seize the summit of wealth.
Neither thy dominion, nor thy might, nor thy wrath have these birds flying through the air attained;
nor have these waters flowing with unblinking eyes reached it, nor those who diminish the power of the wind.
In the bottomless [depth], King Varuṇa, whose will is pure, establishes the summit of the tree upright.
Their branches point downward while their base is above; may our banners be established within it.
For King Varuṇa has made wide for the sun a path to follow;
he has provided feet where there were no feet to set them down, and he is the remover even of that which pierces the heart.
A hundred are your physicians, O King, a thousand; let your benevolence be wide and deep.
Drive Nirṛti far away into the distance, and release us from whatever sin we have committed.
Those stars which were placed on high and are seen at night—where indeed do they go by day?
Unswerving are the ordinances of Varuṇa; the moon moves through the night, looking upon them all.
I seek this from you, worshipping with a sacred prayer; the sacrificer desires this through his oblations.
O Varuṇa, be present here without anger; O you of wide renown, do not steal away our life.
This indeed they tell me by night and this by day; this very thought reveals itself from my heart:
may King Varuṇa, whom the captured Śunaḥśepa invoked, release us.
For Śunaḥśepa, seized and bound to three wooden posts, called upon the Āditya.
May King Varuṇa release him; may the wise, undeceivable one, loosen his bonds.
O Varuṇa, we appease your anger with prostrations, with sacrifices, and with oblations.
O wise Asura, O King, as you rule over us, loosen the sins we have committed.
O Varuṇa, loosen the uppermost bond from us, untie the lower one, and release the middle one.
Then, O Āditya, may we, being blameless, abide in your law for the sake of Aditi.
For whatever law of yours we violate day by day, O God Varuṇa, as subjects do [to their king].
Do not deliver us to the weapon of one who seeks to strike, nor to the wrath of one who is angry.
O Varuṇa, with our songs we would loosen your mind for mercy, as a charioteer loosens a tethered horse.
For my prayers, free from anger, fly forth like birds toward their nests, seeking better fortune.
When shall we bring hither Varuṇa, the hero, the glory of dominion, the far-seeing one, for the sake of his mercy?
That same [work] both of them, longing for it, have attained; they do not turn away from the donor who maintains his sacred vows.
He who knows the track of birds flying through the mid-air,
he, the oceanic one, knows the ships upon the sea.
He who is firm in his vows knows the twelve months rich in progeny;
he knows him who is born thereafter.
He knows the path of the wind, vast, exalted, and great; he knows those who dwell above it.
Varuṇa, whose holy law is firm, has sat down in his dwellings for sovereign rule, he of the excellent wisdom.
From there, the wise one beholds all wonders—
those things already done and those yet to be done.
May that Āditya, the one of noble wisdom, make for us fair paths at all times;
may he prolong our lives.
Wearing his golden mantle, Varuṇa has clothed himself in a bright garment;
his spies have settled all around him.
Him whom the seekers of harm do not wish to injure, nor the malevolent among men— no adversaries can overcome that god.
And he who has established incomparable glory among men—
may it abide within our bellies.
My thoughts go forth like cattle to their pastures,
seeking the one of wide vision.
Let us two speak together again, since my honey has been brought;
like a Hotṛ-priest, you shall consume that which is dear.
Behold now him who is visible to all; behold his chariot upon the earth.
May he take pleasure in these my songs.
O Varuṇa, hear this my invocation today and be gracious; seeking your aid, I call upon you.
O wise one, you rule over all, both heaven and earth;
as such, listen well to us upon your path.
Untie for us the uppermost bond, loosen the middle one, and release those below so that we may live.
Clothe yourself, O worthy of sacrifice, Lord of nourishments;
perform this rite of ours.
May the most excellent Hotṛ, O Agni, youngest one, ever [be present] for us through our prayers, with a word that reaches the heavens.
For indeed, the father sacrifices for his son,
the kinsman for his kinsman, and the excellent friend for his friend.
May Varuṇa, Mitra, and Aryaman, the destroyers of enemies, sit upon our sacred grass, as they did for Manu.
O ancient invoker, rejoice in this our friendship;
truly, hear these songs of ours.
For whatever god after god we sacrifice in this perpetual succession,
in you alone is the oblation offered.
May the lord of the people be dear to us—the delightful and excellent Hotṛ-priest;
may we be dear to those who possess good fires.
For the gods, having good sacrificial fires, have bestowed desirable wealth upon us; we, with our own fires, meditate [upon them].
Then, O Immortal One, may there be mutual praises between us, both the mortals and [the gods].
O Agni, with all your fires, accept this sacrifice and this speech;
grant us delight, O son of strength!
I would praise you, Agni, with prostrations, like a prize-winning horse,
you who rule over the sacrifices.
May he indeed, our son, by his power, far-reaching in his course and most gracious,
become a bountiful giver for us.
O you who possess all life, protect us always from the malevolent mortal, both from afar and from near at hand.
O Agni, do you indeed proclaim this our newest song of praise, this means of winning, among the gods.
Grant us a share in the highest spoils, and in those that are middling; bestow upon us wealth from even the nearest source.
O you of variegated luster, you are distributed in the wave of the Sindhu nearby;
instantly you flow for the donor.
O Agni, that mortal whom you protect in battles and whom you urge on in the contests for booty—
he shall be the master of eternal nourishments.
O Overpowering One, no one at all can surpass him;
his strength is worthy of renown.
May he, who belongs to all people, be a conqueror of booty with his horses; may he be a winner of wealth with his inspired singers.
O Jarābodha, offer this beautiful hymn of praise to Rudra, who is worthy of sacrifice among every tribe.
May he, the great one, free from pride, whose banner is smoke, and who is many-shining,
impel us toward wisdom and toward strength.
Like a wealthy lord of the people, may Agni— the divine banner with great radiance— hear us through our hymns of praise.
Homage to the great ones, homage to the small ones; homage to the young, and homage to the aged.
Let us sacrifice to the gods if we are able; O gods, may I not incur the reproach of those who are superior.
Where the broad-based pressing-stone stands upright for the sake of extracting [the juice],
O Indra, drink heartily of the drops pressed by the mortar.
Where the two pressing-boards are fashioned like two buttocks— there, O Indra, you have known and eagerly swallowed the juices pressed by the mortar.
Where the woman learns both the downward and the upward movement— there,
O Indra, you have known and drunk deeply of the juices pressed by the mortar.
Where they bind the churning-stick like one who restrains reins— there,
O Indra, you have known how to gulp down the juices pressed by the mortar.
For even though you, O mortar, are joined in every single house,
here speak with the greatest brilliance, like the drum of the victors.
And indeed, O Lord of the Forest, the wind blows right at your tip;
therefore, O mortar, press out the Soma for Indra to drink.
The two who win the sacrifice, the best at gaining booty— they indeed are held aloft,
devouring the soma-juices like two bay horses.
O lofty Vanaspatis, press today for us with your lofty pressers this honeyed juice for Indra.
Bring the residue from the two ladles; pour the Soma onto the filter;
place it upon the ox-hide.
For even if, O true Soma-drinker, we are as if unpraised,
O Indra, most wealthy one, do you indeed grant us hope for thousands of beautiful cattle and horses.
O Siprin, Lord of spoils, possessor of power,
by your wondrous deed, O Indra, grant us a share of thousands of beautiful cattle and horses, O most wealthy one!
Lull them to sleep, O you two of opposite appearance; let them lie down without waking.
O Indra, most wealthy one, grant us a share of a thousand beautiful cattle and horses!
Let those enemies sleep; O Hero, let the givers wake!
O Indra, bestower of great wealth, grant us a share of a thousand beautiful cattle and horses.
O Indra, crush the donkey who brays with such wicked intent.
O Indra, most wealthy one, grant us a share of a thousand beautiful cattle and horses.
Let the wind blow far away from the forest with its whirling eddies;
O Indra, most wealthy one, grant us a share of a thousand beautiful cattle and horses!
Slay every reviler; crush the Kṛkadāśva!
O Indra, most wealthy one, grant us a share of a thousand beautiful cattle and horses.
Like those seeking booty, we pour out the most bountiful Indra with drops of Soma, as one pours for the hundredfold lord Krivi.
Whether he [offers] a hundred of the pure or a thousand of the milk-mixed,
he indeed flows like water down a slope.
When [the soma] gathers for the sake of his exhilaration, it indeed fills his belly; he possesses a vastness like that of the ocean.
This [song] of yours you gather together like a pigeon to its nest;
yet you do not take heed of that word.
O Hero, Lord of bounties, you who are carried by songs of praise, may your splendor and truthful abundance be ours.
Stand up for our protection in this contest, O Śatakratu;
let us two converse together concerning the others.
In every endeavor and in every contest for booty, we, as friends, invoke Indra, the most powerful one, for our protection.
May he indeed come if he hears us, with his thousandfold aids and with strengths, to our invocation.
I call upon the hero of many defenses from his ancient dwelling,
whom your father called upon of old.
O you who are invoked by many, O possessor of all boons, we entreat you—
O Friend, O Vasu— for the sake of those who sing your praises.
O Soma-drinker, of us who have beautiful jaws, we who drink the soma— O friend, wielder of the thunderbolt, [be the protector] of your friends.
O Soma-drinker, O friend, wielder of the thunderbolt, let it be so; act accordingly, so that we may desire thy favor.
May there be for us, at the banquet with Indra, wealthy and abundant provisions,
by which we, possessing food, may rejoice.
O bold one, surely you yourself, being approached by your praisers,
have granted them [their desires] like a wheelwright fits the axle into the two wheels.
O Lord of a hundred powers, when you fulfill the service and the desire of those who praise you,
you turn [the wheel] as if with your might, like the rolling of a die.
Evermore Indra has won riches with his snorting, roaring, and panting [steeds].
May he, the wonder-worker, grant us a chariot of gold; may he, the winner, give it to us for our winning. He has bestowed it upon us.
O Aśvins, come with your powerful, horse-drawn chariot to this place rich in horses; O wonder-workers, [come] with wealth in cattle and gold.
For your immortal chariot, O wonder-workers, yoked with a single team,
travels upon the ocean, O Aśvins.
You two have fixed the wheel of the chariot upon the head of the inviolable [bull];
the other goes around the sky.
O Uṣas, dear to all, what mortal enjoys you, the immortal one?
To whom do you go, O radiant one?
For we have meditated upon you from near and from afar,
O you who are as wonderful to behold as a dappled, ruddy horse.
Come to us with those very strengths, O Daughter of Heaven; bestow wealth upon us.
O Agni, you were the first Aṅgiras, the seer; as a god, you became the auspicious friend of the gods.
Under your ordinance, the Maruts were born, the sages who act with wisdom, possessing glittering spears.
O Agni, you are the first, the best of the Aṅgiras; as a seer, you encompass the sacred law of the gods.
Pervasive for the entire world, wise, born of two mothers, you lie down in many ways for the sake of the living man.
O Agni, you were the first for Mātariśvan; you became manifest through your skillful wisdom for Vivasvat.
The two worlds, heaven and earth, trembled at the choosing of the Hotṛ-priest; O Vasu, you bore the burden unswervingly and sacrificed for the great ones.
O Agni, you caused the sky to roar for Manu; for the well-doing Purūravas, you were an even greater doer of good.
When you are released from your parents by means of strength, they led you forward once, and then again back to the beginning.
O Agni, you are the bull who increases prosperity; you become worthy of renown for the one who raises the ladle.
You who know the oblation and the *vaṣaṭ*-utterance, you, as the sole life-force, seek to win over the clans at the beginning.
O Agni, you deliver the man who follows crooked paths at the meeting-place in the assembly, O far-seeing one;
he who, in the clash for heroes or in the pursuit of wealth, even with a few, slays the many in the encounter.
O Agni, you establish that mortal in supreme immortality for the sake of glory day by day— you who,
being thirsty for both races of beings, create bliss and provide nourishment to the wise patron.
O Agni, being praised, make us a glorious singer for the winning of riches;
may we succeed through this new work and ritual action. O Heaven and Earth, together with the gods, protect us!

O Agni, you, the blameless and watchful god among the gods, are in the lap of our parents; be the protector of our bodies and the guardian of the singer. O auspicious one, you bestow all wealth upon us.
O Agni, you are our guardian, you are our father; you are the creator of our strength, and we are your kinsmen.
Hundreds and thousands of riches come together unto you, the protector of sacred vows, the invincible one who possesses heroic sons.
O Agni, the gods made you the first living one for the living man, the lord of the tribes of Nahuṣa;
they made Iḷā the instructor of Manu’s progeny, when a son is born from his father.
O Agni, O worshipful god, protect us with your guardians, both our patrons and our own bodies.
You are the savior of our children and grandchildren and of our cattle, watching over them without blinking while we abide in your sacred law.
O Agni, you are kindled as a four-eyed guardian close at hand for the sacrificer who is without a quiver;
you favor with your mind the prayer even of the poor man who has offered oblations so that he may dwell in safety.

O Agni, you win for the priest who praises you widely that most desirable and supreme wealth; you are called the guardian and the father even of the weak; more knowledgeable than the wise, you instruct the simple and point out the directions.
O Agni, you protect the man who offers the sacrificial fee on all sides, like well-sewn armor;
he who provides sweet food, who makes his dwelling pleasant, and who performs the sacrifice of living beings, is the very image of heaven.
O Agni, forgive this our transgression; forgive this path which we have traveled from afar.
You are the kinsman, the father, the guardian of those worthy of Soma; you are the refuge and the inspirer of mortals.
O Agni, O Angiras, like Manu, like Angiras, like Yayāti, come to our seat as of old, O pure one!
Approach, bring hither the divine host, seat them upon the sacrificial grass, and sacrifice to the beloved one.

O Agni, grow strong by this sacred prayer (*brahman*), whether we have performed it for you with skill or with knowledge. And lead us forward toward greater prosperity; unite us with your benevolence that brings abundant strength.
I shall now proclaim the heroic deeds of Indra, those which the wielder of the thunderbolt performed for the first time:
he slew the serpent, he pierced the waters, and he split open the bellies of the mountains.
He slew the serpent as it lay coiled upon the mountain; Tvaṣṭṛ fashioned for him the thunderbolt that roars like heaven.
Like lowing cows, the flowing waters have gone straight down to the ocean.
Acting like a bull, he chose the Soma; at the Trikadruka rites, he drank of the pressed juice.
Maghavan took up his missile, the thunderbolt; he slew him, the first-born of the serpents.
When you, O Indra, slew the first-born of the dragons, and destroyed the magic powers of the deceivers along with their deceptions;
then, generating the sun, the sky, and the dawn, from that time on you truly found no enemy at all.
Indra slew Vṛtra, the worst of Vṛtras, the shoulderless one, with his great thunderbolt, his deadly weapon;
like tree trunks hewn down by an axe, the serpent lies prostrate, pressed against the earth.
Like a mad warrior who does not fight, he indeed challenged the great hero, the much-opposing one, the drinker of the *ṛjīṣa*.
He did not survive the onset of his weapons; Indra’s enemy, being shattered, was crushed to pieces.
Footless and handless, he challenged Indra; Indra struck his thunderbolt upon his back.
Vṛtra, the eunuch who sought to be a match for the bull, lay scattered in many places.
Over him who lies there like a shattered reed, the waters flow surging upward;
even those which Vṛtra encompassed with his might, over them the serpent has come to lie at the feet.
Her strength was cast down; Indra struck down the weapon against this son of Vṛtra.
The mother was above, the son was below; Dānu lies there like a cow with her calf.
The body was cast into the midst of the standing, unsheltered waters;
the waters flow over Vṛtra’s secret place. He whose enemy was Indra sank into long-lasting darkness.
The waters stood confined, having the Dāsa as their lord and the serpent as their guardian, like cows held captive by the Paṇis.
Having slain Vṛtra, he threw open that which was the closed-up mouth of the waters.
O Indra, you became a horse-hair tail-whisker when the god, alone, struck at you with his bolt;
you won the cattle, O hero, you won the Soma, and you released the seven rivers to flow.
Neither lightning nor thunder could restrain him, nor the mist and the hailstorm that he scattered;
when Indra and Ahi fought, the bounteous Maghavan emerged victorious over them all.
Whom did you see as the pursuer of the serpent, O Indra, when fear came to your heart after you had struck him down?
And when you crossed the nine and ninety flowing rivers, like a hawk afraid, you traversed the regions of space.

Indra, the wielder of the thunderbolt, is the king of what moves and what is stationary, of the hornless and of the horned. He alone rules as king over the peoples; he encompasses them all, as the felly surrounds the spokes.
Come hither, O seekers of cattle, to Indra; may he increase our excellent providence.
Being free from debt, will he not surely turn toward us the highest desire for this wealth of cattle?
I have approached the unassailable giver of wealth; like a falcon to its nest, I fly to him who is well-pleased.
Paying homage to Indra with these highest hymns—he who is to be invoked by those who praise him on his journey.
With his full army, he has hung his quivers; the noble lord drives away the cattle of whomever he desires.
O Indra, bestowing abundant wealth, do not become a miser toward us, O you who have grown great!

For you, O Indra, moving alone with your aids, have slain the wealthy Dasyu with your weapon. From the wealth [of the enemy], the Sanakas who did not sacrifice fled in all directions; they went to their destruction.
Even those who do not sacrifice, O Indra, have turned their heads away from you, vying with those who do sacrifice.
When you, O fierce driver of the bay horses, blew them away from heaven and earth, you cast down the lawless ones.
They sought to battle the army of the blameless one; the Navagva peoples exerted themselves.
Like castrated bulls striving for a bull, they fled in defeat; through their cries, they made themselves known to Indra.
O Indra, you fought these weeping and laughing ones at the far limit of the mid-air;
you burned down the Dasyu from on high from heaven, and you protected the prayer of those who press the juice and offer praise.
Forming an enclosure around the earth, adorning themselves with gold and jewels, they did not overtake Indra as they sped along; he placed his spies around him by means of the sun.
When you, O Indra, encompassed both heaven and earth on all sides with your greatness,
you blew away the Dasyu with your sacred prayers— those who were not mindful, by means of those who were mindful.

They who have not reached the limit of heaven or earth, nor have they overcome the Giver of Wealth with their magic powers—Indra, the Bull, made the thunderbolt his ally; with light, he milked the cows out from the darkness.
The waters flowed according to their own nature; he grew great in the midst of the navigable rivers.
With a concentrated mind, Indra struck him down with his most powerful blow for all time.
Indra shattered the strongholds of Ilībiśa and split apart the horned Śuṣṇa;
O Maghavan, with as much speed and as much might as you possessed, you slew the attacking enemy with your thunderbolt.
The successful one has overcome his enemies; with his sharp bull-like weapon, he shattered the fortresses. Indra struck Vṛtra with his thunderbolt; triumphing, he furthered his own purpose.
O Indra, you protected Kutsa in whom you took delight; you aided the fighting bull Daśadyu.
The dust raised by his hooves reached the sky, and Śvaitreya stood firm for the conquest of men.

You protected the peaceful bull among the Tugryas; O Maghavan, you won the white cow in the contest for land. Having remained there for a long time, they made their effort; you brought low the possessions of those who acted as enemies.
O Aśvins, be mindful of us even thrice today; far-reaching is your journey and your bounty.
For your guidance is like a garment in winter; may you be drawn toward us by the wise.
Three are the fellies on your honey-bearing chariot; all people know it follows the longing for Soma.
Three supports are firmly set for you to grasp; thrice by night you travel, O Aśvins, and thrice by day.
On this same day, O Aśvins, you who conceal the blameless, sprinkle the sacrifice thrice today with honey;
thrice, O Aśvins, swell for us food rich in booty at evening and at dawn.
Come three times to our dwelling, thrice to the people who follow your law; bestow your aid threefold, as if in three ways, upon the one who offers well.
O Aśvins, bring us joy thrice; thrice pour nourishment upon us like inexhaustible waters.
O Aśvins, bring us wealth thrice; thrice in the assembly of the gods and thrice protect our prayers.
Thrice grant us prosperity and thrice grant us renown; thrice has the daughter of the Sun mounted your three-seated chariot.
O Aśvins, grant us thrice the celestial medicines, thrice the earthly, and thrice those from the waters.
O Lords of Splendor, bring threefold protection and well-being for my son, and bestow your shelter.
O Aśvins, worthy of sacrifice, three times every day you have traversed the earth in its threefold extent.
O Nāsatyas, chariot-borne ones, come from the far distance to our three dwellings like the wind to its own resting places.

O Aśvins, thrice with the seven mother rivers, three are the mixing-vessels; the oblation is prepared in three ways. Three earths are beneath you, and you protect the vault of heaven established above by days and nights.

Where are the three wheels of your threefold chariot? Where are the three seats that share a common foundation? When is the harnessing of the vigorous donkey by which you, O Nāsatyas, come to our sacrifice?
O Nāsatyas, come hither; the oblation is being offered. Drink of the honey with your honey-drinking mouths.
For Savitṛ sends forth for you two, at the first flush of dawn, his wondrous, oil-rich chariot for the sake of the cosmic order.
O Nāsatyas, O Aśvins, come here with the thirty-three gods to the drinking of the honeyed mead.
Prolong our lifespan, wipe away our sins, drive off our enemies, and be our companions.
O Aśvins, on your three-wheeled chariot, bring hither to us wealth consisting of heroic sons. Hearing me, I call upon you for protection; be present for our increase and for the winning of booty.
I invoke Agni first for well-being; I invoke Mitra and Varuṇa here for protection. I invoke Night, who brings rest to all that moves; I invoke the god Savitṛ for aid.
Advancing through the dark expanse, establishing both the immortal and the mortal,
the god Savitṛ comes upon his golden chariot, beholding all living beings.
The god goes by the downward path, he goes by the upward path; the worshipful one goes with his two bright bay horses.
The god Savitṛ comes from afar, driving away all difficulties.
Enveloped in pearls, multiform, with a golden yoke-pin, the worshipful and great Savitar, of wondrous luster, has mounted his chariot, assuming his power over the dark realms.
The dark-hued, white-footed steeds have looked upon the people, drawing the chariot with its golden fore-shaft.
Constantly, all the clans and all living beings have stood within the lap of the divine Savitar.
Three heavens belong to Savitṛ; two are his laps, and one is in the realm of Yama, where he dwells among the heroes.
Like the linchpin of a chariot, they have stood firm upon the immortal; let him who understands this declare it here.
The well-winged one has surveyed the mid-air; the Asura of profound inspiration is a good leader.
Where now is Sūrya? Who has perceived it? To which heaven has his ray extended?
Savitar, the golden-eyed god, has come, beholding the eight quarters of the earth, the three desert regions, and the seven rivers; he bestows desirable treasures upon the donor.
Savitar, the golden-handed, the all-beholding, moves between both heaven and earth;
he drives away disease, impels the sun, and reaches the sky through the dark expanse.
May the golden-handed Asura, the good leader, the very gracious and self-strong one, come hither;
driving away the Rākṣasas and Yātudhānas, the god has taken his stand, being praised at every twilight.
O Savitṛ, those paths of yours which are ancient, dustless, and well-prepared in the mid-air—
by those easy-to-traverse paths, protect us today and speak for us, O God!
We implore with hymns and words Agni— the youthful one among many, whom the clans seeking the gods worship, and whom others indeed invoke.
People have established Agni, the increaser of strength; we, possessing oblations, shall worship you. As such, be well-disposed toward us here today as our protector in battles, O worthy one.
We choose you as our messenger, the all-knowing Hotṛ-priest.
As you exist in greatness, your flames spread abroad; your rays touch the heavens.
The gods—Varuṇa, Mitra, and Aryaman—kindle you, the ancient messenger.
O Agni, that mortal who offers oblations to you wins all wealth through you.
O Agni, you are the delightful invoker, the master of the household, and the messenger of the people;
in you all the firm ordinances that the gods have established are gathered together.

In thee alone, O Agni, most youthful and fortunate one, is every oblation offered. As such, being well-disposed toward us today and in the future, worship the gods so that we may possess heroic strength.
To him indeed, the self-radiant one, the reverent ones sit down;
with oblations men kindle Agni, having overcome all failures.
Slaying Vṛtra, they crossed over heaven and earth and the waters; they have made for themselves a wide dwelling.
May the Bull, invoked with oblations, become glorious for Kaṇva; may the steed neigh in the raids for cattle.
Sit down together; you are great. Shine forth, O best invoker of the gods!
O Agni, worthy of the sacrificial food, O praiseworthy one, emit your ruddy smoke, beautiful to behold.
O carrier of oblations, you whom the gods established here for Manu as the best of sacrificers;
you whom Kaṇva Medhyātithi, Vṛṣan, and Upastuta [invoked] as the winner of wealth.
The Agni whom Medhyātithi Kaṇva kindled from the Eternal Order (ṛta)—his flames have shone forth; we magnify that Agni with these very hymns.
Fill us with wealth, O self-dependent one, for you, O Agni, possess kinship among the gods.
You rule over glorious booty; as such, be gracious to us, for you are great.
Stand up erect for our protection, like the god Savitṛ;
stand erect as the winner of booty when we, with our ointments, call upon you together with the priests.
Standing upright, protect us from distress with your banner; burn up every devouring demon.
Raise us up so that we may move and live; find for us honor among the gods.
Protect us, O Agni, from the Rakṣas; protect us from the malice of the stingy.
Protect us from him who seeks to harm us or from him who desires to kill us, O youngest one of lofty luster!
Like a club, strike down on all sides the stingy ones, O you with burning jaws, who seeks to harm us.
Whatever mortal whets his weapon against us through the nights—let not that enemy have power over us.
Agni won great heroic power; Agni [won] prosperity for Kaṇva.
Agni protected Mitra and Medhyātithi; Agni [protected] Upastuta in the winning of booty.
Through Agni we call Turvaśa and Yadu from afar, and Ugrādeva;
Agni brought Navavāstva, Bṛhadratha, and Turvīti as a force for subduing the Dasyu.
Manu established you, O Agni, as a light for all people forever;
you shone forth, O Kaṇva, born of Truth, strengthened by oblations, whom the human races revere.
The brilliant, impetuous, and terrible flames of Agni are not to be withstood;
burn up forever the Rakṣas-demon, the sorcerer, and every devouring Atriṇ.
Sing forth, O Kaṇvas, to your sporting host of Maruts, the unassailable, who shine upon their chariots.
Those who were born with spotted deer, spears, axes, and ointments, possessing their own inherent luster.
As if right here one hears the cracking of the whips in their hands as they speak; they hasten toward a wondrous goal on their journey.
Sing forth a god-given prayer for your impetuous host, of brilliant splendor and mighty strength.
Praise the bull among the cows, for the Marut host is sporting;
it has grown strong upon the savor of the juice.
Who among you, O heroes, shakers of heaven and earth, is the most exalted,
when you shake them as if shaking the very edge?
At your approach, no mortal can withstand your fierce wrath;
even the mountain, the rocky peak, yields away.
At whose marches the earth trembles in fear during their journeys, like an aged lord of the people.
For firm indeed is their birth, their vigor to emerge from the mother,
since their strength is twofold according to her.
These sons have extended their songs like goal-posts in their courses,
lowing as they hasten knee-deep.
Even that long and broad son of the cloud, the one who does not fail,
they cause to move forth on their journeys.
O Maruts, when your strength has caused the people to tremble, you have made even the mountains tremble.
When the Maruts go along, they speak together on the way;
does anyone hear them?
Come forth quickly with your swift steeds; there are offerings for you among the Kaṇvas.
Rejoice well there.
For there is indeed [enough] for your exhilaration; we truly belong to them.
May they grant us a full span of life to live.
When indeed now, O you for whom the sacred grass is trimmed, do you hold [us] in your hands like a father who loves his son?
Where now, and for what purpose, will you go from heaven or from earth? Where do you take delight, like cattle?
Where, O Maruts, are your newest favors? Where are your blessings? And where are all your auspicious gifts?
O you whose mother is Pṛśni, if you were mortals,
your worshipper would be immortal.
May your singer not be like a deer in a pasture that finds no pleasure;
may he not go upon the path of Yama.
Let not Destruction, with her evil intent, strike us down further and further;
let her perish along with Thirst.
Truly, these fierce and impetuous sons of Rudra create windless mist even upon the desert.
Like a lowing cow, the lightning bellows; like a mother following her calf, she follows when their rain has been released.
Even by day they create darkness with Parjanya, the bearer of waters,
when they drench the earth.
Then, at the roar of the Maruts, every earthly dwelling trembled;
all human beings shook.
O Maruts, with your firm-hoofed steeds, travel along the variegated riverbanks with unwearied courses.
Firm be the fellies of your chariots, firm the horses of these steeds, and well-fashioned the reins.
Address yourself with this continuous song to praise Brahmaṇaspati,
to Agni who is as beautiful to behold as Mitra.
Fashion the hymn within your mouth; spread it abroad like Parjanya. Sing the Gāyatra song worthy of praise.
Worship the Marut host, the brilliant, the praiseworthy, the singers;
may they be increased for us here.
When you thus cast forth your measure like a flame from afar—by whose wisdom, O Maruts, by whose form do you go? To whom do you go, O shakers?
May your weapons be firm for driving away the foe, strong for resisting the enemy.
May your power be most praiseworthy; let it not belong to the wily mortal.
When you strike down what is firm, O heroes, and whirl about what is heavy;
you pass through the trees of the earth and through the regions of the mountains.
For no enemy of yours has been found in heaven nor upon the earth, O you who destroy the foe. O Rudras, may your power remain with your own offspring; it is not to be assailed even now.
They make the mountains tremble; they shake the lords of the forest.
O Maruts, you have come forth like those intoxicated with wine—O gods, together with your entire host.
You have harnessed the spotted deer to your chariots; the ruddy horse draws as a leader.
Even the earth itself has listened to your approach; mortal men were struck with fear.
O Rudras, we quickly choose your protection for the sake of our offspring; come now to us with your aid as you did of old, even for Kaṇva who was afraid.
O Maruts, whatever monstrous thing sent by you or sent by mortals assails us,
drive it away with your power, drive it away with your might, and drive it away with your protections.
For you, O wise Maruts, who are worthy of sacrifice, have bestowed the perfect Kaṇva;
come to us with your perfect aids, as lightning brings rain.
O bounteous ones, you possess full power; O shakers, you possess full might.
O Maruts, wrathful against the hater of the seer, do not discharge hatred like an arrow.
Arise, O Brahmaṇaspati! We, seeking the gods, call upon you.
May the Maruts, the bounteous givers, come forward; O Indra, be swift in their company.
For it is you alone, O Son of Strength, that the mortal calls upon when the prize is set; may he who longs for you, O Maruts, obtain great heroic power, good horses, and noble steeds.
May Brahmanaspati come forward; may the goddess Sūnṛtā come forward.
May the gods lead our sacrifice toward the hero, the manly one who bestows fivefold gifts.
He who gives excellent wealth to the singer gains imperishable fame;
for him we offer the *iḷā*—rich in heroes, victorious, and free from blemish.
Now indeed Brahmaṇaspati speaks forth the hymn worthy of praise,
in which Indra, Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryaman, and the gods have made their dwellings.
Let us recite that hymn at the assemblies which brings well-being, O Gods, and is free from blemish.
And may you welcome this speech, O Heroes; may it obtain all desirable things from you.
Who has reached the person who seeks the gods, who has prepared the sacred grass? The donor has stepped forth with his dwellings; he has established a home within, providing for himself.

He bestows sovereign power; he strikes down [enemies] with kings; even in the midst of fear, he establishes a secure dwelling. For the wielder of the thunderbolt, there is no one to obstruct him or overcome him, whether in a great battle or a small one.
The person whom the far-seeing Varuṇa, Mitra, and Aryaman protect—
never indeed is that man harmed.
The mortal whom they carry across as if with their arms and protect from harm,
he prospers entirely, unharmed.
The kings of these [Maruts] strike down difficult passes and hostile fortresses; they lead them across all misfortunes.
Easy to traverse is the path, free from thorns, for him who walks the *ṛta*, O Ādityas;
there is no devouring here for you.
O heroes, O Ādityas, whatever sacrifice you lead by the straight path,
may that reach your devotion.
That mortal, unwearied, goes forth in person toward all precious wealth and toward his offspring.
How, O friends, may we accomplish the hymn of praise for Mitra and Aryaman—
the great refreshment of Varuṇa?
I do not speak back to you who strike nor to him who curses, for he seeks the gods; with good wishes alone do I invite you.
One should fear even one who gives four [cows], until he has finished bestowing them;
one should not long for ill-spoken words.
O Pūṣan, traverse the paths; O Son of Deliverance, pass over our distress. Come, O God, and go before us.
O Pūṣan, whatever malevolent wolf or ill-omened one plots against us—
drive him away from our path.
Drive far away from the path that robber who lies in wait, the thief who plots against us.
Drive him far beyond our track.
Trample with your foot the burning heat of that two-faced, evil-plotting person, whoever he may be.
O wondrous Pūṣan, we choose that aid of yours, O wise one,
by which you urged on our ancestors.
Then, O possessor of all fortune, most excellent wielder of the golden axe, make our riches easy to win.
Lead us beyond those who attack us; make our paths easy to traverse and fair for us to travel.
O Pūṣan, find wisdom for us here.
Lead us toward good pasture; let there be no new fever upon our path.
O Pūṣan, find wisdom for us here.
Be able, fill us full, and bestow; sharpen [our senses] and expand your belly.
O Pūṣan, find the power of will for us here.
We do not provoke Pūṣan; we praise him with hymns.
We beg the wondrous one for riches.
What may we utter to Rudra, the wise, the most bounteous, the most powerful,
that is most pleasing to his heart?
So that Aditi may grant us the power of Rudra for our cattle, for our men, for our kine, and for our offspring.
So that Mitra and Varuṇa, so that Rudra may take heed of us, and so that all the gods, being of one accord, may do the same.
To Rudra, the lord of songs, the lord of sacrifices, the possessor of healing medicines— unto him we seek that auspicious favor which brings well-being.
He who shines like the bright sun, like gold,
the most excellent Vasu among the gods.
May he grant well-being to our horse, a good path for the ram and the ewe,
and for our men, women, and cattle.
O Soma, bestow upon us the splendor of a hundred men,
great renown, and abundant manly strength.
Let not those who obstruct the Soma, nor the enemies, deceive us. O Indu, grant us a share in the prize.

Those offspring of yours who are in the highest abode of immortality, in the realm of *ṛta*—O Soma, as the head and the navel, you, the lover, know them as they adorn themselves; O Soma, you are their wealth.
O immortal Agni, bring hither today from the radiant dawn the wondrous gift, O Jātavedas; bring the gods who awaken at dawn to the one who offers oblations.
For you are the beloved messenger, the bearer of oblations, O Agni, the charioteer of the sacrifices.
In harmony with the Aśvins and Uṣas, bestow upon us great heroic power and high renown.
Today we choose as our envoy Agni, the Vasu, beloved by many—
the one whose banner is smoke, who is radiant with light, and who is the glory of the sacrifice at the break of dawn.
I praise Agni Jātavedas at the break of dawn— the most excellent, the youngest guest, well-invoked, beloved by the man who offers oblations— so that he may go toward the gods.
I shall praise you, O immortal sustainer of all; O Agni, worthy of the sacrificial meal, most excellent sacrificer, bearer of oblations, the immortal protector.
O youngest one, be a bringer of good praise to the singer; you who have honeyed speech and are well-invoked with oblations.
Prolonging the life of Praskaṇva so that he may live, pay homage to the divine host.
For the people kindle you, the all-knowing Hotṛ;
therefore, O Agni, much-invoked and wise one, bring the gods here swiftly.
At the dawning of the night, the Kaṇvas, having pressed the Soma, kindle you— Savitṛ, Uṣas, the Aśvins, Bhaga, and Agni— the bearer of oblations, O performer of the fair sacrifice.
For you, O Agni, are the lord of sacrifices and the messenger of the people;
bring hither today the gods who awaken at dawn and behold the light of heaven, for the drinking of the Soma.
O Agni, rich in light, you have shone throughout the former dawns, visible to all. You are the protector in the villages, the domestic priest, and the friend of men at the sacrifices.
O Agni, we establish you as the accomplisher of the sacrifice, the Hotṛ priest and officiant—
like Manu, O God, the wise, the swift, the immortal messenger.
When you, O Agni, great as Mitra among the gods, go as the domestic priest and the intimate messenger between them,
the flames of Agni flash like the roaring waves of the river Sindhu.
Hear us, O Agni, whose ear is keen, together with the gods who are your carriers and your companions. Let Mitra, Aryaman, and those who go forth at dawn sit upon the sacred grass at our sacrifice.
May the Maruts, the bounteous givers, whose tongue is Agni and who increase the Truth, hear our hymn of praise. May Varuṇa, whose laws are firm, drink the Soma together with the Aśvins and Uṣas.
O Agni, worship here the Vasus, the Rudras, and the Ādityas—
the host of well-performing sacrifices, born of Manu, who sprinkle the clarified butter.
For the wise gods are attentive to the donor, O Agni;
O lover of songs, bring here those thirty-three who have ruddy horses.
O Jātavedas, like Priyamedha, Atri, and Virūpa,
and like Aṅgiras, O you of mighty vows, hear the invocation of Praskaṇva.
The Mahikerus and the Priyamedhas have invoked for their protection Agni,
who rules over the sacrifices with his bright radiance.
O you who are invoked with clarified butter, O Holy One, truly hear these songs by which the sons of Kaṇva call upon you for protection.
O Agni, most renowned for your wondrous glory, the people among the tribes invoke you— the one with flaming hair, beloved by many— to carry their oblations.

The inspired poets have established you, O Agni, as the Hotṛ priest and officiating minister, the greatest finder of wealth, with listening ears and most far-reaching, during the sacrifices for heaven.
The inspired singers, having pressed the Soma, have drawn you toward the sacrificial food;
O Agni, bearing the great light as an oblation for the mortal who offers gifts.
O Bounteous One, Son of Strength, worthy of truth, seat here today upon the sacred grass the divine host who come at dawn, for the drinking of the Soma.
O Agni, with joint invocations, worship the divine host so that they turn hitherward;
O bounteous ones, here is the Soma, drink it which was pressed yesterday.
This unprecedented Dawn shines forth, the beloved of heaven;
I praise you both, O Aśvins, with a lofty hymn.
O wonder-workers, sons of Sindhu, discoverers of riches,
O gods who find wealth through inspired thought!
Your towering steeds are urged forward upon the ancient surface of the earth,
when your chariot flies with its winged birds.
The lover of the waters fills [them] with oblation, O heroes; he is the filler, the father of the cloud, the one who moves among the people.
O Nāsatyas, you who are praised by our hymns, you are the recipients of our prayers;
drink of the Soma with boldness.
O Aśvins, grant us that nourishment which, full of light, may carry us across the darkness. Grant us that food.
Come to us in the ship of our prayers, so that we may reach the further shore; O Aśvins, harness your chariot!
Your oar is broad as the sky; your chariot is at the ford of the rivers. The drops have been yoked by prayer.
O Kaṇvas, the drops [of Soma] are from heaven; [they are] at the place of the rivers' treasure. Where will you two place your own covering?
Light has indeed appeared for the sake of the Soma-stalk; the sun shines forth against it.
He who is dark-tongued has looked out with his tongue.
A path for crossing to the further shore has indeed appeared by the straight way of *ṛta*; the track from heaven has been seen.
This very aid of the Aśvins, who protect us while we drink the Soma, the singer honors again and again.
Dwelling with Vivasvat through the drinking of Soma and by means of our song, O you who bring well-being like Manu, come hither!
The Dawn has followed after the splendor of you two who move around the earth;
you win the cosmic order through the nights.
Drink both of you, O Aśvins; grant us protection both of you with your unimpaired aids.
O you two who increase the cosmic order (*ṛta*), this most honey-sweet Soma has been pressed for you;
O Aśvins, drink it—the [Soma] of the day before yesterday—and bestow treasures upon the donor.
Come hither, O Aśvins, on your well-adorned chariot with three seats and threefold structure;
the Kaṇvas offer prayers for you at the sacrifice—listen well to their call!
O Aśvins, increasers of cosmic order, drink the most honey-sweet Soma.
Then today, O wonder-workers, bringing wealth upon your chariot, come to the donor.
O possessors of all wealth, sprinkle the sacrifice with honey upon the threefold sacred grass;
the Kaṇvas, having pressed the Soma and looking toward heaven, call upon you both, O Aśvins.
O Aśvins, lords of splendor, with those same aids wherewith you protected Kaṇva, protect us as well; drink the Soma, O you who increase the cosmic order.
O wonder-workers, bringing wealth on your chariot, bring nourishment to Sudās, O Aśvins;
bestow upon us riches from the ocean or even from heaven—riches desired by many.
Whether you two Nāsatyas are in the distance, or whether you abide among the Turvaśas,
come hither from there on your well-rolling chariot together with the rays of the sun.
May your coursers, who grace the sacrifice, bring you both hither to the libations;
bestowing nourishment upon the doer of good, O bounteous ones, sit upon the sacred grass, O heroes.
With that chariot of sun-like skin, O Nāsatyas,
come hither— by which you have constantly brought wealth to the donor for the drinking of the sweet Soma.
With hymns and songs of praise, we call hither for protection the two lords of many riches;
for in the beloved assembly of the Kaṇvas, you have repeatedly drunk the Soma, O Aśvins.
O Dawn, daughter of heaven, shine upon us with the left [hand] for our benefit;
O radiant goddess, bestowing gifts, shine forth with great splendor and wealth.
Rich in horses, rich in cattle, bestowing all wealth, they hasten forth in abundance to shine. O Uṣas, stir up for me the gifts of truth; impel the bounty of the liberal patrons.
The goddess Dawn has shone forth and now shines again, she who quickens the chariots— those who,
like those seeking glory upon the ocean, have set their hearts upon her arrivals.
O Uṣas, those wise patrons who yoke their minds for the sake of giving during your arrivals—
among them, here indeed, Kaṇva, the best of the Kaṇvas, praises the name of these heroes.
Like a noble woman, Dawn approaches, bestowing her gifts;
making all that has feet grow old, she moves forth and causes the birds to fly up.
She who sends forth the assembly and the seekers of wealth, she who goes forth like one seeking her station; at your dawning, O lady rich in booty, no birds that have flown remain still.
She has yoked her chariot from afar, from the rising place of the sun; this fortunate Dawn approaches human beings, traveling with a hundred chariots.
The whole world has bowed down before her gaze; the noble daughter of heaven makes light for all. May the wealthy Dawn, the daughter of heaven, shine away our hatreds and drive away our enemies.
O Uṣas, daughter of heaven, shine upon us with your radiant and beautiful light,
bringing us abundant fortune as you dawn during our sacrifices.
For you alone are the breath and the life of all, when you dawn abroad, O noble lady.
As such, O radiant one with great chariot, hear our call, you whose wealth is wondrous.
O Uṣas, win for us the prize that is wonderful among the human race;
with that, bring the well-performed sacrifices hither to those who, as priests, sing your praises.
Bring all the gods from the mid-air, O Uṣas, for the drinking of the Soma! Bestow upon us, O Uṣas, wealth in cattle, wealth in horses, praiseworthy strength, and heroic vigor.
She whose radiant, auspicious rays have appeared—
may that Uṣas grant us wealth containing all boons, well-fashioned and easy to attain.
For even those seers of old who invoked you for protection and great aid— O Dawn,
with your bright radiance, graciously accept our hymns and our offerings of wealth.
O Uṣas, when today you open wide the two doors of heaven with your radiance,
grant us a broad, secure shelter free from danger, and, O Goddess, bestow upon us food consisting of cattle.
