O Dawn, bestow upon us great wealth adorned with all forms; sprinkle us with nourishing offerings, with splendor that overcomes all, and with strengths, O thou who art rich in prizes!
O Uṣas, come with auspicious things even from the luminous realm of heaven;
let those whose steeds are ruddy bring you to the house of the Soma-presser.
O Uṣas, with that well-fashioned and easy-to-drive chariot upon which you have mounted, protect today,
O Daughter of Heaven, the people of illustrious fame.
Even the winged birds, the bipeds, and the quadrupeds,
O radiant Uṣas, have awakened according to the seasons from the very ends of heaven.
For as you shine forth with your rays, you illuminate the entire radiant realm;
as such, O Uṣas, the Kaṇvas, desiring wealth, have invoked you with their songs.
Upward those rays of light bear him, the god Jātavedas,
the Sun, so that everyone may behold him.
Like thieves, those stars depart with the nights for the Sun who beholds all things.
His banners have become visible; his rays extend across the people, shining like blazing fires.
O Sūrya, you are the one who carries us across, visible to all, the maker of light; you illuminate the entire radiant realm.
Facing the clans of the gods, facing men, you rise up;
facing all, you shine for us to see.
O Purifier, with that eye wherewith you, O Varuṇa, behold the people as they stir about, [look upon us].
O Sūrya, you traverse the wide sky and the vast mid-region, measuring out the days by means of the nights, beholding all living beings.
O divine Sūrya, seven bay horses carry you in your chariot— you,
the far-seeing one with hair of flame.
The Sun has yoked the seven bright mares, the daughters of his chariot;
with them, as his own team, he goes forth.
Beholding the higher light beyond the darkness,
we have gone forth from there to the god Sūrya among the gods, to the supreme light.
Rising today, O Sūrya, great as Mitra, ascending the highest heaven, destroy my heart-disease and my jaundice.
We place my yellowness in the parrots, we place it in the starlings;
and so, we deposit my yellowness in the yellow-woodpeckers.
This Āditya has risen with all his power, subduing for me whoever hates me; may I not be subdued by the one who hates me.
Exhilarate with songs that Indra, the ram invoked by many, the praiseworthy one who is a flood of wealth;
him whose human [deeds] do not pass away like the heavens, the most generous, praise the inspired singer for our enjoyment.
His aids have favored him, the one who possesses excellent assistance, who fills the mid-air and is encompassed by powers;
the skillful Rbhus have mounted Indra, who distills exhilaration, the lord of a hundred powers, with swift and pleasant speech.
You opened up the cow-stall for the Aṅgirases; as their protector, you found the way for Atri among the hundred-doored [enclosures].
You brought wealth even with his army to Vimada; in the battle, you made the pressing-stone dance for the one who was clothed in the Soma.
You opened the coverings of the waters; you held the water-bearing wealth upon the mountain.
When you, O Indra, slew the serpent Vṛtra with your might, you then caused the sun to ascend in heaven so that it might be seen.
By your wondrous powers, you cast down the sorcerers who, by their own self-willed acts, offered oblations upon the sleeping ground.
O hero-minded one, you shattered the fortresses of Pipru; you protected Ṛjiśvan in his battles against the Dasyus.
You protected Kutsa in the slayings of Śuṣṇa; you delivered Śambara over to Atithigva.
You trampled even the great Arbuda under your foot. From of old, you were born for the slaying of the Dasyus.
In you all powers are gathered together; your bounty rejoices for the drinking of Soma.
Your thunderbolt, placed within your arms, is manifest; shatter all the manly strengths of the enemy.
Discriminate between the noble ones and those who are Dasyus; subjecting the lawless, bring them under the control of the one who has spread the sacrificial grass.
Be powerful, an inciter for the sacrificer; I delight in all these deeds of yours at our common feasts.
Subduing those who follow no sacred law for the sake of him who follows the law, Indra, with his helpers, struck down the powerless;
though he was already grown great, as he strove to reach the sky while increasing, the praised Vamra shattered his gathered hosts.
When Uśanas fashioned for you a power more powerful than power itself, your might forced the two worlds asunder by its greatness.
O hero-minded one, the mind-yoked steeds of the wind bore you toward glory as you were swelling with strength.
When Indra rejoiced with Uśanas Kāvya, he mounted his two swift steeds, the swifter of the two;
the fierce one set the flowing waters free from their course and shattered the strongholds of Śuṣṇa.
O you who drink from the strong vessels, you mount your chariot among those offerings presented by Śāryāta, in which you take delight;
O Indra, just as you have found pleasure in the pressed Soma-juices, you ascend to the unassailable song of praise in heaven.
O Indra, you gave the young Vṛcayā to the great and eloquent Kakṣīvat, who was pressing the soma.
O wise one, you became the consort of Vṛṣaṇaśva; all these deeds of yours are to be proclaimed at the Soma-pressings.
Indra has been established in the exclusive presence of the pious; among the Pajras, the hymn of praise is like a sacrificial post in the doorway.
Seeking horses, seeking cattle, seeking chariots, and seeking wealth—Indra alone is the ruler and bestower of riches.
This homage has been spoken to the bull, the self-ruling one, whose vigor is truth and who is powerful:
O Indra, in this assembly, may we, with all our heroes and together with the patrons, abide under your protection.
That ram, the finder of light, whom a hundred strong ones accompany all at once—
may I turn Indra hither for aid with well-fashioned hymns, like a prize-winning steed or a chariot that hastens to the call.
Like a mountain unshakable upon its foundations, he of a thousand aids has grown strong in his powers;
Indra, when he struck down Vṛtra who encompassed the rivers, subduing the floods, exulting in the soma-juice.
For he is the opener among openers, the chooser at the udder; he whose base is bright, who is strengthened by exhilaration through the wise.
That Indra I have invoked with a prayer of skillful workmanship—he whose gift is most liberal, for he is the fulfiller of the soma-juice.
Him whom those seated on the sacred grass in heaven fill, like the ocean with their own well-being and desires;
him Indra, the slayer of Vṛtra, his aids followed in battle—his impetuous, unassailable helpers of undeviating form.
In the exhilaration of this [Soma], as he fought for his own rain, his aids sped forth like swift mares down a slope;
when Indra, the wielder of the thunderbolt, boldly emboldened by the plant, shattered the enclosures of Vala as Trita did.
He moves about with fervor; his power has blazed forth. Having encompassed the waters, he lay upon the foundation of the firmament.
When, O Indra, you struck Vṛtra—who was difficult to seize on the slope—with the thunderbolt between his jaws, you brought him low.
For the waves do not overwhelm you, O Indra, like those surging into a lake—those prayers of yours which are your means of strengthening.
Even Tvaṣṭṛ increased your fitting power; he fashioned the thunderbolt of overwhelming force.
Having slain Vṛtra with your bay steeds, O Indra of gathered power, you made a path for the waters for the sake of man.
You hurled the iron thunderbolt from your arms; you established the sun in heaven so that it might be seen.
When they made for themselves that lofty, self-luminous, and powerful ascent to heaven worthy of praise, out of fear;
when the Maruts, the helpers who win the light and accompany the heroes, rejoiced along with Indra in the battles for men.
Even the heaven itself trembled in fear at the roar of your serpent-slaying bolt, O Indra;
when, in the exhilaration of the pressed juice, you shattered with your might the head of Vṛtra as he was pressing against both worlds.
When, O Indra, the earth was tenfold and the peoples spread through all the days, even then,
O Maghavan, your renowned power became equal to heaven in might and greatness.

On the far side of this space, of the sky, you—whose power is self-existent, whose mind is bold—have made the earth a measure of your might; encompassing the waters and the sun, you go unto heaven for our protection.
You have become the counterpart of the earth; you have become the lord of the lofty, vast one whose heroes are exalted.
You have filled the entire mid-air with your greatness. Truly, indeed, there is none other like you.
Neither heaven and earth, nor the rivers have reached the limit of his expanse, nor the end of the mid-world;
nor even his own rain when he fights in its exhilaration—for alone you have brought all else into being in due order.
The Maruts sang their hymns here in this very battle; all the gods rejoiced after you when you, O Indra, struck down the breath of Vṛtra with your sharp-edged weapon.
We bring forth this speech as an offering to the Great One; we offer songs to Indra at the dwelling-place of Vivasvat.
For never indeed have they found wealth like those who sleep; a poor hymn of praise is not recited among the givers of riches.
Thou art the opener of the stall for horses, O Indra, the opener of the stall for cattle, the opener of the stall for barley; thou art the powerful lord of wealth.
Thou who aidest men from of old, who art never wearied by lack of desire, a friend to thy friends—for him we sing this praise.
O powerful Indra, doer of many deeds, most resplendent one, this wealth all around you is known to be yours alone.
Therefore, as a conqueror, gather from there and bring it hither; do not frustrate the desire of the singer who seeks you.
With these days, with these drops, being well-disposed, driving away want with cattle and horses;
with Indra and his drops, may we shatter the Dasyu and, freed from hatred, may we obtain nourishment.
O Indra, may we obtain wealth; may we obtain nourishment; may we obtain spoils that are many-glittering and celestial.
May we obtain divine providence, which is full of heroic vigor, preeminent in cattle, and rich in horses.
Those exhilarations gladdened you, those manly powers, O Lord of the Good, those Soma-draughts in the slayings of Vṛtra—
when for the singer who had spread the sacred grass, you, irresistible, struck down ten thousand Vṛtras.
Battle after battle you indeed go forth with boldness; you destroy stronghold after stronghold with your might.
When, O Indra, through your friendship, you struck down the guileful one named Namuci in the distance by means of your bow.
You slew Karañja and Parṇaya with the most piercing path of Atithigva;
you shattered the hundred forts of Vaṅgr̥da, which were besieged by R̥jiśvan, O irresistible one.

O you who are renowned, with your chariot wheel, you struck down the sixty thousand and ninety-nine men of Janarāja, who had approached with his kinsman Suśravas— the twice-ten— making them difficult to tread upon.
You protected Suśravas with your aids, and with your protections, O Indra, you helped Tūrvayāṇa.
You made Kutsa, Atithigva, and Āyu subject to this great, youthful king.
O Indra, may we be your most auspicious friends at the end of the day, protected by the gods;
through you we shall offer praise, possessing heroic sons and extending our lifespan further into the distance.
O Maghavan, do not abandon us in this distress amidst these battles, for the limit of your power cannot be encompassed.
You made the rivers roar and the forests cry out; how did the two worlds not recoil in fear?
Worship the powerful Śakra, the possessor of might; magnifying him, praise Indra who hears you—he, the bull, who by his bold strength and virility subdues both heaven and earth.
Sing forth a powerful hymn to the lofty Heaven, whose bold spirit possesses its own sovereign might.
The Asura of great renown was made manifest by his own strength; for he is a bull, a chariot drawn by two bay steeds, who stands before us.
You made the ridge of the vast heaven tremble; with your own bold self, you shattered Śambara.
When, O bold one, you—intoxicated by the exhilarating drink—assailed the wielder of magic, the destroyer, with your sharp-edged bolt, the thunderbolt in your hand.
When you strike down at the head of the snorting one, making even the wounded Śuṣṇa’s woods roar,
with a forward-striving and mighty mind— whatever you shall do even today, who can restrain you?
You protected Narya Turvaśa and Yadu; you, O Śatakratu, protected Turvīti and Vayya.
You protected the chariot and Etaśa in the decisive contest for wealth; you destroyed ninety-nine fortresses.
He indeed, the king, the lord of the virtuous, has grown mighty as a man to whom oblations are offered—he who fulfills the command.
Or he who welcomes our hymns with bounty; for him, the giver, the lower regions of heaven overflow.

Unequaled is their dominion, unequaled their wisdom; may these Soma-drinkers excel through their skillful deeds—those who, O Indra, increase your great dominion, your enduring strength, and your virile power as they bestow gifts upon you.

For you alone are these abundant juices, pressed by stones, resting in the vessels, the cups for Indra’s drinking. Pervade them, satisfy your desire for them, and then direct your mind toward the bestowing of wealth.
The mountain stood within Vṛtra’s bellies, a darkness that obstructed the support of the waters.
Indra struck down all those rivers held back by the obstructor as they flowed along their downward courses.
May he bestow upon us glorious splendor that increases our welfare; O Indra, subduer of men, grant us great and powerful dominion.
Protect our patrons and guard our wise leaders; establish us in wealth, in noble offspring, and in nourishment.
Even the expanse of heaven has spread itself wide before him; even the earth does not equal Indra in greatness.
Terrible and mighty, a scorcher for the sake of the people, he sharpens his thunderbolt for brilliance like a bull.
Like the ocean receiving the rivers from the sea with its wide expanses, Indra, the bull, longs for the drinking of Soma; from of old, he, the warrior, is praised for his might.
O Indra, you rule over that mountain-like mass for our enjoyment; you ordain the laws of great manly power.
He is distinguished among the gods by his heroic might; as the fierce one, he is placed at the forefront for every deed.
He indeed is celebrated among the people with reverent words in the forest, proclaiming his lovely Indra-power;
he becomes a desirable bull, a yearning bull, when the Bountiful One (Maghavan) impels the cow with security.
He, the warrior, by his might and by his strength, brings about great battles for the sake of men;
yet even then, they do not believe in the one possessed of brilliance, Indra, as he repeatedly hurls the thunderbolt, his weapon of death.
For he, seeking glory, increasing upon the earth with his might, destroys the man-made dwellings;
creating lights secure for the sacrificer, the one of noble intellect has released the waters to flow.
O drinker of Soma, let your mind be set upon giving; turn hither your two bay steeds, O you who hear our praise.
Those charioteers of yours, O Indra, who are most eager to sacrifice—those restless intentions of yours do not deceive you.

You carry in your hands wealth that is unasked for; you, the renowned one, have placed invincible power within your body. Like wells surrounded by those who dig them, O Indra, many thoughts dwell within your person.

He has lifted up these many ladles for him, as a steed raises its hooves toward a maiden; the active one makes himself drink skill for the great [sacrifice], having turned his golden chariot yoked with bay horses, the work of the *Ṛbhus*.
To him the songs of praise have gone forth, seeking abundance like those eager for gain upon the ocean's path;
they have ascended with splendor, like longing gazes upon a mountain, to the Lord of skill and the power of the assembly.
Victorious and great in manly power, he shines with impetuous might like the peak of a mountain;
by him, in the exhilaration of the soma, the iron-strong one brought down the guileful Śuṣṇa into the snare and bound him fast among the obstacles.

If the divine power (*taviṣī*) has increased thee for aid, it follows after Indra as the sun follows the dawn—he who with bold strength drives away the darkness; unrestrained in his roar, he raises up the dust on high.
When, by your might, you established the unshakable firmament across the expanse of the sky;
when, O Indra, in the exhilaration of the *svarmīḷha* draught, you joyfully struck Vṛtra and released the flood of waters.
By your might, O Indra, you established the support of heaven and the earth in their seats; you, the majestic one.
In the exhilaration of the pressed soma, you released the waters and shattered the boulders of Vṛtra along his entire length.
I bring a hymn to the most generous, the lofty one of vast wealth, whose strength is true and who is powerful—
to him whose bounty is irresistible like water on a slope, which is opened for all life and for his might.
Then let all follow after your sacrifice; like waters flowing downward, let the libations of the one who offers oblations reach you.
When Indra’s beloved, golden, shattering thunderbolt settles upon the mountain, it is as if it has been sharpened.
To this formidable one, bring with homage at the sacrifice, like the radiant Dawn, that which is most worthy of praise;
for him whose domain and name, his Indra-power and light, have been fashioned for glory, so that he may be led forth like a bay horse.
O Indra, praised by many, we here are yours—those who move about having taken hold of you, O Lord of abundant wealth.
For none other than you, O lover of songs, can sustain our hymns; accept this speech of ours as you would the people.
Abundant is your heroic power, O Indra; we belong to you. O Maghavan, fulfill the desire of this singer.
The vast sky yields to your heroic might, and this earth, too, bows before your strength.
O Indra, wielder of the thunderbolt, you shattered that great and wide mountain into pieces with your bolt;
you released the obstructed waters so they might flow, and you have truly possessed all conquering power as your own alone.
Never indeed does the immortal one, born of strength, shrink away, since he has become the Hotṛ-priest and the messenger of Vivasvat;
through the most effective paths he traverses the mid-air, and at the assembly of the gods, he seeks to win [the gods] with the oblation.
Preparing his own food, undecaying, and eager for the dry wood, he stands among the brushwood;
like a horse, his back shines with the moisture of the sprinkled offering; thundering like the ridge of heaven, he has roared.
Active with the Rudras and Vasus, the immortal Hotṛ priest seated in front, a winner of wealth,
like a chariot moving swiftly among the people, the god bestows desirable boons one after another upon the living.
Urged by the wind, he spreads through the dry brushwood at will with his tongues and his scythe, roaring loudly.
When you, O Agni, like a bull, thirstily desire the trees, this path of yours is black, O you of radiant waves, undecaying one.
With glowing jaws, driven by the wind like a bull among the herd, he blows down upon the forest;
advancing with his brilliance toward the inexhaustible space, everything that stands or moves, even the winged birds, trembles in fear.
The Bhr̥gus established you among men, like a lovely treasure, easy to invoke for the people—
the Hotr̥, O Agni, the most excellent guest, as dear as a friend to the divine race.

The Hotṛ, the most skilled sacrificer whom the priests choose at the rites—he who has seven tongues—Agni, the steward of all treasures, I serve with an offering; I approach him for the sake of wealth.
O Son of Strength, O Agni of friend-like majesty, grant today unbroken protection to us who praise you; O Son of Might, deliver the singer from distress with your iron fortresses.
O Radiant One, be a shelter for the singer; O Maghavan, be a protection for the liberal patrons.
O Agni, deliver the singer from distress. May he who is enriched by prayer come quickly in the morning.
O Agni, these other fires are indeed thy branches; in thee all the immortals rejoice.
O Vaiśvānara, thou art the navel of the settlements; like a pillar, thou supportest the people.
Agni is the head of heaven, the navel of the earth; he has become the messenger between the two worlds.
As such, the gods generated you as a god, O Vaiśvānara, as light for the Ārya.

As the rays are fixed in the sun, so have treasures been placed in Agni Vaiśvānara—those which are in the mountains, in the plants, in the waters, and those which are among men; of all that, you are the king.
Like the two great worlds for their son, the human Hotṛ-priest, skillful as Manu, offers many songs—
youthful and most manly— to Vaiśvānara, the possessor of light and true strength.
Even from the great heaven, O Jātavedas Vaiśvānara, thy majesty has exceeded all bounds.
Thou art the king of the human tribes; through battle, thou hast created wide space for the gods.
Now I shall proclaim the greatness of the Bull, whom the Pūrus attend as the slayer of Vṛtra.
Agni Vaiśvānara, having struck down the Dasyu, shook the barriers and shattered Śambara.
Vaiśvānara, who belongs to all people by his greatness, the worshipful and radiant one among the Bharadvājas—
Agni, rich in true blessings, is celebrated with hundreds of songs by Puruṇītha, the son of Śatavani.

Mātariśvan brought to Bhr̥gu a gift worthy of praise— like wealth itself— the carrier of oblations, the glorious banner of the assembly, the excellent messenger who swiftly accomplishes his purpose, the twice-born one.
Both kinds of mortals attend upon his teaching: those who offer oblations and the yearning seekers.
Even before the dawn, the Hotṛ has sat down among the people—the venerable lord of the clans, the wise ordainer.
May our newest hymn of praise reach him who is being born from the heart, he whose tongue is honeyed;
him whom the human priests, the Āyus, providing sacrificial food, have brought forth in the assembly.
Desiring [the gods], purifying, a Vasu among men, the most excellent Hotṛ has been established among the clans;
as the domestic friend and master of the house within the home, Agni has become the lord of riches among riches.
O Agni, we the Gotamas praise you with our hymns as the lord of riches, polishing you like a swift horse that brings the prize. May he who is enriched by prayer come quickly in the morning.

To him, the truly powerful and swift one, I offer this hymn of praise like a refreshing draught—to the majestic Indra, who is worthy of the song, the irresistible one; I present these most excellent prayers.

To him indeed I offer this praise like a gift; I bring forth a hymn of laudation with skillful turning. For Indra, the ancient lord, they have purified their thoughts with heart, mind, and inspired wisdom.
To him indeed I bring this highest praise with my mouth,
he who wins the light of heaven— the most generous patron— to be magnified by my words of thought and well-fashioned hymns.
For him indeed I fashion this hymn of praise, as a carpenter fashions a chariot for its owner;
and I offer these well-formed songs to Indra, the bearer of songs, the one who moves all things, the wise one.
For this Indra, I adorn with my ladle a hymn of praise, like a swift steed, to win glory—
to honor the hero who dwells in the gift, whose fame is celebrated, and who is the destroyer of forts.
For him indeed Tvaṣṭṛ fashioned the thunderbolt, most skillfully wrought and resounding for the battle;
with it, the Lord, increasing his power, smiting Vṛtra, pierced his vital spot—how great was his might!

At the libations of his mother, he has immediately drunk the great draught; having consumed the savory foods, the mighty Viṣṇu, the conqueror, stole the cooked meal. Shooting beyond the rock, he pierced the boar.
For him, for Indra, even the divine dames, the wives of the gods, wove a hymn upon the slaying of the dragon.
He has encompassed both the wide heaven and earth; they have not reached the limit of his greatness.
His greatness indeed exceeds that of heaven, earth, and the intermediate space.
Indra, the self-ruling lord praised by all, the celestial one, the vessel of strength, has grown mighty for the battle within his own home.
By his very might, Indra shattered Vṛtra who was swelling with strength with his thunderbolt;
like cows released from their pen, he set free the flowing waters, being intent on bestowing glory.
At his fierce impetus the rivers ran, when he hemmed them in on all sides with the thunderbolt.
Acting as a lord, bestowing gifts upon the worshipper, the victorious one made a ford for Turvīti.

For him indeed, Vṛtra, bring forth the thunderbolt with haste, O Lord of manifold power! Split his joints asunder like those of an ox, piercing through them so that he may let loose the floods of water to flow.
Proclaim with new hymns the ancient deeds of this impetuous one,
when, brandishing his weapons for battle, he, roaring in his wrath, overcomes his enemies.
Out of fear of him, even the firm mountains and heaven and earth tremble at his birth;
when he repeatedly urged on the dwelling of the longing one, Nodhas immediately became capable of heroic deeds.
To him indeed was granted that [booty] of theirs, which he alone won as the lord of abundance;
Indra aided Pr̥itaśa, who contended with Sūrya, the presser of Soma at the sacrifice for the sake of the son of Suvāśva.

Thus have the Gotamas fashioned these well-crafted prayers for you, O Indra, for your yoking of the bay steeds. Bestow upon them a thought adorned with every beauty; may he who is enriched by prayer come swiftly in the morning.

We meditate upon a strengthening hymn of praise for the mighty one who loves songs, as did Aṅgiras; with well-fashioned verses let us sing a song of worship to the one worthy of praise, the renowned hero.

Bring forth great homage for the Great One; offer a song of praise, a *sāman*, to the powerful one—by means of which our ancient fathers, the Aṅgirases, who knew the tracks, found the cows while singing their hymns.
At the impulse of Indra and the Aṅgirases, Saramā found nourishment for her offspring;
Bṛhaspati split the mountain and found the cows; the men lowed together with the ruddy kine.

With the *suṣṭubh* and *stobha* chants, with the seven seers, and with the resonant voice of the Navagvas, O Indra, you who roar; with the Saraṇyus and the Daśagvas, O Śakra, you shattered the mountain Phaliga and Vala with your thunder.
Praised by the Aṅgirases, O wondrous one, you opened up the darkness with the dawn, with the sun, and with the rays of light.
You spread out the ridges of the earth, O Indra, and you propped up the intermediate region of heaven.
That deed of his, the wonder-worker, is most manifest and most beautiful; it is a wondrous work when, at the secret place, he caused the four rivers with honeyed waters to swell from the heights.
Twofold he has disclosed the two ancient, co-nested [worlds], O tireless one, through the hymns of praise;
like Bhaga, the one of wondrous deeds has supported the two worlds, heaven and earth, in the highest firmament.

From of old, from heaven and from earth, the two young women of different forms, ever-renewed, move one after the other according to their own laws: Night with her dark limbs, Dawn with her radiant bodies.

Seeking to perform noble works, the Son of Wonderous Deeds has established a friendship that endures to the end; by his might, he has placed the ripe milk within the raw cows—white milk within the black and the ruddy ones.
From of old, the sisters dwelling in the same nest, the unaging and immortal ones, protect the laws with their powers;
like wives, many thousands of them serve the one who is free from shame.
Seeking your aid, O Wonder-worker, our newest thoughts, seeking wealth, have sped forth with obeisance and hymns;
like longing wives touching their yearning husband, these inspired thoughts touch you, O Lord of Might.
From of old, O Wondrous One, the riches in your hand have neither diminished nor failed;
you are brilliant, wise, and full of power, O Indra—grant us your aid with your mighty powers.
For him who seeks the ancient, Gotama has fashioned a new prayer for Indra, for the yoking of the bay horses. O powerful one, may Nodhas, rich in vision, come quickly to us at dawn with his guidance.
O Indra, you are great, you who at your birth established heaven and earth with your might;
when all the mountains, even those firm and vast, trembled in fear before you like dust before the wind.
When you, O Indra, drive hither your two bay steeds of different courses, your singer places the thunderbolt in your arms—
that weapon by which, O Lord of unassailable will, you, being much-invoked, shatter the many fortresses of our enemies.
O Indra, you are the true one, the bold; you are Ṛbhukṣan, the friend of men, the subduer. You slew Śuṣṇa in the fray for the sake of food, at the impulse of the youthful and radiant Kutsa.
O Indra, you indeed then urged on that [Vṛtra] as a friend; when you, O wielder of the thunderbolt, O performer of manly deeds, struck Vṛtra down.
When, O hero of virile mind, you, the effortless conqueror, scattered the Dasyus far away from their dwelling place.
O Indra, you indeed were there when, seeking to harm, you struck down even the firm [fortress] of mortals in their displeasure.
Drive away from us the barriers for our steed; O wielder of the thunderbolt, crush the enemies like [crumbling] banks.
O Indra, in that contest for waters and for the light of heaven, men call upon you in the battle.
O self-dependent one, may this aid of yours be brought swiftly to us in the assembly and in the contests for booty.
O Indra, wielder of the thunderbolt, you indeed shattered those seven fortresses for Purukutsa while fighting;
just as you effortlessly spread the sacrificial grass for Sudās, O King, you created wide space for Pūru out of distress.

O Indra, O God, you have made that wondrous nourishment swell for us, like waters flowing all around, by which, O Hero, you may grant us back our own self, so that it may flow forth at all times like vital strength.
O Indra, these prayers have been fashioned for you by the Gotamas; they have been spoken with reverence for your two bay steeds.
Bring us well-adorned booty; may he who is enriched by prayer come quickly in the morning.
O Nodhas, bring forth a well-fashioned hymn to the bull-like host, the most bountiful and wise Maruts;
like a skillful craftsman with a steady hand, I, the sage, adorn my songs in my mind for those who are present at the assemblies.

They were born from heaven, the lofty bulls, the youths of Rudra, the Asuras free from blemish; they are purifying and bright like suns, like warriors with glittering drops of sweat, terrible in form.
The youthful Rudras, ageless destroyers of those who do not give, have grown irresistible like mountains;
by their might, they cause even all firm earthly and celestial beings to tremble.
With brilliant ointments they anoint themselves for beauty; they have fastened golden ornaments upon their chests for splendor.
Upon their shoulders the spears rest firmly; these heroes were born together by their own inherent power from heaven.
The shakers, destroyers of enemies, acting as lords, have created the winds and lightnings by their powers;
the shakers milk the celestial udders, and wandering all around, they swell the earth with milk.
The Maruts, the bounteous givers, swell the waters; present at the sacrifices, they provide milk mixed with ghee.
Like a swift steed for rain, they lead forth the prize-winner; they milk the thundering, inexhaustible spring.
Like mighty buffaloes, wondrously radiant, like mountains self-strong and swift-gliding;
like wild elephants you devour the forests when you have yoked your powers among the ruddy dawns.
Like lions they roar, the wise ones; like boars, well-furred, they possess all-knowledge.
Enlivening the nights with their spotted deer and spears, they come together, pressing one another with their might, full of serpent-like fury.
Address the two worlds, O you who possess the splendor of a host; you heroes who seek men, impetuous in your might like serpents.
Like a brilliant vision upon a chariot-seat, like lightning, your splendor has taken its place upon your chariots, O Maruts.
O all-knowing ones, dwelling together with riches, united with powers and overflowing with strength,
these heroes— whose mouths are like bulls and whose vigor is infinite— have taken up their arrows in their hands as archers.
With their golden fellies, increasing the waters, they strike up the mountains like rushing streams;
the vigorous, tireless Maruts, self-moving, shaking the firm, performing fierce deeds, with glittering spears.
We praise with our invocation the impetuous, purifying, forest-ruling, all-beholding son of Rudra;
follow for the sake of glory the host of Maruts, who traverse the mid-air, who are powerful, who possess the Soma dregs, and who are virile.
That mortal indeed surpasses all people in strength through your aid, O Maruts, whom you have protected.
With his horses he wins booty, with his men he gains wealth; he dwells in a praiseworthy wisdom and prospers.

O Maruts, bestow upon our patrons a praiseworthy, invincible, and radiant strength; grant us wealth-seeking, hymn-worthy, and all-people-encompassing offspring. May we nourish our children and grandchildren for a hundred winters.

Now, O Maruts, bestow upon us enduring wealth, accompanied by heroes, which overcomes the onset of enemies—a thousandfold, hundredfold, and ever-increasing. May he who is enriched by prayer come quickly in the morning.
Like a thief lurking in a cave, he who yokes himself with homage and carries it away.
In unison, the wise ones have followed your footsteps; all the worshipful gods have sat down near you.
The gods follow the ordinances of *ṛta*; let there be a surrounding protection like that of heaven over the earth.
The waters have magnified him with praise—the well-formed infant, well-born in the womb, the source of the Eternal Order.
Like nourishment, he is delightful; like a broad dwelling, he is expansive; like a mountain, he is a source of enjoyment; like water, he is a bringer of bliss.
Like a steed urged forward in the race, like the flood of a river— who can restrain him?
The kinsman of the rivers, like a brother among his sisters, he devours the forests like a king [devouring] the rich.
Or when, impelled by the wind, Agni has spread through the forests, he indeed shears the hair of the earth.
He breathes within the waters like a swan resting; most wise in his purpose, he awakens at dawn for the sake of the people.
Like Soma, he is a wise ordainer born of Truth; like a young animal, he is pervasive and far-reaching.
Like wondrous wealth, like the sun to behold, like life-breath, like a son who is one's own.
Like a swift, restless beast he hastens toward the woods; pure and radiant, he is like a cow yielding milk.
He maintains security, like a pleasant home; he is like ripened barley, the conqueror of men.
Like a praising seer among the people, like a well-pleased steed, he bestows vitality.
With a flame difficult to approach, like the eternal will, he is sufficient for everyone, like a wife in her home.
When he has shone forth, variegated like a white horse among the people, brilliant like a golden chariot in battles.
Like an army let loose, he bestows vigor; like the missile of an archer, he has a brilliant appearance.
Yama was born first; Yama is the progeny of birth; he is the lover of maidens and the husband of wives.
May we reach him with our service, as cows reach their home at evening when he has been kindled.
Like the flood of the Sindhu, they have rushed downward; the cows have lowed at the sight of the sun.
Born in the forests, a friend among mortals, he chooses obedience like an undecaying king.
May he be a secure protector, a virtuous plan, and auspicious; may he be a self-reliant invoker and a bearer of oblations.
Holding all manly powers in his hand, the Unassailable One placed the gods within the secret cave while dwelling therein.
There, the men who conceive inspired thought find her, as they recite the hymns fashioned in their hearts.
Like an unborn one, he has supported the earth and propped up the sky with true mantras.
O Agni, guard the dear tracks of the cattle; as the life of all, go from hiding place to hiding place.
He who has perceived him dwelling in the secret cave, he who has sat down at the stream of the Eternal Order (Ṛta).
Those who, honoring the cosmic order (*ṛta*), perform their work, for them indeed he has proclaimed riches.
He who by his greatness has established himself within the plants, and within offspring and the wombs of those about to give birth.
The wise ones, possessing all life, have fashioned him within the dwelling of the waters like a seat, as if through inspired thought.
Blending [the oblations], the swift one has approached heaven; he has uncovered the nights for all that stands and moves.
When he alone, as a god among all the gods, encompassed them with his greatness.
Then indeed all [the gods] took pleasure in your wisdom, O God, when you were born alive from the dry wood.
All partake in the name of divinity, honoring the eternal Law (ṛta) with their courses toward immortality.
The impulse of Truth, the thought of Truth—All-living, all have performed their works.
To him who offers to you, or who would strive for you, do you, being wise, grant wealth.
The Hotṛ, seated among the offspring of Manu, he indeed is the lord of these riches.
Desiring seed within their bodies, they have come together in mutual accord; undeluded, they have united through their own innate powers.
Like sons [delighting] in their father's will, they have taken pleasure in his rite—those swift ones who listen to his command.
The possessor of much food has thrown open the doors of wealth; the friend of the house has adorned the firmament with stars.
Bright and shining like the lover of the Dawn, he has filled the two joined worlds like the light of heaven.
Once born, you have encompassed all through your wisdom; though being their son, you have become the father of the gods.
Agni, the wise and undaunted one, discerning like the udder of cows, is the sweetness of nourishments.
Like a kinsman dear to the people, worthy of invocation, he sits in the midst, delightful within the dwelling.
Like a son born in the home, delightful; like a prize-winning steed, well-pleased, he has crossed over the people.
When I call upon the clans together with the heroes from their common dwelling, may Agni attain all divine powers through his godhead.
No one violates these laws of yours, since you have granted obedience to these men.
That indeed is your wondrous deed, that you struck down [the foe] together with your peers; joined by the men, you rent asunder the demonic powers.
Like the lover of the Dawn, the radiant one, whose form is well-known, may he take notice of this man.
Carrying themselves by their own power, they opened wide the doors; they all shouted aloud at the sight of the sun.
May we win many thoughts of the noble one; may Agni, shining beautifully, attain all things.
He who is wise has taken note of the divine ordinances and of the birth of the human race.
He who is the embryo of the waters, the embryo of the forests, the embryo of all that stands, and the embryo of all that moves.
Even within the rock, in his dwelling, he is like the immortal one among the people, well-disposed.
For he, Agni, is the lord of wealth for the one who serves him well with hymns throughout the night.
O wise one, protect these beings; you who know them, guard the generations of the gods and mortals alike.
May the many nights of diverse forms increase him, the chariot that stands firm and is impelled by the *ṛta*.
The Hotṛ has been successfully established, seated in the light, performing all true deeds.
You bestow renown upon the cattle and the forests; may all bring us tribute to the light of heaven.
Men have worshipped you in many places; they bring forth your treasures as one brings the possessions of a living father.
Like a skillful man, he is not greedy; like a hero with a sword, like a charioteer, he is formidable and fierce in battles.

The longing sisters, dwelling in the same nest, have stirred him who longs for them, as wives do for their own husband; they have delighted in the dark and the ruddy [dawns], as cows delight in the brightly shining Dawn.
Even the firm and solid [fortress], our fathers, the Aṅgirases, shattered with their hymns and with a roar;
they made for us a path to the lofty heaven, and they found the day, the light, and the banner of the dawn.
Establishing the cosmic order (*ṛta*) and setting his inspired thought in motion, the noble ones, though widely scattered, now desire to win him over;
unthirsting and active, they go toward the gods, strengthening the divine race with sacrificial food.
When Mātariśvan, being borne along, churned him forth, he became the bright, noble one in every house;
then, like a companion to a more powerful king, the descendant of Bhr̥gu undertook his office as messenger.

When he prepared that juice for his great father Dyaus, the wise one stealthily approached the Pṛśanī. The archer boldly discharged the missile at him; the god cast his brilliance upon his own daughter.

He who, in his own home, shines for you, or offers homage day after day to you who desire it—O Agni, increase his vital strength twofold; may he whom you urge on reach his goal with wealth in a single chariot.
All nourishments attend upon Agni, as the seven mighty rivers flow toward the ocean.
Our strength is not distinguished by its kinsmen; may he, the wise one, find favor among the gods for us.
When the brilliance reached the lord of men for nourishment, the pure seed was poured down from heaven in the encounter;
Agni brought forth and perfected the blameless, youthful host, making them well-disposed.
He who, like thought, traverses the paths instantly, alone, the hero who rules over all wealth;
the two kings Mitra and Varuṇa, with beautiful hands, who guard the beloved nectar among the cattle.
O Agni, as a wise seer, do not neglect our ancestral friendships, you who are possessed of knowledge.
Old age impairs the form like a cloud; before that curse reaches us, take heed.
Holding in his hand many manly poetic insights, Agni, the ordainer, has performed these for all eternity; he has become the lord of riches, bestowing all immortal powers upon us.
The all-wise immortals, though seeking him, did not find the calf hidden within us;
wearying themselves, following his tracks and intent on the prayer, they stood at the supreme, beautiful station of Agni.
When, O Agni, the pure ones worshipped you, the pure one, with clarified butter for three autumns,
they assumed names worthy of sacrifice and perfected their bodies, being well-born.
Making themselves known throughout the two great worlds, the worshipful sons of Rudra have come forth.
The mortal, discerning in the distribution of the sacrificial portions, has found Agni stationed in the highest place.
Acting in unison, they sat down on their knees; accompanied by their wives, they paid homage to the one worthy of homage.
Having cast off [their former] bodies, they fashioned for themselves new forms, as friends guarding the blink of an eye for their friend.
When the worshipful ones discovered the thrice-seven secret steps deposited within you, they guard the immortality with them in harmony; protect the cattle and all that is stationary and moving.

O Agni, you who know the ways of the peoples, bestow nourishments in due order for the sake of life. Knowing the paths traveled by the gods within, you have become the tireless messenger, the bearer of the oblation.
The wise ones, knowing the cosmic order (*ṛta*), opened wide the doors of wealth—the seven mighty rivers from heaven.
Saramā found the firm enclosure of cattle, by which the human race now prospers.
Those who have established all noble offspring, making for themselves a path toward immortality—
by their greatness, the great Aditi, the mother, has spread out the earth with her sons, so that she may nourish the bird.
The immortals established beautiful splendor upon him when they fashioned the two eyes of heaven.
Then, like rivers released, the red ones flowed downward; O Agni, they recognized them as they went forth.
Like wealth inherited from his father, he bestows vital strength; like the instruction of one who knows, he is a wise guide.
Like a guest resting in comfort, he is gratifying; like a Hotṛ priest, he has overspread the dwelling of the worshiper.
Like the god Savitṛ, whose thoughts are true, he protects all strongholds by his wisdom;
much-praised, true like the immortal spirit, he has become dear as one's own self, worthy of being cherished.

Like a god who sustains the entire earth, he dwells as one whose friends are well-disposed, like a king; like heroes seated in the citadel for protection, he is blameless, like a woman beloved by her husband.
O Agni, men have attended upon you, ever-kindled in their homes within secure dwellings.
They have bestowed abundant splendor upon you; be the sustainer of all life and the foundation of riches.
O Agni, may the liberal patrons obtain nourishment; may the wise givers attain a full span of life.
May we win booty in the battles of the enemy, establishing our portion among the gods for the sake of glory.
For the milch-cows of Truth, lowing and bestowed by Heaven, have swelled with full udders;
seeking favor from afar, the rivers have flowed forth across the rock.
Seeking thy favor, O Agni, the worshipful ones have established glory in heaven;
they have made Night and Dawn of different forms, and have joined together the dark color and the ruddy.
O Agni, may we and our patrons be those mortals whom you lead to wealth;
like a shadow, you accompany the entire world, having filled the two worlds and the intermediate space.
O Agni, aided by thee, may we overcome steeds with steeds, men with men, and heroes with heroes;
being masters of wealth inherited from our fathers, may our wise patrons attain a hundred winters.
O Agni, O Ordainer, may these hymns of praise be pleasing to your mind and heart.
May we be able to control the well-yoked riches you bestow, while maintaining the glory allotted by the gods.
Approaching the sacrifice, let us address a prayer to Agni,
who hears us even from afar.
He who, being the foremost, protected the household of the donor when the peoples were gathered together in their longings.
And let the people say: "Agni has been born as a slayer of Vṛtra, a winner of wealth in every battle."
In whose house you are the messenger, and to whose oblations you go for enjoyment,
there you perform the wondrous sacrifice.
Him indeed, O Aṅgiras, the people call one to whom oblations are well offered, a possessor of good gods, O son of strength, and one who has excellent sacrificial grass.
And bring those gods here for our praise,
O bright-shining one, so that they may enjoy the oblations.
No sound of a horse is ever heard, nor any rattling of a chariot,
when you, O Agni, go on your mission as a messenger.
Favored by you, O Agni, the modest steed, urged on from behind, has surpassed the one before; the worshipper has risen up.
And, O divine Agni, you win for the worshipper great splendor and abundant heroic strength from the gods.
Accept this most expansive word, most delightful to the gods,
as you offer the oblations into your mouth.
Now, O Agni, best of the Aṅgirases and most skilled in rites, may we speak to you a beloved prayer that brings gain.
Who among men is your kinsman, O Agni? Who is the one who offers the sacrifice?
Who indeed are you, and upon whom do you rest?
O Agni, you are the kinsman of men; you are their dear friend; as a comrade, you are to be praised by your companions.
Sacrifice for us to Mitra and Varuṇa; sacrifice to the gods and to the lofty *ṛta*.
O Agni, worship in your own abode.

What approach is there for the favor of your mind, O Agni? What inspired thought might become most peaceful for you? Or who has attained your skill through sacrifices? With what mind, indeed, shall we worship you?
Come here, O Agni; sit down as our Hotṛ-priest, undeceived and be our excellent leader.
May Heaven and Earth, who pervade all things, protect you. Sacrifice to the gods for our great goodwill.
O Agni, burn up all the Rākṣasas; become the protector of our sacrifices against curses.
Then, bring the Lord of Soma with his two bay horses; we have prepared hospitality for this most bountiful one.
With offspring-providing speech and with my mouth, I call upon you as the bearer; sit down here together with the gods.
Perform the office of the *hotṛ* and the *potṛ*, O worshipful one; be the giver and the progenitor of riches.
Just as you, O sage, being yourself a seer, sacrificed to the gods with the oblations of the wise Manu,
even so, O most truthful Hotṛ, Agni, sacrifice today with your joyous ladle.

How may we offer worship to Agni? What song, beloved by the gods, is recited for him, the radiant one—who, being immortal among mortals, the observer of *ṛta*, the most excellent invoker, brings the gods here?
Him who is most peaceful at the sacrifices, the upholder of *ṛta*, the Hotṛ—bring him hither with salutations!
For when Agni goes to the gods for the sake of mortals, he shall perceive them with his mind and perform the sacrifice.
For he is the will, he is the hero, he is the perfect one; like Mitra, he has become the charioteer of the wondrous.
Him, the wondrous one, the Aryan clans, seeking the gods, address first at the sacrifices.

May that Agni, the most heroic among men, the destroyer of enemies, accept our songs, our prayer, and our protection. And may those most powerful patrons, impelled by strength, further this thought through their enduring bounty.
Thus has Agni, the follower of Truth, Jātavedas, been praised by the inspired Gotamas.
May he increase their splendor among them; may he grant them strength, and being wise, he comes to them with nourishment according to his pleasure.
O Jātavedas, you who are far-seeing, we the Gotamas exalt you with our song; we celebrate you aloud with splendors.
Desirous of wealth, Gotama honors you with his song; we praise you aloud with splendors.
We invoke you, the greatest winner of booty, like Aṅgiras;
we celebrate you aloud with splendors.
And thee, O best slayer of Vṛtra, who hast shaken off the Dasyus—
we praise thee aloud with splendors.
We of the Rahūgaṇa clan have spoken a honeyed word to Agni;
with splendors we celebrate him aloud.
Golden-haired in the expanse of the mid-air, he is like a roaring serpent, impetuous as the wind;
resplendent and pure, he is the witness of the dawns, who are glorious, active, and true.
Your well-winged birds have sped along their courses; the black bull has bellowed when this [world] was here. He has come with the auspicious, smiling [waters]; the mists fall and the clouds thunder.
When Aryaman, Mitra, and Varuṇa, the wanderer, being beloved by the milk of *ṛta*, lead it along the straightest paths of *ṛta*, they moisten the skin in the womb of the lower region.
O Agni, lord of wealth consisting of cattle, O young son of strength,
bestow upon us, O Jātavedas, great renown.
Being kindled, the wise Agni, worthy of praise with our song,
O you of many aspects, shine forth wealth upon us.
O King Agni, by night and by yourself, and at the breaking of dawn,
O you with sharp teeth, burn against the Rākṣasas.
O Agni, worthy of praise in all our prayers, protect us with your aids during the recitation of the Gāyatra hymn.
O Agni, bring to us wealth that is all-conquering, most excellent,
and invincible in all battles.
O Agni, with your gracious favor, bestow upon us wealth that nourishes all our life, and grant us mercy so that we may live.
O Gotama, desiring his favor, bring forward these purified words and songs for Agni, whose flame is sharp.
O Agni, may he who seeks to harm us, whether near or far, fall down;
do thou bring about our prosperity alone.
The thousand-eyed Agni, who observes all people, drives away the demons;
he is the praiseworthy Hotṛ priest who is celebrated in hymns.
For thus, in the exhilaration of Soma, the priest has fashioned a strengthening hymn for you;
O most powerful wielder of the thunderbolt, by your might you have driven the serpent from the earth, praising your own sovereign rule.
That bull-like exhilarating Soma, pressed and brought by the falcon, has intoxicated you— that [Soma] by which,
O wielder of the thunderbolt, you struck Vṛtra down from the waters with your might, while singing in accordance with your own sovereignty.
Go forth! Advance! Be bold! Your thunderbolt shall not be held back.
O Indra, for manly is your power; slay Vṛtra, win the waters, and sing in praise of your own sovereignty.
O Indra, from the earth you struck down Vṛtra, and from heaven;
release these life-sustaining waters accompanied by the Maruts. Singing praises, follow after your own sovereign rule.
Indra, incensed, having advanced with his thunderbolt against the ridge of the surging Vṛtra,
strikes him down, impelling the waters to flow, while singing in accordance with his own sovereign rule.
He strikes down upon the summit with his hundred-jointed thunderbolt;
exhilarated by the soma-juice, Indra seeks a path for his friends, praising his own sovereign rule.
O Indra, wielder of the thunderbolt, lord of the pressing-stones, yours alone is that irresistible heroic power.
For you, by means of your own creative power, slew that wily beast; thus they sang in praise of your self-sovereignty.
Your thunderbolts have been launched along the ninety navigable rivers.
O Indra, great is your heroic power; strength has been placed within your arms. Singing praises, we acknowledge your sovereign dominion.
Sing forth together a thousandfold; let twenty chant the hymn of praise around him.
A hundred have shouted acclaim after him for Indra, as the sacred prayer is offered up; they sing in accordance with his self-sovereignty.
Indra struck down the power of Vṛtra with his overwhelming force;
great was that manly deed of his. Having slain Vṛtra, he released the waters, singing in praise of his own sovereign rule.

Even these two great worlds tremble in fear at your wrath, O Indra, wielder of the thunderbolt, when you, accompanied by the Maruts, struck Vṛtra with your might; they sang in praise of your self-sovereignty.
Neither by trembling nor by thundering did Vṛtra terrify Indra;
against him the iron thunderbolt with its thousand points was hurled, while they sang in praise following his own sovereignty.

When you, O Indra, fought Vṛtra and your thunderbolt together with the bolt, as you sought to slay the serpent, O Indra, your power was established in heaven; we sing in praise of your sovereign rule.
At your roar, O wielder of the stone, both that which stands and that which moves tremble;
even Tvaṣṭṛ himself quivers with fear before your wrath, O Indra, as he acknowledges your sovereign rule.

For indeed, there is no one who surpasses Indra in heroic deeds, as we acknowledge; in him the gods have concentrated manly strength, wisdom, and power, while they sang in praise of his sovereign rule.
The prayer which Atharvan, Manu’s father, and Dadhyañc performed—the *brahmans* and hymns met together with Indra therein as of old; they sang in praise following his self-rule.
Indra, the slayer of Vṛtra, has been strengthened by men for exhilaration and for power.
Him indeed we invoke in great battles and in small; may he further us in the contests for booty.
For you, O hero, are worthy of the army; you are the one who bestows much.
You are the increaser even of the meager; you grant wealth in abundance to the sacrificer who presses the soma for you.
When battles arise and booty is set for the bold, yoke your two bay steeds that flow with exhilaration. Whom will you slay? To whom will you grant wealth? O Indra, place us in wealth.
By his wisdom, the great and terrible one has increased his power according to his own nature;
lofty in majesty, the fair-cheeked, tawny-hued god has placed the iron thunderbolt in his two hands at the very forefront.
He has filled the earthly expanse and has propped up the luminous realms in heaven.
O Indra, no one like you has ever been born, nor will there ever be; you have grown beyond all.
May Indra, who bestows upon the donor the food of mortals that belongs to the noble one, grant us his aid; distribute your abundant wealth among us, and may I partake of your bounty.
For time and again our upright-minded [god] has given us herds of cattle;
grasp for yourself many hundreds of riches with both hands, sharpen them, and bring wealth hither!
Rejoice in the pressed juice, O Hero, for the sake of strength and bounty;
for we know you as the possessor of many riches, and we have released our desires toward you—therefore, be our protector.
O Indra, these people of yours nourish every desirable thing; for you, as the noble one, look within upon the wealth of those men who do not offer oblations. Bring that wealth to us.
Listen well, O Maghavan, to our songs like a mother;
when you have granted us wealth accompanied by true blessings, then indeed, Indra, yoke your two bay horses.
They have eaten and they have rejoiced; the dear ones have shaken themselves free.
The self-luminous sages have been praised with a most new hymn. Now, O Indra, yoke your two bay steeds!
O Maghavan, we shall pay homage to you, who are so beautiful to behold.
Now, O you whose chariot-seat is full, being praised, go according to our desires; yoke now, O Indra, your two bay horses.
He indeed shall mount that bull-like chariot, the winner of cattle, who, O Indra, keeps in mind the full vessel for the yoking of the bay steeds; now, O Indra, yoke your two bays.
O Śatakratu, let your right hand be yoked and your left as well;
with that, exhilarated by the soma-juice, go toward your beloved wife. Now, O Indra, yoke your two bay horses.
I yoke for you with prayer the two long-maned bay steeds; come hither, for you hold them in your hands.
The impetuous pressed juices have exhilarated you; O wielder of the thunderbolt, accompanied by Pūṣan, you have rejoiced together with your wife.
O Indra, the mortal man whom you protect well with your aids goes foremost among those possessing horses and cattle;
him indeed you fill with even greater wealth, as the conscious waters flow from all sides toward the ocean.
Like the divine waters, they approach the Hotṛ’s station; they look down as if upon the wide expanse of the intermediate region.
The gods lead the seeker of the gods forward with their rays; like suitors, they take pleasure in him who loves the sacred word.
You have bestowed praiseworthy speech upon the two who, with uplifted ladles, worship you as a pair.
Unrestrained, he dwells and prospers within your sacred law; auspicious is the power for the sacrificer who presses the soma.
Then the Aṅgirases first attained vital strength, they who kindled the fires through their skillful labor and sacred rite.
Those heroes found all the Panis’ provisions; they brought back cattle and livestock consisting of horses and kine.
Atharvan first stretched out the paths with sacrifices; from there Sūrya was born, the guardian of the law, the seer.
Uśanas Kāvya drove forth the cows together; we worship the immortal birth of Yama.
Whether the sacrificial grass is trimmed for the sake of good offspring, or the hymn proclaims its fame in heaven,
or where the pressing-stone speaks and the singer is worthy of praise— Indra takes delight in those occasions when they have arrived.
The Soma has been pressed for you, O Indra; most powerful and bold one, come hither!
Let Indra-power fill you, as the sun fills the mid-air with its rays.
The two bay steeds carry Indra, whose power is unassailable,
toward the praises of the seers and toward the sacrifice of human beings.
Mount the chariot, O slayer of Vṛtra; your two bay steeds have been yoked by our prayer.
May the pressing-stone, with its roar, turn your mind toward us.
O Indra, drink this pressed juice, the most excellent, immortal exhilaration;
the streams of the bright [Soma] have flowed toward you at the seat of Cosmic Order.
Now sing to Indra and proclaim your hymns;
the pressed drops have exhilarated him. Pay homage to his supreme might.
No one is a better charioteer than you, O Indra, when you restrain your two bay horses; no one has ever equaled you in might, nor has anyone with fine steeds attained your level.
He alone who bestows wealth upon the mortal who offers oblations—
the sovereign, the irresistible Indra— verily he is so.
When will he trample with his foot the ungenerous mortal like a mushroom?
When indeed, O Indra, will you truly hear our songs?
For whoever, having pressed the soma, seeks to win you over from among many—Indra indeed possesses that fierce power; truly so.
The Gauri-cows drink thus of the sweet, pervasive honey, they who, traveling together with the bull Indra, rejoice for the sake of splendor; being excellent, they follow their own sovereignty.
These spotted cows of his, longing for the touch, mix the Soma;
Indra’s beloved milch-cows urge on the thunderbolt, the missile, according to their own excellent sovereignty.
With homage, those wise ones worship his conquering power;
they follow his many ordinances for the sake of primordial awareness, the excellent ones following his self-sovereignty.
With the bones of Dadhyac, Indra, irresistible, struck down ninety-nine Vṛtras.
Desiring the horse's head which was hidden away in the mountains,
he found it at Śaryaṇāvat.
There they recognized the secret name of Tvaṣṭṛ’s cow,
right there in the dwelling of the moon.

Who today yokes to the pole of Order the impetuous, fierce, and ill-disposed bulls—those who carry arrows in their mouths, who pierce the heart, yet bring delight? Only he who fulfills their service shall live.
Who flees? Who is struck with fear? Who is afraid? Who will recognize Indra as being present and near?
Who will speak in favor of offspring, of cattle, of wealth, or of his own body, or for the sake of the people?

Who prays to Agni with an oblation of ghee? Who shall sacrifice with the ladle according to the fixed seasons? To whom shall the gods bring [the offering] for the swift sacrifice? Who, possessing a good god, will consider himself a successful offerer?
O most powerful god, you alone shall truly praise the mortal;
O bounteous Indra, there is no one other than you who shows compassion—this word I speak to you.
O Vasu, let not your bounties nor your aids ever fail us;
O Manu’s son, bestow upon us all riches from among the peoples.

Those sons of Rudra who adorn themselves like wives or like coursers on their journey, performing wondrous deeds—they have indeed made heaven and earth grow; the heroes, impetuous in the assemblies, rejoice.
Having grown strong, they have attained greatness; the Rudras have established their seat in heaven.
Chanting their hymn and generating vital power, these sons of Pṛśni have clothed themselves in splendor.
When the cow-mothers adorn themselves with ointments, the radiant ones have placed shining ornaments upon their bodies;
they drive away every adversary, and along their paths, clarified butter flows.
Those who shine forth as great warriors with their spears, shaking even the unshakable by their might—
when you Maruts, whose hosts are like bulls, yoked the spotted deer to your chariots that are swift as thought.
When you have harnessed the spotted deer to your chariots, O Maruts, speeding the stone in the contest for booty;
then the streams of the ruddy one burst forth, and like a skin with water, they drench the earth.
May your swift-gliding, rapid-flying coursers carry you hither; come forward with your arms.
Sit upon the sacrificial grass; a wide seat has been prepared for you. O Maruts, rejoice in the sweet soma-juice.
They grew strong by their own power through their greatness; they ascended to the firmament and made for themselves a wide dwelling.
When Viṣṇu ran to the bull who distills intoxication, they sat down like birds upon the beloved sacrificial grass.
Like heroes eager for combat, like warriors rushing forward, they have exerted themselves in battles like those seeking glory.
All beings are afraid of the Maruts; these men are like kings, terrible to behold.
When Tvaṣṭṛ, the skillful artisan, fashioned the well-made golden thunderbolt with its thousand points, Indra took it up to perform manly deeds; he slew Vṛtra and released the flood of waters.
By their might they pushed the well upward; they split even the firmly fixed mountain asunder. Blowing their pipe, the bounteous Maruts performed deeds of joy in the exhilaration of Soma.
They pushed aside the obstructing well in that direction and poured forth the fountain for the thirsty Gotama.
Coming with their aid, O you of wondrous luster, they satisfied the desire of the sage by means of their powers.
The protections that you have for the one who exerts himself, grant those threefold protections to the donor. Extend them to us, O Maruts; bestow upon us, O bulls, wealth accompanied by heroic sons.
O Maruts, of great splendor, that person in whose dwelling you drink from heaven is indeed the most well-protected of people.
O Maruts, you who are borne by sacrifices, whether through our sacrifices or through the hymns of the inspired singer, hear our call!
Or he, for whom the prize-winners have fashioned a sage,
shall go to a stall filled with cattle.
Upon the sacrificial grass of this hero, Soma is pressed during the daily rites;
the hymn of praise and the exhilarating draught are recited.
May all the peoples listen to him, he who surpasses them all;
may the strengthening draughts flow even toward the Sun.
For through many autumns we have offered worship to you, O Maruts,
with the protections granted to the people.
O Maruts, may that mortal be fortunate whom you, O most worshipful ones,
carry across in your advances.
O heroes of true strength, you who find the sweat of the one striving in worship,
and the desire of the longing seeker.
O you of true strength, reveal that [deed] by your greatness;
pierce the *rakṣas* with your lightning-flash.
Concealing the secret darkness, drive away every devouring demon; create the light that we desire.
Exceedingly vigorous, powerful, overflowing with strength, unbowed and unshakable, drinkers of the dregs;
most beloved and most manly, they have adorned themselves with ointments like some who spread their rays over the dawn.
When you have gathered on your secret paths like birds on their flight, O Maruts, along whatever road you travel;
then the casks drip upon your chariots—sprinkle the honey-colored ghee for the one who sings your praise!
At their onset, the earth trembles as if unsteady during their marches when they yoke themselves for glory;
they, the playful, the roaring, with glittering spears, the shakers, themselves proclaim their own greatness.
For he is the self-moving host with spotted horses, the youthful one; you are the ruler, surrounded by powers.
You are the true one, the seeker of debts, the blameless one; you are the furtherer of this prayer and the bull-like host.
Through the lineage of our ancient father, we speak; the tongue of Soma goes forth with his vision.
When the chanters reached Indra with their labor, they assumed names worthy of sacrifice.
For the sake of glory, they have mingled themselves with splendors; they, together with the rays and the chanters, are well-armed.
Armed with axes, impetuous, and fearless, they have found the beloved domain of the Maruts.
O Maruts, come hither with your lightning-bright chariots, well-sounding, armed with spears, and winged with horses;
fly toward us like birds with most abundant food, O you of wondrous power.
They come for our choice, with their ruddy, tawny horses that hasten the chariot for our welfare;
brilliant like a golden ornament, equipped with axes, they strike the earth with the tires of their chariot.
For the sake of glory, do you place axes upon your bodies? May they make the sacrificial offerings stand upright like forests.
For you, O well-born Maruts of great splendor, they set the pressing-stone in motion.

The days have come around to you, O eagles; the Gotamas, performing the sacred prayer with their hymns, have sent forth this divine thought and the song of praise, so that you may drink from the uplifted vessel of the well.
This very bond was not perceived, O Maruts, when Gotama beheld you in secret— beholding you as you sped along on golden wheels, with tusks of iron, like wild boars.
O Maruts, this voice of yours, like that of a singer, resounds in response; it has spontaneously caused the songs to throb according to the self-power within his hands.
May auspicious intentions come to us from every side—intentions that are undeceived, unimpeded, and victorious.
May the gods always be with us for our prosperity, our guardians day by day, never failing in their care.
May the auspicious favor of the gods who walk uprightly be ours; may the bounty of the gods turn toward us.
We have sought the friendship of the gods; may the gods extend our lifespan that we may live.
We invoke them with an ancient invocation: Bhaga, Mitra, Aditi, Dakṣa, and the infallible Aryaman, Varuṇa, Soma, and the Aśvins. May Sarasvatī, the bringer of good fortune, grant us happiness.
May the Wind blow that healing medicine upon us which brings delight; may Mother Earth grant it, and Father Heaven grant it.
May the pressing-stones that press the Soma, bringing delight, grant it; and do you two, O Ashvins, mindful ones, hear this.
We invoke for our protection that Lord, the master of all that moves and stands, the inspirer of the intellect;
may Pūṣan be the increaser of our wealth, our protector and undeceivable guardian for our well-being.
May Indra of far-reaching fame grant us well-being; may Pūṣan, the knower of all, grant us well-being;
may Tārkṣya, whose wheel-rims are uninjured, grant us well-being; may Bṛhaspati bestow well-being upon us.
The Maruts, whose horses are spotted, whose mother is Pṛśni, who move in beauty and frequent the assemblies;
the Manavas, whose tongue is Agni and whose eyes are the sun—may all the gods come here to us with their protection.
O Gods, may we hear with our ears what is auspicious; O Holy Ones, may we see with our eyes what is auspicious.
With firm limbs and bodies, praising you, may we attain that lifespan ordained by the gods.
A hundred autumns indeed are before us, O gods, within which you have ordained the aging of our bodies;
wherein sons become fathers—do not harm our life-span in its course.
Aditi is heaven, Aditi is the mid-air; Aditi is the mother, she is the father, she is the son.
All the gods are Aditi, the five peoples are Aditi; Aditi is what has been born, Aditi is what is to be born.
May Varuṇa and Mitra, the wise, lead us with straight guidance;
may Aryaman, in harmony with the gods, do the same.
For they are the masters of wealth; they are never overcome by their own greatness. They guard the sacred laws at all times.
May they, the immortals, grant protection to us mortals,
driving away our enemies.
May Indra and the Maruts mark out our paths for our well-being;
may Pūṣan and Bhaga, the ones worthy of praise, do so as well.
And may our prayers, headed by the acquisition of cattle— O Pūṣan, O Viṣṇu, you who move swiftly—
make us possessors of well-being.
The winds blow honey for the one who follows the cosmic order; the rivers flow with honey; may the plants be sweet for us.
May the night be honey-sweet, and may the dawns be honey-sweet; may the earthly realm be honey-sweet, and may our Father Heaven be honey-sweet for us.
May the Lord of the Forest be honey-sweet for us; may the Sun be honey-sweet;
may the cows be full of sweetness for us.
May Mitra be auspicious to us, may Varuṇa be auspicious, and may Aryaman be auspicious to us.
May Indra and Bṛhaspati be auspicious to us, and may Viṣṇu of the wide stride be auspicious to us.
O Soma, you are preeminent in wisdom; you lead us along the straightest path.
Under your guidance, O Indu, our wise fathers obtained their share of treasure among the gods.
O Soma, through your mental powers you have become one of noble intellect; through your skills you have become one of noble skill, the knower of all.
You are a bull by your bull-like qualities and your greatness; through your splendors, O splendid one, you have become the beholder of men.
Truly, thy laws are those of King Varuṇa; lofty and profound, O Soma, is thy domain.
Thou art pure, like the beloved Mitra; thou art to be honored like Aryaman, O Soma.
Those abodes of yours which are in heaven, those on earth, and those in the mountains, in the plants, and in the waters—
with all of them, O King Soma, being well-disposed and free from anger, accept our offerings.
O Soma, you are the lord of the virtuous; you are the king and the slayer of Vṛtra;
you are the auspicious power of will.
And you, O Soma, being our will, let us not die, but live on— you,
the Lord of the Forest, whose hymns are dear.
O Soma, you bestow great fortune upon the aged, and you grant strength for life to the youth who follows the eternal law.
O Soma, O King, protect us from every side against the one who intends us evil;
a friend such as you shall never come to harm.
O Soma, those bliss-bestowing aids of yours which exist for the donor—
with those, be our protector.
Enjoying this sacrifice and these words, come hither;
O Soma, be for our prosperity.
O Soma, we who are skilled in speech magnify you with our songs; enter us as one who is most gracious.
O Soma, be a good friend to us— you who increase the home, drive away disease, find wealth, and augment prosperity.
O Soma, take delight in our heart, as cattle do in pastures,
like a young man in his own home.
O divine Soma, whatever mortal delights in your friendship,
him the skillful sage attends.
Protect us from calumny, O Soma; guard us from distress. Be a most gracious friend to us.
Swell up; let virile power come to you from every side, O Soma; be present at the gathering of the prize.
Swell up, O most intoxicating Soma, with all your stalks;
become for us a most glorious friend for our prosperity.
May thy milks, thy strengths, and thy bull-like powers that overcome the assailants come together;
swelling for the sake of immortality, O Soma, bestow the highest glories upon us in heaven.
Those abodes of yours which they worship with oblation—may all those be encompassers of our sacrifice.
Increasing the household, furthering us, rich in heroes and not slaying our men, O Soma, enter the dwellings.

Soma gives a milch-cow; Soma gives a swift steed; Soma gives a hero, skillful in action—one who is effective in the household, eminent in the assembly, and worthy of the council hall, who brings glory to his father, to him who offers oblations to him.

Unconquered in battles, the furtherer in conflicts, winner of light, winner of waters, guardian of the stronghold, born for the fray, providing secure dwelling and great renown— O Soma, may we rejoice after you as you conquer!
O Soma, you generated all these plants; you generated the waters and the cows.
You have stretched out the wide mid-air; with light, you have dispelled the darkness.
O divine Soma, with your divine mind, O powerful one, fight for our share of wealth. Let it not fail you; you are the master of heroic might. Provide for both sides in the struggle for cattle.
These Dawns have indeed raised their banner; in the eastern half of the mid-region they anoint themselves with light.
Like bold warriors preparing their weapons, the ruddy cows, the mothers, come forth toward us.
The ruddy beams have flown upward at will; they have yoked their own red, self-yoked cows. The dawns have performed their works as of old; the ruddy ones have spread forth their radiant light.
The women sing out with their labors like busy ones, traveling from afar by a common path;
bringing nourishment to the well-doer who gives good gifts, they do so every day for the sacrificer who presses the soma.
Like a dancer, she puts on her ornaments; like a cow baring her udder, she uncovers her breast. Creating light for the whole world, Dawn has opened up the darkness as cows leave their pen.
Her radiant ray has been seen facing us; it spreads abroad and drives away the black monster.
Like one anointing a sacrificial post with ornament at the rites, the Daughter of Heaven has spread her wondrous luster.

We have crossed to the further shore of this darkness; the dawning Uṣas makes the paths clear. Smiling for the sake of beauty like a song, she shines forth with radiant countenance; she has awakened us for well-being.
Radiant leader of true blessings, the Daughter of Heaven is praised by the Gotamas.
O Dawn, grant us strengths that consist of progeny, heroes, and horses, and have cattle as their foremost part.
O Dawn, may I obtain that glorious wealth consisting of brave sons, preceded by the subduing of Dāsas and culminating in horses—
wealth that you, O auspicious one, radiate forth with wondrous fame, impelled by strength and exalted.
Beholding all beings, O Goddess, she shines far and wide with her gaze turned toward us.
Awakening every living creature to movement, she has found the speech of every thoughtful man.
Being born again and again, ever ancient, adorning herself with the same color,
like a skillful gambler winning the stakes, the goddess wears away the life of mortals.
Uncovering the ends of heaven, she has awakened; she drives her sister far away. Diminishing the ages of men, the maiden shines forth with the glance of her lover.
Like cattle, the wonderful and blessed one has spread herself out; like the flood of a river, she has shone far and wide.
Not violating the divine ordinances, she is perceived as she becomes visible with the rays of the sun.
O Uṣas, rich in prizes, bring to us that wondrous wealth by which we may obtain offspring and descendants.
O Uṣas, rich in cattle and horses, resplendent one, shine here today upon us, O bounteous lady, with wealth and joy.
Yoke, O Uṣas rich in steeds, your ruddy horses today;
then bring to us all auspicious fortunes.
O Aśvins, wonder-workers, come to our dwelling rich in cattle and gold; with one mind, direct your chariot hitherward.
Since you two have thus brought forth from heaven a song of praise and light for mankind,
O Aśvins, bring nourishment to us.
May the gods, the wonder-workers who bring bliss, whose paths are golden, and who awaken at dawn, come here to drink the Soma.
O Agni and Soma, you two bulls, graciously hear this my invocation;
accept these hymns with favor and be a source of joy to the donor.
O Agni and Soma, to him who today honors you with this speech,
bestow heroic strength, abundance of cattle, and possession of good horses.
O Agni and Soma, whoever offers an oblation or presents a prepared sacrifice to you,
may he, through his offspring, enjoy heroic vigor and a full span of life.
O Agni and Soma, that heroic power of yours is celebrated, whereby you stole the food, the Pani, and the cows;
