you struck down the offspring of Bṛsaya and found the single light for many.
O Agni and Soma, you two of one mind have placed these luminous realms in heaven;
O Agni and Soma, you two have released the rivers from reproach and from the snare.
Mātariśvan brought one from heaven; the falcon churned the other from the mountain.
O Agni and Soma, strengthened by our prayer, you have made wide space for the sacrifice.
O Agni and Soma, enjoy this presented oblation; O bulls, desire it and take pleasure in it.
For you have become providers of good protection and good help; therefore, bestow well-being and prosperity upon the sacrificer.
O Agni and Soma, protect the vow of him who honors you with an oblation, who honors you with a mind directed toward the gods, and who honors you with clarified butter;
guard him from distress and grant great protection to his people and his household.
O Agni and Soma, you who possess common wealth and are invoked together, accept our songs; you have both become present among the gods.
O Agni and Soma, for him who honors you with this [offering] or with clarified butter,
shine forth greatly for him.
O Agni and Soma, may you both enjoy these our oblations;
come together to us.
O Agni and Soma, protect our horses; let the cows that yield the oblation swell with milk.
Bestow strength upon us and upon our patrons, and make our sacrifice successful and full of prompt obedience.
For this worthy Jātavedas, let us fashion this hymn of praise with our intellect, as one fashions a chariot;
for his providence is auspicious for us in the assembly. O Agni, in your friendship, may we never suffer harm.

He for whom you perform the sacrifice succeeds; he dwells free from enemies and possesses great heroic strength. He prospers, and no distress reaches him. O Agni, in your friendship may we never suffer harm.

May we be able to kindle you; may our prayers be fulfilled. In you the gods eat the offered oblation. Bring hither the Ādityas, for we desire them; O Agni, in your friendship may we never suffer harm.
Let us bring fuel and prepare oblations for you, mindful of you at every joint of the ritual;
further our prayers so that we may live. O Agni, in your friendship, may we never suffer harm.
The guardians of the people, his creatures, move about during the nights—both bipeds and quadrupeds.
Wondrous is the herald of the Dawn; great art thou, O Agni. In thy friendship, may we never suffer harm.
You are the Adhvaryu and the ancient Hotṛ; by birth you are the Praśāstṛ, the Potṛ, and the Purohita.
Knowing all the priestly functions, O wise one, you cause them to flourish, O Agni. In your friendship, may we never suffer harm.

O Agni, you who are beautiful to behold from every side and uniform in appearance, though far away you shine like lightning; O God, you see even through the darkness of night. In your friendship, may we never suffer harm.
O Gods, let the chariot of the one who presses the soma be foremost; may our hymn of praise overcome the evil-minded.
Take note of this and let our word flourish; O Agni, in your friendship may we never suffer harm.
Strike down the evil-minded with your weapons; slay all the devourers, whether they be far away or near.
Then, O Agni, make the path easy for the sacrifice and for the one who praises you; in your friendship, may we never suffer harm.

When you have yoked to your chariot the two ruddy, red steeds, impelled by the wind—your roar is like that of a bull; then you consume the trees with your smoke-bannered flame. O Agni, in your friendship may we never suffer harm.

Then at your roar, even the winged birds were struck with fear, when your sparks, devouring the grass, scattered abroad. May that path be easy for you and for your chariots; O Agni, in your friendship may we never suffer harm.

May this [hymn] serve for the satisfaction of Mitra and Varuṇa; may it appease the wondrous wrath of the Maruts. O Agni, be gracious to us and turn their minds toward us again; in your friendship, may we never suffer harm.
O God, you are the wondrous friend among the gods; O Vasu, you are the beloved among the Vasus at the sacrifice.
May we abide in your most expansive protection; O Agni, in your friendship may we never suffer harm.
That is your blessing, that when kindled in your own abode and invoked with Soma, you awaken as the most merciful one.
You bestow jewels and wealth upon the donor; O Agni, in your friendship may we never suffer harm.
To whomsoever you, O possessor of excellent wealth, grant sinlessness in the fullness of Aditi’s protection—
to him whom you impel with auspicious strength, may we be those who possess your wealth consisting of progeny.
O Agni, you who are the knower of good fortune, prolong our lifespan here, O God.
May Mitra, Varuṇa, Aditi, the Sindhu, the Earth, and also the Sky grant us that.
Two of different forms move toward their own goal; one after the other, they suckle the calf.
With the one, he becomes tawny, possessing his own nature; with the other, he is seen bright and full of splendor.
The tireless young women brought forth this embryo of Tvaṣṭṛ, who was to be distributed;
him with sharp-edged face, self-glorious among men, and shining brightly, they carry around.
They honor his three births: one in the ocean, one in heaven, and one in the waters.
Governing the seasons, he has duly established them according to the eastern quarter of the earthly realms.
Who among you has perceived this hidden one? The calf has brought forth his mothers by his own powers.
As the embryo of many, the great seer moves out from the lap of the active waters, self-sustaining.
The lovely one, worthy of invocation, grows great among these; rising upright in his own glory within the lap of the prostrate ones, he flourishes.
Both worlds tremble at Tvaṣṭṛ’s son as he is born; turning toward him, they welcome the lion.
Both auspicious ones delight him like two women; like lowing cows they have approached him with their ways.
He has become the lord of skill among the skilled, he whom they anoint from the right with oblations.
Like Savitṛ, he stretches out his arms; the terrible one, rushing forward, strives to join both skirts of his garment.
He draws up a bright mantle for himself alone; from his mothers he casts off his worn-out clothes as if they were new.
He assumes a brilliant form, even higher, as he mingles with the waters and the milk in his dwelling;
the seer, through his inspired thought, polishes the foundation. This has become the assembly at the gathering of the gods.
Wide extends your course around the foundation, the shining domain of the Great Bull.
O Agni, kindled with all your own glories, protect us with your infallible guardians.
In the desert he creates a stream, a path, and a wave; with his bright waves he reaches the earth.
He places all ancient things within his bellies; he moves within the new-born plants.
Thus, O Agni, increasing by our fuel, shine forth with wealth, O Purifier, for the sake of glory.
May Mitra, Varuṇa, Aditi, Sindhu, Earth, and Heaven grant us this.
Born by force as of old, he has instantly assumed all poetic wisdom.
Both the waters and the Dhiṣaṇā have made him their friend; the gods have established Agni as the bestower of wealth.
By means of the ancient invocation and his prophetic wisdom, he brought forth these progeny of men;
with Vivasvat as their eye, the gods maintained Agni, the giver of wealth, [to sustain] the heavens and the waters.
The Āryan clans magnified him, the first accomplisher of sacrifice, who is invoked with oblations and who strives forward;
the gods maintained Agni, the son of strength, the bearer, the giver of flowing gifts, the bestower of wealth.
May Mātariśvan, whose nourishment brings many boons, find a path for his offspring and win the light of heaven.
The guardians of the people, the progenitors of the two worlds, the gods have established Agni as the bestower of wealth.
Night and Dawn, blending their colors, suckle the one infant together;
between heaven and earth the golden disk shines forth. The gods have established Agni, the giver of wealth.
The foundation of wealth, the gatherer of treasures, the banner of sacrifice, the fulfiller of thought, the bird—
protecting their immortality, the gods maintained this Agni as the giver of riches.

Now as of old, the gods have maintained Agni, the bestower of wealth, the dwelling place of riches for what has been born and what is being born, the guardian of what exists and of what shall become abundant.
May the Giver of Wealth bestow upon us the wealth of the swift one; may the Giver of Wealth grant us the wealth of heroes.
May the Giver of Wealth grant us food accompanied by brave sons; may the Giver of Wealth grant us long life.
Thus, O Agni, increasing by our fuel, shine forth with wealth, O Purifier, for the sake of glory!
May Mitra, Varuṇa, Aditi, Sindhu, Earth, and Heaven grant us this.
May our evil be burned away; O Agni, shine wealth upon us;
may our evil be burned away.
With a desire for good fields, for a good path, and for wealth, we sacrifice;
may he burn away our evil.
When he, the most excellent among these, has been praised, and our wise patrons have also praised him,
may he burn away our evil.
O Agni, when through thee the wise patrons are born, may we also be born through thee;
may he burn away our evil.
When the rays of the powerful Agni go forth in all directions,
may he burn away our evil.
For you, O you whose face is turned everywhere, encompass all things from every side;
burn away our evil.
O you whose face is turned in every direction, carry us across our enemies as if with a boat;
burn away our evil.
May he carry us across for our well-being, as one crosses a river by boat;
may he burn away our evil.
May we abide in the good-will of Vaiśvānara; for he is the king, the glory of all beings.
Born from here, he beholds this entire universe; Vaiśvānara strives in harmony with the Sun.
Sought in heaven, sought on earth, Agni has entered all the plants;
Vaiśvānara Agni, sought with power, may he protect us from harm by day and by night.
O Vaiśvānara, let that be true for you: may riches and liberal patrons attend us.
May Mitra, Varuṇa, Aditi, the Sindhu, the Earth, and also Heaven grant us this.
Let us press the Soma for Jātavedas; may he burn away the wealth of the one who acts with hostility.
May Agni carry us across all difficulties, as if across a river with a boat, beyond all misfortunes.

May that Indra, the bull who dwells together with his bull-like powers, the sovereign lord of the great heaven and earth, whose warriors are true, who is to be invoked in battles— may he, accompanied by the Maruts, be our protection.
He whose course is unassailable like that of the sun, who possesses the strength of a Vṛtra-slayer in every battle;
may Indra, the most virile one with his own companions and according to his wonted ways, come to us for aid, accompanied by the Maruts.
Whose paths, like the streams of heaven’s seed being milked, go forth unassailable by might;
he who overcomes hatreds and is victorious through his manly deeds—may Indra, accompanied by the Maruts, be our protection.
He, the best of the Aṅgiras, became [one] with the Aṅgiras; the bull, being a friend with his bull-like friends;
the singer, with the singers; the most excellent one with his paths—may Indra, accompanied by the Maruts, be for our protection.
Skilled like Rudra with his sons, he has overcome the enemies in the battle for men;
surpassing those of common origin toward glorious deeds—may Indra, accompanied by the Maruts, be our protection.
He who quells the fury of the combatant, the maker of the fray, may he win the sun with our men;
on this very day, may Indra—the lord of the virtuous, much-invoked, accompanied by the Maruts—be with us for our protection.
His aids gladden him in the battle for booty; the peoples make him the protector of their security.
He alone is the lord of every pious deed. May Indra, accompanied by the Maruts, be ours for our protection.
Men seek him out for help at the festivals of strength, that hero, for his protection and for wealth;
may Indra, accompanied by the Maruts, who finds light even in blinding darkness, be our aid.
With his left hand he restrains even those who are swelling with pride; with his right hand he gathers the spoils of war.
Even through the singer, he wins riches. May Indra, accompanied by the Maruts, be our protection.
He wins with his hosts and he wins with his chariots; may he be known today by all the people.
May Indra, the overcomer of curses through his manly deeds, accompanied by the Maruts, be our protection.
When he, invoked by many, comes according to his wont to the sacrifice with kinsmen or with strangers,
may Indra, accompanied by the Maruts, be our protector for the winning of waters, of offspring, and of progeny.
May that wielder of the thunderbolt, slayer of the Dasyus, terrible and fierce, possessing a thousand insights and a hundred ways,
skillful and like the Soma-juice in power, Indra— belonging to the five peoples and accompanied by the Maruts— be our protection.
His thunderbolt roars along, winning the light of heaven; like the brilliant, impetuous roar of the sky, it resounds with might.
Victories attend him and treasures follow him; may Indra, accompanied by the Maruts, be our protection.

He whose hymn of praise, through his constant power, encompasses both heaven and earth on every side—he, Indra, being exhilarated by our rites, shall protect us; may he come to us with the Maruts for our aid.

Neither gods among the gods, nor mortals, nor even the waters have reached the limit of his might. He who has overspread the earth and heaven with his power—may that Indra, accompanied by the Maruts, be our protection.
The ruddy mare, dark-brown, well-adorned with a mark on her forehead, celestial, and the bringer of wealth for R̥jrāśva—
she who bears the stallion-drawn chariot at the yoke-poles, the joyous one, has been noticed among the tribes of Nahuṣa.
This is that hymn for you, O Indra, the Bull; the sons of Vṛṣāgir praise your bounty.
Ṛjrāśva with his side-horses, Ambarīṣa, Sahadeva, and Bhayamāna Surādhas [participate].
O you who are invoked by many, having slain the Dasyus and the Śimyus by your own power, you have struck them down upon the earth with your arrow.
With your brilliant friends, the wielder of the excellent thunderbolt has won the land, he has won the sun, and he has won the waters.
May Indra be our advocate every day; may we, unassailed, win the prize.
May Mitra, Varuṇa, Aditi, Sindhu, Earth, and Heaven grant us this.
Sing forth a word full of nourishment to the gladdening one, who with Ṛjiśvan struck down [the demons] whose wombs were black.
Seeking aid, we invoke for friendship the bull who wields the thunderbolt in his right hand, accompanied by the Maruts.
Indra, who with his exultant fury struck down Vyansa, who slew Shambara and the lawless Pipru, and who cast down the insatiable Shushna— we invoke him, accompanied by the Maruts, for friendship.
He whose great manly power is heaven and earth, in whose ordinance Varuṇa and Sūrya abide,
and whose law the rivers follow— that Indra, accompanied by the Maruts, we invoke for friendship.
He who is the master and controller of horses and of cattle, who is invoked and remains steadfast in every rite—
he, Indra, the slayer even of the strong man who pours no libations, him we invoke with the Maruts for friendship.
He who is the lord of all that moves and breathes, who first found the cows for the Brahman,
Indra, who cast down the Dasyus— him, accompanied by the Maruts, we invoke for friendship.
He who is to be invoked by the brave and by the timid, who is called upon by those fleeing and by those victorious—
he, Indra, whom all beings have united under their protection, him we invoke, accompanied by the Maruts, for friendship.

The far-seeing one goes forth by the direction of the Rudras; the maiden extends her wide course with the Rudras. The inspired thought praises Indra, the renowned; we invoke him, accompanied by the Maruts, for friendship.

Whether you rejoice, O Lord of the Maruts, in the highest dwelling place, or in the lowest assembly, come from there toward our sacrifice; desiring you, we have prepared the oblation, O bestower of true wealth.
O Indra of great skill, for you we have pressed the Soma; O you who are borne by our prayer, for you we have prepared the oblation.
Therefore, O Lord of the teams, together with your host of Maruts, rejoice at this sacrifice upon the sacred grass.
Rejoice with the bay steeds that are yours, O Indra; unbind your jaws and open wide your lips.
Let the bay steeds, O fair-jawed one, bring you hither; desiring our offerings, graciously accept them.
We, the guardians of the host that praises the Maruts, may we win booty through Indra.
May Mitra, Varuṇa, Aditi, Sindhu, Earth, and Heaven grant us this.

I bring forth this great prayer for you, the mighty one, since my mind has been adorned for his praise. At the festival and at the impulse [of sacrifice], the gods have followed Indra with power, acknowledging him as the conqueror.
The seven rivers bear his fame; heaven and earth and the broad world bear his beautiful form. For us to behold, O Indra, the sun and moon move in their alternating course for the sake of faith.
O Maghavan, favor that victorious chariot of yours for our gain, which we shall cheer on in the encounter;
O Indra, praised by many, in this battle, O Maghavan, grant protection with your mind to us who are devoted to you.
May we, with you as our ally, conquer the foe; protect our share in every battle.
O Indra, grant us wide space and easy passage; O Maghavan, shatter the virile strength of our enemies.
For these various people, desiring wealth and praising you with their aid, call upon you from many sides, O upholder of riches.
Ascend our chariot for the sake of gain; for victorious, O Indra, is your steadfast mind.
His arms are winners of cattle; he is the peerless one of boundless power. At every deed, he provides a hundredfold aid; he is the stirrer of the fray.
Indra, incomparable in his might, is without a match; therefore, people invoke him as they desire to win.

O Maghavan, your fame among the people has surpassed a hundred and even more than a thousand; you have exceeded them all. Your measureless inspiration has glowed for you greatly; thus, O Purandara, you strike down the Vṛtras.
A match for thy might is the threefold heaven; O Lord of men, thou hast extended beyond the three earths and the three luminous realms.
This entire world thou hast grown beyond; Indra, from birth thou hast been without an enemy from of old.
We invoke you first among the gods; you have become the conqueror in battles.
May Indra place this singer Upaniṣṭha at the forefront in our enterprise, making him a breaker-through like a chariot.
You have conquered; you did not withhold wealth, O Maghavan, in battles whether small or great.
We sharpen you, the fierce one, for protection; therefore, O Indra, impel us in our invocations.
May Indra be our advocate every day; unassailed, may we win the prize.
May Mitra, Varuṇa, Aditi, Sindhu, Earth, and Heaven grant us this.
That supreme power of yours, the seers sustained in the distance even before this [world] existed.
One part of it is on earth, another is in heaven; these two are joined together like a banner in a gathering.
He supported the earth and spread it out; having struck with his thunderbolt, he released the waters.
He slew the serpent, he split Rauhiṇa asunder, and Maghavan struck down Vyaṃsa with his mighty powers.
Possessing innate strength and full of faith, he advanced, shattering the forts of the Dāsas.
O wielder of the thunderbolt, knowing the way, hurl your weapon at the Dasyu; O Indra, increase the Aryan power and his glorious splendor.

To him who spoke thus, these human ages have come, as he bears the praiseworthy name Maghavan. Approaching for the slaughter of the Dasyus, the wielder of the thunderbolt has indeed assumed the name Son for the sake of glory.
Behold this vast abundance of his; place your faith in the heroic power of Indra.
He found the cattle, he found the horses; he found the plants, he found the waters, and he found the forests.
For the bull of many deeds, the vigorous one of true might, let us press the Soma;
he who, like a hero ambushing on the road, goes about distributing the wealth of the non-sacrificer.
O Indra, you truly performed that heroic deed when with your thunderbolt you awakened the sleeping dragon;
the wives, the birds, and all the gods rejoiced after you as you were exultant.
When you, O Indra, slew Śuṣṇa, Pipru, Kuyava, and Vṛtra, and shattered the fortresses of Śambara—
may Mitra, Varuṇa, Aditi, Sindhu, Earth, and Heaven grant us that as a great boon.
A seat has been prepared for you, O Indra, to sit upon; sit down there like a neighing steed.
Unyoke your birds, unharness your horses—those most swift carriers—at evening and at dawn, at the time of departure.
Those heroes have indeed come to Indra for aid; may he swiftly traverse those paths.
May the gods quench the fury of the Dāsa, and may they lead our people toward prosperity.
He himself brings down the one who knows the signal; he himself brings down the foam upon the water.
Bathed in milk, the two wives of Kuyava shall lie slain in the steep descent of the Śiphā river.
The kinship of the lower Āyu has perished; the hero extends and rules with his ancient [deeds].
Añjasī, Kuliśī, and Vīrapatnī, swelling with milk, bring forth the waters.
When that path of the Dasyu was revealed, she who knows her way went toward our dwelling as if to her own home. Now, O Maghavan, remember us; do not cast us away like one who has lost his wealth.
As such, O Indra, grant us our share in the sun, in the waters, and in sinlessness, for the sake of living praise.
Do not harm our inner enjoyment; we have placed our trust in your great Indra-power.
Now, therefore, I believe that faith has been placed in you; as a bull, impel us toward great wealth.
O Indra, invoked by many, do not leave us in an unprepared dwelling; give food and drink to those who hunger.
Do not slay us, O Indra; do not abandon us; do not steal away our beloved enjoyments.
O Maghavan, O Śakra, do not pierce our eggs; do not shatter our vessels that are born together with us.
Come hither; they say you desire Soma—here it is pressed, drink of it for exhilaration!
O wide-extending one, pour it down into your belly; being invoked, hear us like a father.
The moon moves within the waters; the fair-winged one hastens through the sky.
O you whose rims are gold, the lightnings do not find your track. Discern this for me, O Heaven and Earth!
Seeking their purpose, indeed, those who seek it unite; the wife embraces her husband.
They pour forth vigorous milk; having bestowed the essence, she yields the sap. O Heaven and Earth, take note of this for me!
O gods, let not that light fall down from heaven; let us never be deprived of the Soma that brings prosperity. O Heaven and Earth, take note of this for me!
I ask about the lowest sacrifice; may he, as a messenger, declare that. Where has the ancient *ṛta* gone? Who maintains it now? O Heaven and Earth, find this out for me.
O you gods who are there in the three bright realms of heaven—what is truth for you, and what is untruth? Where is your ancient oblation? Take note of this for me, O Heaven and Earth!
What is the support of the Eternal Order? What is the gaze of Varuṇa?
How may we, O Heaven and Earth, avoid the evil-minded on the path of the great Aryaman? Be aware of this for me.
I am he who formerly, when the soma was pressed, would speak certain words.
Desires pursue me, like a wolf a thirsty deer; O Heaven and Earth, take note of this for me!
My ribs pain me on all sides like rival wives;
my testicles gnaw at me like mice. O Śatakratu, you devour your praiser. O Heaven and Earth, take note of this for me!
Those seven rays which exist—therein my navel is extended. Trita, the son of Āptya, knows that; he proclaims it because of kinship. O Heaven and Earth, find this for me!
Those five bulls who stand in the midst of the great heaven—worthy of being proclaimed among the gods—they have turned together toward one goal. O Heaven and Earth, take note of this for me!
These well-winged ones sit in the midst of the ascent of heaven;
they ward off the wolf from the paths as he crosses the swift waters. O Heaven and Earth, take note of this for me!
This is a new hymn, worthy of praise, well-proclaimed, O gods;
the rivers flow according to the *ṛta*, and Sūrya has spread out the truth. Discern this for me, O Heaven and Earth!

O Agni, that kinship of yours which is worthy of praise exists among the gods. Seated here like Manu, sacrifice for us to the gods, you who are most wise. O Heaven and Earth, take note of this of mine.

Seated like a man, the Hotṛ-priest, most wise, goes toward the gods; Agni, the god, skillfully prepares the oblations among the gods, he who is full of wisdom. O Heaven and Earth, take note of this for me!
Varuṇa, the Brahman, makes [the path] for him who knows the way; we entreat him.
He unfolds the thought in the heart; may a new [insight] be born. O Heaven and Earth, bear witness to this truth for me!
That path of the sun which has been made manifest in heaven—O gods, mortals do not overstep it; you do not see it. O Heaven and Earth, bear witness to this for me!
Trita, cast down into the well, called upon the gods for help;
Bṛhaspati heard that, making wide room from distress. Bear witness to this for me, O Heaven and Earth!
A ruddy wolf indeed saw me once as I was going along the path;
having perceived it, I rise up like a carpenter whose back is ailing. O Heaven and Earth, take note of this for me!
Through this hymn of praise, may we, accompanied by Indra and with all our heroes, prevail in the assembly;
may Mitra, Varuṇa, Aditi, Sindhu, Earth, and Heaven grant us this.
We invoke Indra, Mitra, Varuṇa, Agni, the host of Maruts, and Aditi for our protection.
Like a chariot from a difficult pass, O Vasus, you bounteous givers, deliver us from all distress.
O Ādityas, come hither for our complete well-being; O gods, be our benefactors in the battles against Vṛtra.
Like a chariot from a difficult pass, O Vasus, you bounteous givers, deliver us from every distress.
May the Pitṛs, worthy of our praise, and the two goddesses, mothers of the gods and increasers of cosmic order, protect us.
Like a chariot from a difficult pass, O Vasus, givers of good gifts, deliver us from all distress.
Seeking strength, we here implore with prayers for favor Narāśaṃsa, the vigorous, and Pūṣan, who dwells among heroes;
O Vasus, bounteous givers, deliver us from all distress as one delivers a chariot from a difficult pass.
O Bṛhaspati, always make for us an easy path; we beg for that which is health and well-being, established by Manu for you.
Like a chariot from a difficult pass, O Vasus, givers of good gifts, deliver us out of all distress.
Kutsa, the seer, having been pinned down in the pit, called upon Indra, the slayer of Vṛtra and lord of power, for help.
O bounteous Vasus, rescue us from all distress, as one rescues a chariot from a difficult pass.
May the goddess Aditi protect us along with the gods; may the god Trātṛ save us, never failing.
May Mitra, Varuṇa, Aditi, Sindhu, Earth, and Heaven grant us this.
The sacrifice goes forth toward the favor of the gods; O Ādityas, be gracious to us. May your benevolence turn hitherward, which finds wider space even from distress.
May the gods come to us with their protection, being praised by the Sāmans of the Aṅgirases;
may Indra with his powers, the Maruts with the Maruts, and Aditi with the Ādityas grant us shelter.
May Indra grant us this; may Varuṇa, Agni, Aryaman, and Savitar find this pleasing.
May Mitra, Varuṇa, Aditi, Sindhu, Earth, and Heaven grant us this as our gift.
O Indra and Agni, with that most wondrous chariot of yours which looks upon all living beings, come hither, mounted together on the same car; then drink of the pressed soma.
As vast as this entire world exists— broad in its extent and deep in its magnitude—
so much let this Soma be for your drinking, O Indra and Agni, sufficient for your minds.
For you two have made for yourselves a blessed name together; O slayers of Vṛtra, you are indeed united.
Therefore, O Indra and Agni, sitting down together as bulls, do you two, the mighty ones, drink of the mighty Soma.
When the fires are kindled, anointing yourselves and extending the sacrificial grass with uplifted ladles,
come hither, O Indra and Agni, for our goodwill, having been sprinkled with the potent Soma juices.

O Indra and Agni, whatever heroic deeds you have performed, whatever forms and powers you possess, and whatever ancient and auspicious friendships you have— by means of these, drink of the pressed Soma.
When I first spoke to you both while choosing, saying, "This Soma is to be invoked by us against the Asuras," come indeed toward that true faith, and then drink of the pressed Soma.
O Indra and Agni, when you rejoice in your own dwelling, or with a priest, or with a king,
O worshipful ones— come hither from there, O showerers of blessings, and drink of the pressed soma.
O Indra and Agni, whether you are among the Yadus, the Turvaśas, the Druhyus, the Anus,
or the Pūrus— come hither from there, O bulls, and drink of the pressed soma.
O Indra and Agni, whether you are on this lowest earth, on the middle one, or on the highest, come hither from there, O showerers of blessings; then drink of the pressed Soma.
O Indra and Agni, whether you are in the highest earth, in the middle one, or even in the lowest, come hither from there, O showerers of blessings; then drink of the pressed soma.
O Indra and Agni, whether you are stationed in heaven, on earth, upon the mountains, in the plants, or in the waters—from there, O showerers of blessings, come hither; then drink of the pressed Soma.
O Indra and Agni, when you rejoice according to your own will at the rising of the sun and in the midst of heaven,
come hither from there, O bulls, and drink of the pressed soma.
Thus, O Indra and Agni, having drunk of the pressed juice, win for us all riches.
May Mitra, Varuṇa, Aditi, Sindhu, Earth, and Heaven grant this to us.

For I have looked out with my mind, O Indra and Agni, desiring better things—whether kinsmen or fellow-clansmen; no other youthful providence exists for me. Therefore, I have fashioned this hymn for you that strives for the prize.
For I have heard that you two are more generous givers than a father-in-law or even a brother-in-law;
therefore, O Indra and Agni, as the Soma is offered to you, I generate a new hymn of praise.
"May we not sever the reins," so they cry out, as they follow the powers of the fathers;
for Indra and Agni, the bulls rejoice in them, for those two stones are in the lap of Dhiṣaṇā.
For you two, O Indra and Agni, the goddess Dhiṣaṇā, desiring it for your exhilaration, presses the Soma.
O Aśvins, with auspicious hands and fair palms, hasten hither; mix [the draught] with honey in the waters.
O Indra and Agni, I have heard that you two are most powerful in the distribution of wealth and in the slaying of Vṛtra;
therefore, having taken your seats upon the sacrificial grass at this sacrifice, O leaders of men, rejoice in the pressed soma.
You two surpass all people in the calls to battle; you exceed both the earth and the heavens in greatness.
You surpass the rivers and the mountains in majesty; O Indra and Agni, you transcend all other beings.
Bring hither, bestow your gifts, O you whose arms wield the thunderbolt; O Indra and Agni, protect us with your powers.
These indeed are the rays of the Sun, by which our fathers attained companionship.
O Purandaras, wielders of the thunderbolt, grant us aid; O Indra and Agni, protect us in battles.
May Mitra, Varuṇa, Aditi, Sindhu, Earth, and Heaven grant this to us.
That work of mine was performed, and it is being performed again; this most sweet hymn is recited for praise.
This ocean here belongs to all the gods; O Ṛbhus, satisfy yourselves with that which has been consecrated with the cry of Svāhā!
When they went forth seeking enjoyment, some of my kinsmen turned westward while others turned east;
O sons of Sudhanvan, you came by the abundance of your journey to the house of the liberal donor, Savitṛ.
Savitar bestowed immortality upon you, that which is unhidden, when you went seeking renown;
that very chalice, the drinking-vessel of the Asura, which was but one, you made fourfold.
Having performed their labor with skillful swiftness, the Ṛbhus, though being mortals, attained immortality;
the Ṛbhus, sons of Sudhanvan, with the eyes of the sun, were united with their prayers after a year.
Like a field, the Rbhus measured out with a rod that single, quivering vessel;
praised with hymns, seeking the highest, they strove for glory among the immortals.
With wisdom, let us offer our inspired thought to the heroes of the mid-air, like clarified butter poured from a ladle;
for the *Ṛbhus*, who by their skillful crossing followed this Father, have ascended to the realm of heaven for the sake of booty.
R̥bhu is Indra by his power, most new; R̥bhu is the giver of wealth with riches and treasures.
O gods, through your protection on the dear day, may we overcome the battles of those who do not press the Soma.
O Ṛbhus, you fashioned the cow out of hide; you reunited the mother with her calf. O sons of Sudhanvan, through your skillful craftsmanship, you made your aged parents young again.
With strengths, aid us in the winning of strength; O Indra, rich in *Ṛbhus*, disclose wondrous bounty to us.
May Mitra, Varuṇa, Aditi, Sindhu, Earth, and Heaven grant this to us in abundance.
The R̥bhus, whose works are performed with wisdom, fashioned the well-rolling chariot; they fashioned the two bay steeds that carry Indra, rich in virile wealth.
The R̥bhus fashioned vital strength for their parents; they fashioned for the calf a mother who was ever by its side.

Fashion for our sacrifice a vital strength rich in *ṛbhu*-power; grant us food accompanied by good offspring for wisdom and skill, so that we may dwell with a clan consisting of all heroes. Bestow upon this our host your own inherent power.
O R̥bhus, fashion for us means of acquisition; O heroes, fashion a means of acquisition for our chariot and a means of acquisition for our horse.
May you ever grant us victorious gain, which overcomes both kin and stranger in battles.
I invoke Indra, the lord of the *Ṛbhus*, for our protection; the *Ṛbhus*, the *Vājas*, and the *Maruts* to drink the Soma.
May both Mitra and Varuṇa, and now the Aśvins, impel us toward gain, toward prayer, and toward victory.
May Ṛbhu sharpen our success for the sake of the prize; may Vāja, the winner in battle, protect us. May Mitra, Varuṇa, Aditi, Sindhu, Earth, and Heaven grant this to us.
I praise Heaven and Earth for the first thought, Agni, the Gharma, and the fair-shining one for the journey and for the sacrifice.
With those aids wherewith you quicken the prize in battle for the sake of the portion, with those very aids come hither, O Aśvins!

For the sake of your gift, the well-prepared, inexhaustible [oblations] have mounted upon your chariot as if for the purpose of thought. With those aids by which you protect our prayers for the performance of the sacrifice—O Aśvins, come hither with those very aids!
By your power, you two rule over those divine clans under the command of immortality;
O heroes, with those aids wherewith you cause the barren cow to swell, come hither to us with those very succors, O Aśvins.
With those [powers] by which Parijman, through the greatness of his offspring, and the son of two mothers, swift among the swift, displays his splendor;
with those by which Trimantu became far-sighted—with those excellent aids, O Aśvins, come hither!

With those [powers] by which you caused Rebha, who was bound and submerged in the waters, to emerge and made Vandana see the light of heaven; with those by which you protected Kaṇva as he strove for gain—with those excellent aids, O Aśvins, come hither!
With those unswerving aids wherewith you quickened Antaka as he was wasting away in the conflict, and wherewith you restored Bhujyu to life,
and wherewith you gave strength to Karkandhu and Vayya— with those very succors come hither, O Aśvins!

With those [powers] by which you helped Śucanti, the winner of wealth and the one well-seated at the assembly, and with which you aided Atri when the *gharma* was heated for him; with those by which you protected Pṛśnigu and Purukutsa—with those very aids, O Aśvins, come hither quickly!
With those powers by which, O bulls, you enabled the blind and the lame to see and walk,
and with those by which you released the swallowed quail— come hither, O Aśvins, with those very aids!
With those [powers] by which you made the Sindhu river full of sweetness and inexhaustible, with which you, O ageless ones, quickened Vasiṣṭha,
and with which you protected Kutsa, Śrutarya, and Narya— come hither, O Aśvins, with those very aids.

With those aids by which you quickened Viśpalā, the winner of wealth and Atharvan’s daughter, when she was brought as a prize of a thousand in the race; with those aids by which you protected Vaśa Aśvya and Preṇi—come hither, O Aśvins, with those very succors.

With those aids by which, O bounteous ones, the vessel of honey flowed for the merchant Dīrghaśravas, the son of Uśij; with those aids by which you protected Kakṣīvat the singer—come hither, O Aśvins, with those excellent succors.
With those [powers] by which you made the Rasā river swell with the flood of water, with which you aided the horseless chariot to victory,
and with which Triśoka drove forth the cows— with those excellent aids, O Aśvins, come hither!
With those aids wherewith you encompassed the sun in the distance, and helped Mandhātṛ in his lordship over the lands;
with those aids wherewith you protected the sage Bharadvāja—come hither, O Aśvins, with those very succors.
With those aids by which you protected the great Atithigva, Kaśoju, and Divodāsa in the slaying of Śambara;
with those aids by which you protected Trasadasyu at the breaching of the forts—with those very aids, O Aśvins, come hither to us.
With those [powers] by which you honored Vamra when he was drinking deeply and receiving praise, with which you favored Kali who had won a wife,
and with which you protected Vyaśva and Pṛthi— with those very aids, O Aśvins, come hither to us.

With those aids by which, O Heroes, you sought a path for Śayu, for Atri, and for Manu in ancient times; with those by which you struck down the Śārīs for Syūmaraśmi—with those very succors come hither, O Aśvins!
With those [powers] by which Paṭharvā, through the greatness of his belly, shone like a piled-up fire kindled on its course;
with those by which you protected Śaryāta in the great contest for wealth—with those very aids, O Aśvins, come hither to us.
With those [powers] by which, O Aṅgiras, you two went forth in spirit and reached the front in the opening of the flood of cattle;
with those [powers] by which you aided the heroic Manu with nourishment—come hither, O Aśvins, with those excellent aids!
With those [powers] by which you brought home wives for Vimada, or with which you bestowed the ruddy cows;
with those by which you carried Sudās to the state of having good gods—come hither, O Aśvins, with those very aids!
With those aids by which you become sources of peace for the donor, with which you protect Bhujyu and with which you protect Adhrigu—
with those most gracious and well-sustaining succors, O Aśvins, come hither, you who praise the Eternal Order.
With those aids wherewith you honored Kṛśānu at his discharge, and wherewith you helped the young man’s steed in the race;
with those aids wherewith you bring the dear honey to the bees—come hither, O Aśvins, with those very succors.
With those aids wherewith you quicken the man who fights for cattle in the contest for men, and at the winning of land and offspring;
with those wherewith you protect chariots and wherewith you protect the coursers—with those excellent aids, O Aśvins, come hither!
With those aids wherewith you, O Śatakratus, protected Kutsa, the son of Arjuni, and Turvīti and Dabhīti;
with those wherewith you protected Dhvasanti and Puruṣanti—with those very aids, O Aśvins, come hither to us.

O Aśvins, make our speech effective; O wonder-workers, bulls, fulfill our inspired thought. In this non-gambling [contest], I invoke you both for protection; be with us for our increase in the winning of the prize.
O Aśvins, protect us day and night with unimpaired blessings and good fortune!
May Mitra, Varuṇa, Aditi, Sindhu, Earth, and Heaven grant this to us.
This most excellent light among lights has come; the bright, far-reaching signal has been born.
Just as [the night] was sent forth for the impelling of Savitṛ, even so has Night yielded her womb to Uṣas.
Bright with her radiant calf, the shining one has come; the dark one has entered her dwellings.
Of common kinship, immortal, following one after the other, the two heavens move along, wearing away their color.

Common is the path of the two sisters, endless; taught by the gods, they travel it one after the other. They do not clash, nor do they stand still; well-established, Night and Dawn are of one mind though diverse in form.
Radiant leader of true blessings, she has been perceived; wonderful, she has opened the doors for us. Stretching forth the world, she has revealed our riches; Dawn has awakened all living beings.
O Bounteous One, for the crooked-eyed to move, for enjoyment, for sacrifice, and for wealth— for those who see but a little— you, O Uṣas, have awakened all beings with wide vision.
For dominion you, for glory you, for greatness you; for sacrifice you, as one goes for wealth—you.
Beholding diverse ways of life, Dawn has awakened all beings.
This daughter of heaven has appeared, shining forth, a young woman clad in radiant raiment.
O Uṣas, sovereign lady of all earthly wealth, shine brightly here today, O auspicious one!
She follows the path of those who have departed and is the first of the endless mornings yet to come.
Dawning, Uṣas rouses every living being, yet she awakens no one who is dead.
O Uṣas, that you have caused Agni to be kindled, that you have shone forth with the eye of Sūrya,
and that you have awakened the men who intend to sacrifice— that auspicious work you have performed among the gods.
How great is that which shall be when she has come together with those who have shone forth and those who will surely shine?
Longing for the former ones, she yearns; reflecting, she goes gladly with the others.
Gone are those mortals who beheld the Dawn as she shone forth in times long past;
now has she become visible to us, and they too are coming who shall behold her in future days.
Driving away enemies, guardian of the cosmic order (*ṛta*), born of the cosmic order, bringing forth blessings,
and inspiring true speech— O Dawn, most auspicious, bearing the feast for the gods, shine forth here today as the most excellent one.
Again and again has the goddess Dawn shone forth in the past; and so today, the bountiful one, she has shone here.
And she shall shine forth through future days as well; undecaying and immortal, she moves by her own inherent powers.
With her bright ornaments she has shone across the expanse of heaven; the goddess has cast off her black mantle. Awakening [the world], Dawn approaches with her ruddy horses on a well-yoked chariot.
Bringing forth nourishment and desirable treasures, she displays her wondrous banner as she shines forth.
The first of the eternal dawns that have passed away, Uṣas has shone brightly.
Arise! The living breath has come to us; darkness has departed and light approaches.
She has cleared a path for Sūryā to travel; we have arrived where they prolong our lifespan.
With the shuttle he draws forth the voice; the singer, being praised, extols the shining Dawns.
Shine forth today, O bounteous one, for the one who praises you; bestow upon us a life rich in progeny.
Those Dawns which shine forth for the mortal donor, rich in cattle and with all heroes—
may the presser of Soma obtain them at the conclusion of Vāyu’s bounteous gifts, for they bestow horses.
Mother of the gods, the face of Aditi, the banner of sacrifice, O Great One, shine forth!
Bringing praise to our sacred prayer, dawn upon us; O possessor of all boons, bring us to the people.
Whatever wonderful wealth the Dawns bring as a blessing to the one who has sacrificed and labored— the auspicious gift—
may Mitra, Varuṇa, Aditi, Sindhu, Earth, and Heaven grant that to us.
We offer these prayers to Rudra, the powerful one with matted hair, the lord of heroes,
so that there may be well-being for our bipeds and quadrupeds, and so that everything in this village may be nourished and free from disease.
Be gracious to us, O Rudra, and grant us joy; we shall worship you with homage, you who rule over heroes.
Whatever health and prosperity our father Manu won through sacrifice, may we attain that under your guidance, O Rudra.
May we obtain your favor through the sacrifice to the gods, O bounteous Rudra, you who dwell among heroes;
coming toward us with goodwill, may you approach our people, and with our heroes unharmed, may we offer the oblation to you.
We invoke for our protection the brilliant Rudra, the fulfiller of sacrifice, the swift one, the seer;
may he cast far from us the divine wrath, and we choose only his goodwill.

With reverence, we invoke the ruddy boar of heaven, the one with braided hair, the brilliant form. May he, holding in his hand the most excellent medicines, grant us protection, armor, and a secure dwelling.

This speech, sweeter than the sweet, is spoken for the father of the Maruts, for the strengthening of Rudra. And grant us, O Immortal One, the food of mortals; be gracious to ourselves, to our children, and to our descendants.
Do not harm our great ones, nor our small; do not harm our growing, nor our grown.
Do not slay our father, nor our mother; O Rudra, do not injure our dear bodies.
Do not harm us in our children or grandchildren, nor in our own lives; do not harm us in our cattle or our horses.
O Rudra, do not slay our heroes in your wrath. Bearing oblations, we invoke you always.

Like a herdsman, I have brought these hymns of praise near to you; O Father of the Maruts, grant us your favor. For your benevolence is auspicious and most compassionate; therefore, we choose your protection alone.
Far from us be your cow-slaying and man-slaying [missile], O Lord of Heroes; let your favor be with us.
Be gracious to us, speak for us, O God, and grant us protection, you of double strength.
Seeking help, we have uttered our homage to him; may Rudra, accompanied by the Maruts, hear our call.
May Mitra, Varuṇa, Aditi, Sindhu, Earth, and Heaven grant us this.
The brilliant face of the gods has risen—the eye of Mitra, Varuṇa, and Agni.
Sūrya, the soul of all that moves and stands, has filled the heaven, the earth, and the mid-air.
Sūrya follows after the radiant goddess Uṣas, as a young man approaches a maiden;
there, where men seeking the gods extend their generations toward auspiciousness for the sake of the auspicious.
The auspicious, bay, and dappled horses of the Sun—wondrous, swift, and worthy of praise—standing in homage, have ascended to the back of heaven; they traverse heaven and earth in an instant.

That is the divinity of Sūrya, that is his greatness: in the midst of his work, he withdraws what was spread out. When he has unyoked his bay horses from their station, then Night spreads her garment over all.
In the lap of heaven, Sūrya assumes that form of Mitra and Varuṇa for all to behold;
one part of his radiant power is infinite and white, while the other is black, which the coursers bring together.
O gods, at the rising of the sun this day, deliver us from distress and from reproach!
May Mitra, Varuṇa, Aditi, Sindhu, Earth, and Heaven grant us this!
To the two Nāsatyas I offer up my hymns like sacred grass; I send them forth as the wind drives the clouds.
They who, with their chariot swift as an army, brought back a wife for the young Vimada.
Whether by means of strong-winged, swift-gliding [birds], or by the impulses of the gods, being confident,
the donkey won those thousand [cows] from Yama in the contest, O Nāsatyas, in the prize-winning race.
Tugra, indeed, had abandoned Bhujyu in the cloudless sky, as one who has died leaves behind his wealth;
you carried him away with self-propelled ships that glide through the mid-air and are free from water.
O Nāsatyas, with winged steeds that traverse three nights and three days,
you carried Bhujyu across the ocean, on the shore of the moist desert, by means of three chariots having a hundred feet and six horses.

O Aśvins, you displayed your heroism in that ocean which offers no support, no foothold, and no place to grasp, when you carried Bhujyu back to his home, who had boarded a ship equipped with a hundred oars.

The white horse which you, O Aśvins, gave to Aghāśva as perpetual well-being—that gift of yours was great and worthy of praise; the prize-winning steed of Pedu has always been an object of invocation for the noble man.
O Heroes, for the praising Kakṣīvat, the son of Pajra, you two dug out abundant wealth;
from the hoof of your stallion, O bulls, you poured out a hundred jars of *surā* from the *kārotara* vessel.

With snow you warded off the scorching heat from Agni; you bestowed upon him nourishing food and strength. O Aśvins, you brought forth Atri, who had been cast into the cauldron, together with all his followers, in safety.
O Nāsatyas, you raised up from afar that well whose base was high and whose opening was tilted;
you made its waters flow for the sake of wealth, so that the thirsty Gotama might drink and obtain a thousandfold riches.
O Nāsatyas, you stripped away the aged skin from Cyavāna, like a garment, as he grew old;
O wonder-workers, you prolonged the life of the abandoned man and made him the husband of young maidens.
O Nāsatyas, that praiseworthy and successful protection of yours, which brings aid— since you two, being wise,
brought it forth like a hidden treasure from its concealment for Vandana to behold.
O Heroes, I make manifest that mighty deed of yours for the sake of gain, like thunder making rain manifest,
since Dadhyañc Ātharvaṇa, with the head of a horse, proclaimed to you the honeyed secret.
O Nāsatyas, you who possess many enjoyments, Purandhi invoked you both for the great journey;
hear that, O Aśvins, as Śasu did for Vadhrimatī—you gave her a son with golden hands.
O Nāsatyas, heroes, you released the quail from the mouth of the wolf in the encounter;
and you, O lords of many enjoyments, restored the lamenting seer to sight.
For in the contest for the prize, you cut off the leg like the wing of a bird;
instantly, you fitted an iron shank for Viśpalā so that she might run when the wealth was at stake.
To him who had cut up a hundred rams for the she-wolf, R̥jrāśva, his father made blind;
for him, O Nāsatyas, you two, the wonder-workers and physicians, bestowed eyes that see clearly, beyond all reach.
The daughter of Sūrya mounted your chariot, as a mare wins with her steed;
all the gods approved it in their hearts, for you, O Nāsatyas, are united with splendor.
When you two, O Aśvins, speeding along, came to Divodāsa for the sake of Bharadvāja’s dwelling, your benevolent chariot brought wealth; a bull and a porpoise were yoked to it.
O Nāsatyas, bringing wealth with good dominion, offspring, long life, and heroic strength,
you came together with vigor to Jahnavī, who offered her portion three times a day.
Jāhuṣa was besieged on all sides; you two bore him away by easy paths through the regions at night. O Nāsatyas, with your piercing chariot, you two who never grow old, traversed the mountains.
On one day you two came to the aid of Vaśa for the joy of battle, O Aśvins, so that he might win thousands;
together with Indra, you two bulls drove away misfortune and the hostilities of Pṛthuśravas.

From the very low you raised the waters on high for Śara, the son of Arcatka, so that he might drink; O Nāsatyas, by your wondrous powers, you made the barren cow swell with milk even for the exhausted Śayu.

To Viśvaka, the son of Kṛṣṇa, who sought your aid, who praised you, and who acted with integrity, O Nāsatyas, you restored Viṣṇāpū by your wondrous powers, so that he might see him again, like a lost animal.
For ten nights and nine days, Rebha had been bound and pierced within the waters;
you two drew him out from the water where he was cast away and submerged, like Soma with a ladle.
I have proclaimed your wondrous deeds, O Aśvins; may I be the master of this [wealth], possessing good cattle and brave sons.
And beholding and attaining long life, may I reach old age as if returning home.
O Aśvins, the ancient Hotar-priest invites you for the exhilaration of the sweet Soma;
the gift is spread upon the sacred grass, the song is extended—come hither, O Nāsatyas, with nourishment and with spoils.

O Aśvins, that chariot of yours, swifter than thought, drawn by noble horses, which visits the clans— by that very chariot with which you go to the dwelling of the righteous, come to our abode, O Heroes.
O Heroes, you released the seer Atri, who belongs to the five tribes, from distress and from the pit by means of your host;
destroying the magic powers of the malevolent Dasyu, O Bulls, you urged him forward in succession.

O Aśvins, O heroes, O bulls, you rescued the seer Rebha—who was hidden like a horse by the wicked ones—within the waters; you restored him who was shattered by your wondrous deeds. Your ancient exploits do not age.
Like one who has fallen asleep in the lap of Destruction, or like the sun dwelling in darkness, O wonder-workers,
you two Aśvins raised up Vandana for glory— him who was buried like a brilliant golden ornament.

O Nāsatyas, O Heroes, that deed of yours is worthy of praise by Kakṣīvat, the son of Pajra, as you traveled around: from the hoof of a swift horse, for the sake of the people, you poured out a hundred jars of honey.
O Heroes, you gave Viṣṇāpū to Viśvaka, the son of Kṛṣṇa, who praised you;
O Aśvins, you gave a husband even to Ghoṣā, who was growing old in her father’s house.
O Aśvins, you gave a radiant [wife] to Śyāva, the son of Kaṇva, from the great host;
that deed of yours, O bulls, is worthy of proclamation, that you bestowed glory upon the descendant of Nṛṣad.
Assuming many forms, O Aśvins, you brought down the swift horse for Pedu—
a prize-winner who wins a thousand, irresistible, slayer of the serpent, glorious, and a conqueror.
These glorious deeds of yours, O bounteous givers, are a prayer, a hymn of praise, and a dwelling-place between the two worlds;
when the Pajras invoke you, O Aśvins, come with nourishment and grant strength to the wise man.
O Aśvins, being praised by the son’s hymn, you who are swift and bestow strength upon the sage,
having grown great through the prayer at Agastya’s rite, O Nāsatyas, you restored Viśpalā.
Where were you going when you found the excellent praise of Kāvya, O sons of Heaven, O bulls, while he was lying in his bed?
Like a buried jar of gold, O Aśvins, you dug it up on the tenth day.
O Aśvins, by your powers you made Cyavāna, who was aging, young again; O Nāsatyas, the daughter of Sūrya chose your chariot together with splendor.
O youthful ones, you who possess renewed thought, you became manifest to Tugra through your ancient ways;
you carried Bhujyu out from the ocean, from the midst of the waters, with winged, ruddy horses.
The son of Tugra called upon you, O Aśvins, having been cast into the sea yet remaining unshaken;
you brought him out in safety on your well-yoked chariot, swift as thought, O powerful ones.
The quail invoked you, O Aśvins, when you released her from the jaws of the wolf;
with your victorious chariot you sped over the ridges of the mountain, and you slew Jātaviṣvāc with poison.

To him who had offered a hundred rams to the she-wolf and was led away into darkness by his malevolent father, you two, O Aśvins, restored his two white-eyed eyes; you bestowed light upon the blind man so that he might see.
"Success! For the blind man, O Aśvins, bulls among heroes, she the she-wolf called out, 'O men!
Like a youthful lover who carves up his food, R̥jrāśva offered one hundred and one rams."
Great is your aid, O Aśvins, bringing bliss; you heal even the cripple, O bountiful ones.
Then Purandhi called upon you both; come hither, O bulls, with your protections.
O Aśvins, wonder-workers, you made the barren cow swell with milk for Śayu, though she was dry and bound;
by your powers, you brought home the wife of Purumitra, the daughter of Vimada.
O Aśvins, wonder-workers, you sow barley with the wolf, milking nourishment for mankind;
blowing away the Dasyu with the *bakura* wind, you have created vast light for the Ārya.

O Aśvins, you restored the horse's head to Dadhyanc, the son of Atharvan; he, observing the cosmic order (*ṛta*), proclaimed to you both the honeyed secret of Tvaṣṭṛ which was hidden within your armpits, O wonder-workers (*dasrau*).
O Sages, I always desire your favor; O Aśvins, further all my prayers.
O Nāsatyas, bestow upon us great wealth, accompanied by offspring and worthy of renown.
O Aśvins, O heroes, bestowing gifts, you gave a son with golden hands to Vadhrimatī. O bounteous givers, O Aśvins, you raised up Śyāva, who had been cut into three pieces, so that he might live.
O Aśvins, these heroic deeds of yours, performed in the past, the Āyus have proclaimed.
Performing sacred prayer for you two, O Bulls, may we, possessing brave sons, speak at the assembly.
O Aśvins, may your chariot, flying like a falcon, most gracious and self-reliant, come hither—
your chariot which is swifter than the mind of a mortal, three-seated, O Bulls, and possessing the speed of the wind.
Come hither on your well-rolling, three-wheeled chariot, with its triple seat and triple framework;
O Aśvins, cause our cows to swell, quicken our horses, and increase the hero among us.
O wonder-workers, on your well-rolling chariot that is worthy of praise, hear this cry from the pressing-stone.
Why indeed do the ancient sages say that you, O Aśvins, are the most frequent visitors in return?
O Aśvins, let the falcons carry you both on the chariot—yoked, swift, and winged;
those who cross the waters like divine eagles, O Nāsatyas, bring you toward the offerings.
May the youthful daughter of Sūrya ascend your chariot here, O heroes, having found it pleasing. May your beautiful, winged, and ruddy horses carry you both forward at the encounter.
By your wondrous deeds, O wonder-workers, you raised up Vandana; by your powers, O mighty ones, you raised up Rebha.
You brought Tugrya out from the ocean, and you made Cyavāna young again.
O Aśvins, you bestowed strength and protection upon Atri when he was cast into the heated pit;
you restored sight to Kaṇva when he was deprived of it, graciously accepting his excellent hymn of praise.
O Aśvins, you caused the cow to swell for the ancient Śayu who had entreated you;
you released the quail from distress, and you restored the leg to Viśpalā.
O Aśvins, you two gave to Pedu a white horse, impelled by Indra, a slayer of serpents—
a steed to be invoked with loud cries, a conqueror of the enemy, fierce, winning thousands, virile, and firm-limbed.
O heroes, well-born Aśvins, we, imploring you for help, call upon you both.
Come to us with your chariot laden with wealth, graciously accepting our songs for our prosperity.
Come to us with the fresh swiftness of a hawk, O Nāsatyas, acting in harmony;
for I, having offered oblations, call upon you both at the dawning of every most recent Uṣas.

I call hither for life your wondrous chariot, swift as thought, drawn by vigorous horses, worthy of sacrifice— possessing a thousand banners, rich in wood, a hundredfold wealth, obedient, and bestowing wide space toward our offerings.
The prayer has been raised up toward him at his departure; the quarters of the sky have come together for his praise.
I prepare the warm oblation; the aids approach it. O Aśvins, Ūrjānī has mounted your chariot.
When they have come together, vying with one another, the vigorous, immeasurable, and swift ones for the sake of glory in the contest;
then your chariot is made manifest on the slope, O Aśvins, when you carry the patron to his desired goal.

You two went with your self-yoked birds to Bhujyu as he was struggling, carrying him away to his ancestors. O Bulls, you traveled to the dwelling that was to be sought; for Divodāsa, your great protection became manifest.

O Aśvins, the two voices have directed toward you for the sake of beauty your own powerful, self-yoked chariot. Having come to you for friendship, the noble maiden chose you both as her husbands, even though you possess the power of flight.
You rescued Rebha from his confinement; with cold you quenched the fever that had scorched Atri.
You made the cow swell with nourishment for Śayu, and Vandana was delivered by you through a long span of life.
O Wonder-Workers (Dasras), you restored Vandana, who was bound by old age, as craftsmen repair a chariot;
through your inspired praise, you brought forth the sage from the field, and your wondrous deed has been manifest for the one who honors you here.

You two came to him who was lamenting in a far-off place, oppressed by the abandonment of his own father. From here, your aids were full of light; indeed, your wondrous assistances were present for help in the encounter.
And for you two, this honeyed [soma] the bee has hummed; in the intoxication of Soma, the son of Uśij calls out.
You two won over the mind of Dadhyañc, and then the horse's head spoke to you.
O Aśvins, you bestowed upon Pedu the white horse, the granter of many boons, the overcomer of enemies;
a steed shining with arrows, invincible in battles, worthy of praise, and subduing the people like Indra.
Which invocation of yours, O Aśvins, will be successful? Or what is pleasing to you both?
How shall the one lacking wisdom perform the ritual service?
Only the two who know should ask about the doors; another, who is thus ignorant and lacks understanding, would never [know] regarding a mortal who is not a fool.
Knowing this, we invoke you two; as those who know, may you two declare our prayer today. The one devoted to you has begun to sing, full of longing.
I ask the gods with simple sincerity, O wonder-workers, concerning the wondrous oblation consecrated by the *vaṣaṭ* cry.
May you two protect us from the more powerful one and from the more violent one.
The speech which shines forth like [the flame] in the dwelling of the Bhr̥gus, with which the son of Pajra worships you both— he,
like a wise one who sends forth the sacrificial calls.
I have heard the *gāyatra* hymn of Takavāna; for I have indeed sung praises to you both, O Aśvins. O Lords of Splendor, look upon me with your eyes!
For you two were present at great contests, or when you two brought [the prize] forth;
as such, O Vasus, be our good protectors; protect us from the wolf, from the one who intends evil.
Do not deliver us over to any enemy; let not the milch-cows depart from our houses anywhere, even those that provide nourishment for the suckling calves without their mothers being present.
May they yield milk for our alliance with you; measure out for us wealth consisting of booty, and measure out for us nourishment consisting of milch-cows.
The chariot of the Aśvins, which possesses no horse yet is full of vigor— by means of that, I have greatly rejoiced.
This chariot, easy to ride, shall surely carry me along with the people to the drinking of Soma.
Now, both the dreamer and the wealthy man who does not enjoy it— both of them vanish at dawn.

When will he, hastening, hear the songs of the Aṅgirases—those men who are devoted to the gods as their vessel? When he has reached the people of the house, the worshipful one strides widely at the sacrifice.
He propped up the sky and sprinkled the foundation; as a skillful *Ṛbhu*, he bestowed wealth upon the hero for the sake of booty.
The buffalo beheld his own kin, the cow; he looked around at the mare, the mother of the horse and of the cow.
May the ruddy dawns reach the ancient call of the sovereign, the swift lord of the Angirases day after day.
He fashioned the thunderbolt and harnessed the teams; he propped up the sky for the four-footed and the two-footed beings of men.
In his exhilaration, he gave the resonant, hidden face of the cows to the one who upholds the cosmic order (*ṛta*).
When the three-peaked [mountain] turned back at the onset, he threw open the doors for you from the treachery of man.
For you, O possessor of excellent seed, the two parents, swift and active, brought milk as a gift for your impelling;
they offered to you that pure wealth, the milk of the cow Sabardughā, the radiant one.

Then he has been born, the swift one; may he exhilarate us. He shines forth like the sun at this dawn—the drop (indus) by which, with those who offer sweat as their oblation, he has reached his dwelling, pouring with the ladle into the aging [vessels].
When the fuel-strewn wood-pile has been prepared at the sacrifice, may the Sun [drive] away the enclosures of the cow;
for when you shine through the days toward the decisive deed, you are for the swift one who seeks cattle and lacks a chariot.
From the great heaven, the eight [rays] have brought hither the two bay steeds; may he, the glorious victor, fight for the spring.
When they have milked for your increase the exhilarating, golden, mountain-born [Soma], which is impetuous as a bull and invigorated by the wind.
O skillful one, you turned back the iron rock brought down from heaven for the cow;
where, O much-invoked one, favoring Kutsa, you encompassed Śuṣṇa with endless weapons of death.
When the sun was still hidden from the darkness, O wielder of the stone, you launched that bolt against Phaliga;
you consumed even that power of Śuṣṇa which was fortified and firmly bound from heaven.
The two great, wheelless expanses, heaven and earth, rejoiced in your deed, O Indra.
You with your mighty thunderbolt struck down Vṛtra, the boar, as he lay upon the rivers.
O Indra, you who protect men, mount the manly, well-yoked, and most swift horses of the wind;
[mount] that exhilarating, Vṛtra-slaying, and decisive thunderbolt which Kāvya Uśanas fashioned for you.
You, O Indra, made the sun’s bay horses rest for the men; Etaśa brought the wheel here as he did not.
You rolled it across the ninety navigable rivers to the further shore, casting down those who do not sacrifice.
O Indra, wielder of the thunderbolt, protect us from this malevolent assault and from misfortune in the encounter.
Bestow upon us riches consisting of chariots and horses for our sustenance, for glory, and for the gift of true abundance.
May that benevolence of yours never fail us; O most mighty one, may we win together abundant nourishments.
O Maghavan, grant us a share of the cattle of the enemy; may we be your most liberal companions in the feast.
O you of swift wrath, bring forward the Soma-juice for your protection; present the oblation to the bounteous Rudra.
With the heroes of the Asura of heaven, I have praised the Maruts, as if seeking a boon from both worlds.
Like two wives eager for the first invocation, Dawn and Night, appearing in many forms, have increased [the sacrifice].
Like a barren woman wearing a loosened garment, she is beautiful to behold with the splendor of the Sun and her golden ornaments.
May Parijman, the slayer of the dawn-demons, exhilarate us; may Vāta, the bull of the waters, exhilarate us.
O Indra and Parvata, sharpen our wits for us! May all the gods grant us this wide space.
And those two glorious ones, who come to the white light and drink the draughts, shall I, the descendant of Uśij, invoke.
Bring forward for yourselves the Son of the Waters; bring forward the two Parents of the impetuous Āyu.
The son of Uśij shall call upon your roaring one, as Ghoṣā did in the winning of Arjuna’s praise.
I shall speak forth to you for Pūṣan’s gift, toward the wealth-bestowing power of Agni.
O Mitra and Varuṇa, hear my invocation; hear it from every side at this place of assembly. May the giver of hearing hear us—the one who hears well, the Sindhu with her waters, whose fields are fair.
I praise that gift of yours, O Varuṇa and Mitra: hundreds of cattle bestowed upon the Pajras at the *pṛkṣayāma* feasts.
Having received them on their famous chariot and their beloved chariot, they have come, instantly securing for themselves abundant prosperity.

I praise the bounty of this one whose wealth is great; may we, together with brave sons, win from Nahus the gift of that man who possesses abundant food for the Pajras—a patron who provides me with horses and chariots.
The man who, being treacherous and acting crookedly like one who harms the waters, pours libations for you, O Mitra and Varuṇa—
he himself lays consumption within his own heart, even though he is a follower of the *ṛta* through his sacrificial offerings.
He, the mighty one, impelled by wondrous deeds, the subduer of the hosts of men, whose glory is praised;
he who bestows gifts freely, moving with rapid stride, is ever the hero in all battles.
Then, coming at the call of the patron Nahuṣa, O kings of immortality, you who are delightful, hear [him];
for you, who move through the clouds, bestow bounty upon the one with the chariot for the sake of great praise.
"This is the host of that patron," they have said, "at the distribution of the tenfold gift.
May those in whom splendors and riches delight, all of them, win the prize in the contests.
We rejoice in the tenfold nourishment when the two [teams] come bearing the five foods;
why do these masters, with well-wished horses and well-wished reins, striving for victory, urge on the men?
The sea with golden ears and jeweled neck—may all the gods grant us space for that.
May the songs of the pious man who has come instantly to them, and the dawns, take pleasure in both of us.
Four horses of Maśarśāra’s young steed, and three of King Ayavasa,
the victorious— your chariot, O Mitra and Varuṇa, with its long-reaching waters and reins as its rays, has shone like the sun.
Broad is the chariot of Dakṣiṇā; the immortal gods have yoked it and have mounted it.
From the darkness has she arisen, the noble and far-reaching one, providing guidance for the human dwelling.
Awakened before all the world, the lofty one who wins the prize and gathers wealth;
the youthful maiden, born again, has looked out on high; Dawn has come first at the morning invocation.
O well-born goddess Uṣas, when you today distribute a portion among men for mortals,
may the divine Savitṛ, the friend of the household, declare us sinless here before Sūrya.
Day after day the Dawn goes toward every house, bestowing her names; desiring to win, the radiant one has come again and again, and she enjoys the very best of treasures.

Sister of Bhaga, kinswoman of Varuṇa, O Uṣas, true and generous one, be the first to be awakened by our praise! May he who is the establisher of evil be left behind; may we conquer him with the chariot of the sacrificial fee.
Let the pleasant voices rise up, let the inspired thoughts arise; the Agnis have risen up, shining brightly.
Making manifest the desirable treasures hidden by darkness, the Dawns shine forth.
One departs and the other approaches; the two days of different forms move together.
One has made the darkness around the dwelling a secret cave; Dawn has shone forth on her brilliantly glowing chariot.
Equal today and likewise equal tomorrow, they follow the long-lasting ordinance of Varuṇa.
Blameless, each one traverses thirty leagues in an instant, encompassing his will.
Knowing the name of the first day, the bright one has been born from the black as the white one;
the maiden of *Ṛta* does not violate her laws, coming daily to the appointed place.
Like a maiden displaying her body, O Goddess, you go toward the god who desires to sacrifice;
smiling, a youthful woman, as you shine forth, you reveal your breasts.
Radiant as a maiden groomed by her mother, you reveal your body so that it may be seen.
O auspicious Dawn, shine forth even further; no other Dawns have attained what you possess.
Rich in horses, rich in cattle, possessing all desirable things, striving with the rays of the sun,
the Dawns go forth and come back again, bearing auspicious names.
Following the rein of Cosmic Order (*ṛta*), bestow upon us every auspicious intention.
O Dawn, easy to invoke, shine forth for us today; may riches be ours and with our patrons.
As the Dawn shines forth while the fire is kindled, and as the Sun rises, he has spread his light far and wide.
May the god Savitṛ now impel our purpose here, so that bipeds and quadrupeds may go forth.
Not violating the divine ordinances, yet diminishing the human generations,
Dawn has shone forth as the foremost of the endless dawns that have passed and of those yet to come.
This daughter of heaven has appeared, clothing herself in light from the front in her accustomed place;
she follows the path of Truth perfectly, and like one who knows, she does not confound the quarters of space.
The breast of the pure one has been seen, as it were; like Nodhas, she has revealed her dear things.
Like one sitting at the feast, awakening those who sleep, she has come again, the most constant of those who return.
In the eastern half of the unattainable realm, the mother of the cows has raised her banner;
she spreads out further and wider, filling both the laps of her parents.
Truly, she is most manifest for all to see; she avoids neither the stranger nor the kinsman.
Displaying herself with a stainless body, she does not shrink from the small nor does she flee from the great as she shines forth.
Like a brotherless maiden she goes forth toward men; like one mounting a chariot-seat for the winning of riches;
like a longing wife well-attired for her husband, Dawn, like a smiling woman, bares her bosom.
The sister has yielded her place to her elder sister; she departs from her as if to look back upon her.
Shining forth with the rays of the sun, she anoints herself with ointment like women going to a festival.
Of these former sisters, in the days gone by, each later one follows after the earlier one from behind.
May those Dawns, newer than the ancient ones, now shine forth upon us with wealth and auspicious days.
Awaken, O bountiful Uṣas, those who bestow gifts; let the stingy niggards sleep on, remaining unawakened.
Shine forth with wealth for the liberal patrons, O bountiful one; shine forth with wealth for the singer, O truthful Dawn, as you bring them to old age.
The young woman has been seen from the east; she yokes her team of ruddy kine.
Now indeed shall she shine forth; her light appears, and Agni stands near every house.
Even the birds have flown up from their dwelling at your dawning, as have the men who partake of food.
O Goddess Uṣas, you bring much desirable wealth to the mortal who gives offerings and dwells at home.
O Dawn goddesses, worthy of praise, you have been lauded by my prayer; you have increased our prosperity, O longing Dawns.
O goddesses, through your protection may we win booty consisting of hundreds and thousands.
The early-coming one bestows treasure at dawn; the wise man, having received it, lays it aside.
Increasing his offspring and lifespan thereby, he, possessed of brave sons, abides in the abundance of wealth.
May he be rich in cattle, rich in gold, and rich in horses; to him Indra bestows great vitality— to him who, O *prātaritvan*, as you approach with wealth, seizes him like a bird caught in a snare.

Desiring good fortune this morning, he has come today with a wealth-filled chariot, seeking the son of the sacrifice. Make him drink the pressed juice of the exhilarating *aṃśu* plant; increase the hero who dwells among men with true and pleasant words.
The rivers flow toward him, bringing refreshment; like milch-cows, they serve both the one who has sacrificed and the one who intends to sacrifice.
Seeking glory, the streams of clarified butter approach from every side the one who bestows gifts and the one who fulfills them.

He who gives stands supported upon the ridge of heaven; he indeed goes among the gods. For him the waters and the rivers flow with clarified butter; for him this sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā) ever overflows.

These wonders belong indeed to those who give sacrificial gifts; for those who give sacrificial gifts, the suns are in heaven. Those who give sacrificial gifts partake of immortality; those who give sacrificial gifts prolong their life.
May those who give not fall into misfortune and sin; may the wise patrons of good vows never suffer decay.
Let there be some other boundary for them; let sorrows fall upon the one who gives nothing.
With inspired thought, I offer forth unceasing hymns of praise for Bhāvya, who dwells upon the river—
he, the unconquered king, seeking glory, who measured out for me a thousand libations.
A hundred gold coins from the king who entreated me, and a hundred horses presented to me, I accepted at once;
Kakṣīvat received a hundred cows from the lord, and he has extended his undecaying fame to heaven.
Ten chariots drawn by dark horses, accompanied by maidens and given by Svanaya, have come to me;
six thousand head of cattle followed after them. Kakṣīvat won this at the close of the days.
Forty chestnut horses of Daśaratha lead the procession at the head of a thousand; the Pajras, the Kakṣīvat-s, have groomed these steeds that drip with ichor and are adorned with pearls.
I have accepted the former gift: three yoked oxen and eight cows that yield their milk without fail.
Those Pajras, the Subandhus, like common folk in a crowd, yet possessing wagons, have sought renown.
She who clings and clings all around, who wriggles like a worm;
she, the wide-striding one, bestows upon me hundreds of things to be enjoyed from the swift steeds.
Come close and stroke me; do not think my hairs are few.
I am entirely covered in hair, like a sheep from among the Gandhāris.

I honor Agni as the Hotṛ-priest, the bountiful, the Vasu, the Son of Strength, Jātavedas— the wise one, like a sage, Jātavedas— who, a god with his own sacrifice, with a form directed toward the gods that rises upward,
desires the radiant glow of clarified butter, of the offered fatness, accompanied by his flame.
We, the sacrificers, invoke you, the most excellent sacrificer, the eldest of the Aṅgirases, O inspired one, with our prayers— O bright one, with the prayers of the inspired.
You who encompass heaven like the sun, the invoker of the peoples,
the flame-haired bull whom these clans must favor for their impulsion— the clans [favor him].
For he, shining with his many-fold, radiant power, becomes the subduer of the malicious; like an axe, he is the subduer of the malicious. At whose onset even that which is firm yields like wood;
prevailing, he restrains and leads; as one who overcomes the desert, he leads.

Even firm things yield before him, as is well known; with the sharpest kindling-sticks, one should offer to Agni for his aid, one should offer for his aid. He who plunges into many [woods] hews them like forests with his flame;
even solid foods he destroys with his might, even solid things he destroys with his might.
